children.translated_text: <s>Nāṭakacandrikā</s> (The Moonlight on Drama)
Obeisance to the illustrious <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya Candra</s>!
Having examined the treatise of <s>Bharata Muni</s> and the delightful <s>Rasapūrvasudhākara</s>,
this definition of <s>nāṭaka</s> (drama) is written here in very condensed form. || 1 ||
Because of not being entirely coherent and because of contradicting the views of <s>Bharata Muni</s>,
the method of the <s>Sāhitya-darpaṇa</s> has mostly not been adopted. || 2 ||
Endowed with the divine, the divine-and-non-divine, or the non-divine [hero],

children.text: dhīreṇāḍhyam udāttena kṛṣṇaś ca lalitena ca || 3 ||
children.translated_text: enriched with a steadfast [hero] — <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> being of the exalted type and also of the charming type, || 3 ||
having <s>śṛṅgāra</s> (erotic love) or <s>vīra</s> (heroic) as the principal <s>rasa</s>, delightful, connected with the unceasing [plot],
connected with the introduction and conclusion, furnished with <s>sandhis</s> (junctures) and <s>sandhy-aṅgas</s> (sub-junctures), || 4 ||
with twenty-one sub-junctures, endowed with thirty-six ornaments,
furnished with <s>patākā-sthānakas</s> (banner-stations) and also with <s>upakṣepakas</s> (introductions), || 5 ||
endowed with proper use of language, containing the qualities of good poetry,
a <s>nāṭaka</s> (drama) should be free from faults and bestow delight to all. || 6 ||
Therein, the hero —
One whose divine sovereignty is self-manifest is called divine — <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> and others;
though divine, because of acting like a human, <s>Raghūdvaha</s> (Rāma) is called divine-and-non-divine. || 7 ||
Non-divine is <s>Dharmaputra</s> (Yudhiṣṭhira) and others; among these, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> is superior in qualities,

children.text: nāyakānāṃ guṇāḥ sarve yatra sarva-vidhāḥ smṛtāḥ || 8 ||
children.translated_text: in whom all the qualities of all types of heroes are recognized. || 8 ||
In him, charm and nobility are manifest, and the abundance of splendor is supreme;
therefore he is the fitting hero for a drama predominating in <s>śṛṅgāra rasa</s> (erotic sentiment). || 9 ||
That which the learned have declared as the subordinate status of the <s>paroḍhā</s> (married-to-another) and <s>upapati</s> (paramour),

children.text: tat tu kṛṣṇaṃ ca gopīś ca vineti pratipāditam || 10 ||
children.translated_text: that has been established as not applying to <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> and the <s>gopīs</s>. || 10 ||
Thus it is also stated in the <s>Rasa-vilāsa</s> (by <s>Sudeva</s>) —

children.text: neṣṭā yad aṅgini rase kavibhiḥ paroḍhā
children.translated_text: That which poets do not desire — the <s>paroḍhā</s> (married heroine) — in the principal <s>rasa</s>,
that [restriction] does not apply to the lotus-eyed women of <s>Gokula</s>;
for by expectation of the rules of <s>rasa</s>, as occasions for its descent,
by the enemy of <s>Kaṃsa</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>), the crest-jewel of the assembly of <s>rasikas</s> (connoisseurs). || 11 ||
Now the <s>rasas</s> (aesthetic sentiments) —
The <s>rasas</s> — <s>śṛṅgāra</s> (erotic), <s>vīra</s> (heroic), and others — should be known from the <s>Rasa-sudhārṇava</s>;

children.text: anye hāsyādayaḥ kāryā asminn aṅgatayā budhaiḥ || 12 ||
children.translated_text: the others — <s>hāsya</s> (comic) and so on — should be employed by the wise as subordinate elements in this [drama]. || 12 ||
Now the plot —

children.text: itivṛttaṃ bhavet khyātaṃ k ptaṃ miśram iti tridhā |
śāstra-prasiddhaṃ khyātaṃ syāt k ptaṃ kavi-vinirmitam |
children.translated_text: Well-known is that which is established in scripture; invented is that fashioned by the poet;

children.text: tayoḥ saṅkulatā miśraṃ k ptaṃ ramyaṃ tu nāṭake |
children.translated_text: the intermingling of both is mixed. The invented is delightful in drama.

children.text: nāṭakaṃ khyāta-vṛttaṃ syāt k pta-vṛttā tu nāṭikā |
children.translated_text: A <s>nāṭaka</s> should have a well-known plot; a <s>nāṭikā</s> has an invented plot;
an <s>īhāmṛga</s> has a mixed plot — thus it is stated in the <s>Nāṭyāṅga</s>.
The plot is threefold: well-known, invented, and mixed.
Now the <s>prastāvanā</s> (introduction) —
Now the <s>prastāvanā</s> is called the gateway to the subject to be presented.

children.text: prastāvanāyāṃ tu mukhe nāndī kāryā śubhāvahā ||
children.translated_text: In the <s>prastāvanā</s>, at the beginning, the auspicious <s>nāndī</s> (benediction) should be composed.
It should contain any one of: a blessing, an act of obeisance, or an indication of the subject matter;

children.text: aṣṭabhir daśabhir yuktā kiṃ vā dvādaśabhiḥ padaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: it should consist of eight, ten, or twelve metrical feet.
It should generally bear the name of the moon, and shine with words conveying auspiciousness.
Auspicious things include the <s>cakra</s> (discus), <s>kamala</s> (lotus), <s>cakora</s> (partridge), <s>kumuda</s> (water-lily), and so on.
Therein, one containing a blessing — as in <s>Lalita-mādhava</s> (1.1) —
Tormenting the breast-<s>kokas</s> (cakravāka birds) of the beautiful women of the enemies of the gods,
and also their lotus-faces, may the undivided
moon of the fame of <s>Mukunda</s>, the joy-giver to <s>cakora</s> birds, the friend of all,
forever bestow delight upon you!
One containing an act of obeisance — as in the same work (1.2) —

children.text: aṣṭau prokṣya dig-aṅganā ghana-rasaiḥ patrāṅkurāṇāṃ śriyā
children.translated_text: Sprinkling the eight directions' women with the dense essence, with the beauty of sprouting leaves,
ever making an ornament of the garland of beautiful creeping vines,

children.text: yaḥ pīne hṛdi bhānujām atulabhāṃ candrākṛtiṃ cojjvalāṃ
children.translated_text: he who in his broad chest holds the incomparable, moon-shaped, and radiant

children.text: rundhānaḥ kramate tam atra mudiraṃ kṛṣṇaṃ namaskurmahe ||
children.translated_text: daughter of the Sun (<s>Yamunā</s>) — to that dark cloud, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, we offer obeisance!

children.text: vastu-nirdeśānvitā cātraiva aṣṭau prokṣya digaṅganā ityādir eva |
children.translated_text: And one containing an indication of subject matter is also there — 'Sprinkling the eight directions' women' and so forth, the same verse.

children.text:
aṣṭapada-yuktā yathā vīra-carite prathamāṅke (prastāvanāyāḥ prathamaḥ
ślokaḥ)-
children.translated_text: An example with eight metrical feet — as in <s>Vīra-carita</s>, first act (the first verse of the introduction) —
To the eternally self-luminous <s>Deva</s>, whose sins are destroyed,
who transcends the division of sequence — obeisance to the light of <s>Caitanya</s>!

children.text: kaścid aṣṭa-padāṃ pādair aṣṭabhiḥ padyayor jagau || 17 ||
children.translated_text: Someone composed an eight-footed verse with eight feet in two <s>pādas</s>. || 17 ||
An example with ten metrical feet — as in <s>Abhirāma-rāghava</s> —
In all actions auspicious, having risen from the serpent-bed,
his side-glances are waves of the flowing stream of compassion's essence;
those of <s>Hari</s>, friends of the beauty of the lotus-petal of <s>Lakṣmī's</s> play,
smiling with the essence of nectar, attainable only through extraordinary good conduct.
An example with twelve metrical feet — as in 'Tormenting the breast-kokas of the beautiful women of the enemies of the gods' and so on (LalM 1.1).
In that same verse, the inclusion of the moon's name and auspicious meaning is present.

children.text: bhāraty atrocitā vṛttir eṣā tu caturaṅgikā |
children.translated_text: The <s>Bhāratī vṛtti</s> (verbal style) is appropriate here; this [introduction] is fourfold:
<s>prarocanā</s> (enticement) in the opening, and <s>vīthī</s> (one-act) and <s>prahasana</s> (farce) likewise. || 18 ||
Therein, the <s>prarocanā</s> (enticement) —
Making the audience eager through praise of the country, time, story, patron, and audience members —
this is called <s>prarocanā</s> (enticement). || 19 ||
As in <s>Lalita-mādhava</s> (1.7) —

children.text: sūtradhāraḥ | kim ity evam ucyate | paśya paśya --
children.translated_text: The <s>sūtradhāra</s> (stage director) says: Why is it said thus? Look, look —
The autumn festival shines forth, the assembly of <s>Vaiṣṇavas</s> sparkles,
the mountain after a long time pours forth the pure stream of <s>Hari's</s> fame;

children.text: kim anyad iha mādhavo madhura-mūrtir udbhāsate
children.translated_text: what more — here <s>Mādhava</s> of sweet form radiates,
therefore this is the rise of your pure meritorious fortune!
Now the <s>āmukha</s> (prelude) —

children.text: sūtradhāro naṭīṃ brūte svakāryaṃ prati yuktitaḥ |
children.translated_text: When the <s>sūtradhāra</s> (stage director) addresses the actress regarding his own purpose,

children.text: prastutākṣepi citroktyā yat tad āmukham īritam || 20 ||
children.translated_text: through a striking expression that alludes to the main subject — that is called <s>āmukha</s> (prelude). || 20 ||

children.text: yad āmukham iti proktaṃ saiva pratsāvanocyate |
children.translated_text: What is called <s>āmukha</s> — that itself is called <s>prastāvanā</s> (introduction).
Five sub-divisions of the <s>āmukha</s> are described: <s>kathodghāta</s> (narrative opening) and <s>pravartaka</s> (instigator), || 21 ||
<s>prayogātiśaya</s> (dramatic excess), and also a pair of <s>vīthī</s> sub-elements:
<s>udghātyaka</s> (elaboration), <s>avalagita</s> (interweaving), and <s>saṅgaka</s> — so stated by the sage. || 22 ||
Therein, the <s>kathodghāta</s> (narrative opening) —
When a word of the <s>sūtradhāra</s> or its meaning coincides with the plot,

children.text: svīkṛtya praviśet pātraṃ kathodghātaḥ sa kīrtitaḥ || 23 ||
children.translated_text: and a character enters taking it up — that is called <s>kathodghāta</s>. || 23 ||
As in <s>Harivilāsa</s> —
Of those whose greatness is incomparable, whose nature is incomprehensible to the world,
whose deeds are supramundane — who is able to know their heart?

children.text:
(nepathye) hanta bhoḥ satyam āttha lokottara-caritānāṃ hṛdayaṃ ko jñātum
īśatīti ||
children.translated_text: (From behind the curtain) Ah! You speak truly — 'Who is able to know the heart of those whose deeds are supramundane?'
Now the <s>pravartaka</s> (instigator) —
When what is hinted at is advanced by temporal coincidence, that is the <s>pravartaka</s>. || 24 ||
As in <s>Keśava-carita</s> —
Delighting the clusters of flowers all around,
instantly enhancing the glory of <s>Uddhava</s>,

children.text: dhīraṃ numer api mano madayan samantād
children.translated_text: intoxicating even the steadfast mind of <s>Manu</s> on all sides —
O beautiful one, this <s>Mādhava</s> (spring/Kṛṣṇa) arrives, bestowing bliss!
Thus they exit. Then <s>Mādhava</s> enters.
Or as in <s>Vidagdha-mādhava</s> (1.10) —
This very spring season has arrived, in which
that perfect Lord, bearing fresh passion,
with planets concealed, along with the beautiful <s>Rādhā</s>,
on a full-moon night, <s>Paurṇamāsī</s> will bring them together for love-play.
Now the <s>prayogātiśaya</s> (dramatic excess) —
When through a hint such as 'Here he is!' and through the stage director's performance,
the entrance [of a character] is indicated — that is called <s>prayogātiśaya</s>. || 25 ||
As in <s>Lalita-mādhava</s> (4.16), in the interlude act —
Though <s>Rādhikā</s> is constantly being restrained by the elder woman,

children.text: nirābādhaṃ sadā sādhu ramayaty eṣa mādhavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: this <s>Mādhava</s> always delights her without hindrance, in a good manner.
Now the <s>udghātyaka</s> (elaboration) —
When words whose meaning is not yet realized are connected by people

children.text: yojayanti padair anyais tad udghātyakam ucyate || 26 ||
children.translated_text: with other words for the purpose of arriving at their meaning — that is called <s>udghātyaka</s>. || 26 ||
As in <s>Lalita-mādhava</s> (1.11) —
While acting on stage, having defeated the <s>Kirāta</s> king, by the treasure-house of arts,
at the right time, the grasping of the hand of the virtuous <s>Tārā</s> should be enacted.
(From behind the curtain) Alas! The wedding of <s>Rādhā</s> and <s>Mādhava</s>, out of fear of King <s>Kaṃsa</s>,

children.text: abhivyaktam udāhartum asamartho naṭatā kirāta-rājam ity upadeśena bodhayan
children.translated_text: unable to express it openly, he conveys it through the allegory 'Having defeated the Kirāta king' —

children.text: dhanyaḥ ko'yaṃ cintā-viklavāṃ mām āśvāsayatīti tatra paurṇamāsī-praveśaḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'Who is this blessed one who consoles me, distressed with anxiety?' — thereupon the entrance of <s>Paurṇamāsī</s>.
Now the <s>avalagita</s> (interweaving) —
Where, while engaged in one matter, another matter is accomplished
due to a prior commitment — that should be known by the wise as <s>avalagita</s>. || 27 ||
As in <s>Kaṃsa-vadha</s> —
'O <s>Naṭarāja Puruṣottama</s>, why do you delay?'

children.text: (nepathye) bhoḥ kas tvam asi yad atra māṃ tvarayasi |
children.translated_text: (From behind the curtain) 'Sir! Who are you that you urge me here?'

children.text:
sūtradhāraḥ -- katham ayaṃ gopāla-veśo bhagavān upasthita eva paśya paśya
ityādi ||
children.translated_text: The <s>sūtradhāra</s> says: 'How! This is the Lord himself arrived in the guise of a cowherd! Look, look!' and so on.

children.text: śṛṅgāra-pracure nāṭye yuktam āmukham eva hi |
children.translated_text: In a drama rich in <s>śṛṅgāra rasa</s>, only the <s>āmukha</s> (prelude) is appropriate;

children.text: vīthī prahasanaṃ ceti dvividhe nātra lakṣite || 28 ||
children.translated_text: <s>vīthī</s> (one-act) and <s>prahasana</s> (farce) — these two types are not applicable here. || 28 ||
Therefore the <s>āmukha</s> is employed there in <s>Lalita-mādhava</s>.
The <s>prastāvanā</s> (introduction) and <s>sthāpanā</s> (establishment) are the two sub-types of <s>āmukha</s>;

children.text: ity ākhyāya sphuṭaṃ kecit tayoḥ kurvanti lakṣaṇam || 29 ||
children.translated_text: having declared this, some provide definitions for both. || 29 ||
As follows —
That which involves dialogue between the actress, the <s>vidūṣaka</s> (jester), the actor, and the <s>sūtradhāra</s> (stage director),
accompanied by brief <s>vīthī</s> elements — that is the <s>prastāvanā</s> form of <s>āmukha</s>.
That which is accompanied by all <s>vīthī</s> elements — that itself is called <s>sthāpanā</s> (establishment).
In works predominantly featuring <s>vīra</s> (heroic) and <s>adbhuta</s> (wondrous) rasas, the <s>prastāvanā</s> is suitable.
In works predominantly featuring <s>hāsya</s> (comic), <s>bībhatsa</s> (disgusting), and <s>raudra</s> (furious) rasas, the <s>sthāpanā</s> is considered appropriate.

children.text: vīthī-prahasane dve tu rūpakāṇāṃ bhide smṛte ||
children.translated_text: <s>Vīthī</s> (one-act) and <s>prahasana</s> (farce) are the two types of <s>rūpaka</s> (dramatic form).
Now the <s>sandhi</s> (juncture) —
The conjunction of each state with each element of the plot, one by one,
is to be known as <s>sandhi</s> (juncture) by those learned in the science of drama. || 30 ||
Therein, the <s>prakṛti</s> (plot element) —

children.text: pāñcavidhyāt kathāyās tu prakṛtiḥ pañcadhā smṛtā |
children.translated_text: Because the story is fivefold, the <s>prakṛti</s> (plot element) is considered to be of five kinds:

children.text: bījaṃ binduḥ patākā ca prakarī kāryam eva ca || 31 ||
children.translated_text: <s>bīja</s> (seed), <s>bindu</s> (drop), <s>patākā</s> (banner), <s>prakarī</s> (episode), and <s>kārya</s> (denouement). || 31 ||
Therein, the <s>bīja</s> (seed) —

children.text: yat tu svalpam upakṣiptaṃ bahudhā vistṛtiṃ gatam |
children.translated_text: That which is introduced in small measure and expands in many ways,

children.text: kāryasya kāraṇaṃ dhīrais tad bījam iti kathyate || 32 ||
children.translated_text: and is the cause of the denouement — that is called <s>bīja</s> (seed) by the wise. || 32 ||

children.text:
yathā lalita-mādhave prathama-dvitīyayor aṅkayoḥ kalpite mukha-sandhau nirūḍho
rādhā-mādhavayor anurāgo bījam ucyate |
children.translated_text: As in <s>Lalita-mādhava</s>, in the first and second acts, within the <s>mukha-sandhi</s> (opening juncture), the well-established love between <s>Rādhā</s> and <s>Mādhava</s> is called the <s>bīja</s> (seed).
Now the <s>bindu</s> (drop) —
When the principal fruit of the <s>bīja</s> is interrupted by other incidental results,
that which causes its continuity is called <s>bindu</s> (drop). || 33 ||

children.text:
yathā tatraive tṛtīya-caturthayoḥ kalpita pratimukha-sandhau
kṛṣṇa-pura-gamanādinā mukhya-phale vicchinne tenaiva samāśāsanaṃ etās tūrṇaṃ
nayata kiyatīḥ ity ādi sūrya-vākya-śravaṇa-janita-kṛṣṇa-pratyāśāṃ nīre
maṅkṣu-mimaṅkṣum (4.10) ityādyuktyā garbhāṅkaś ca binduḥ |
children.translated_text: As in that same work, in the third and fourth acts, within the <s>pratimukha-sandhi</s> (counter-opening juncture), when the principal fruit is interrupted by <s>Kṛṣṇa's</s> departure to the city and so on, the consolation through his own reassurance — 'Take them quickly, however many' — and the hope for <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> born from hearing <s>Sūrya's</s> words, 'Into the water, about to immerse quickly' (4.10) and such expressions, and the interlude act — that is the <s>bindu</s>.
Now the <s>patākā</s> (banner) —
That which serves as an aid to the principal matter and incidentally achieves its own purpose —
that is called <s>patākā</s> (banner) by the wise, like the activities of the <s>Yādava</s> minister. || 34 ||

children.text:
yathā tatraiva pañcama-ṣaṣṭhyoḥ kalpite garbha-sandhau
paurṇamāsy-uddhava-vṛttaṃ patākā |
children.translated_text: As in that same work, in the fifth and sixth acts, within the <s>garbha-sandhi</s> (embryonic juncture), the activities of <s>Paurṇamāsī</s> and <s>Uddhava</s> constitute the <s>patākā</s>.
Now the <s>prakarī</s> (episode) —

children.text: yat kevalaṃ parārthasya sādhakaṃ ca pradeśa-bhāk |
children.translated_text: That which merely accomplishes something for another's purpose and occupies a limited space —
that is designated as <s>prakarī</s> (episode), like the activities of <s>Nava-Vṛndā</s> and others. || 35 ||

children.text:
yathā tatraiva saptamāṣṭayoḥ kalpite vimarṣa-sandhau yathā
nava-vṛndādi-kulādi-vṛttaṃ prakarī ||
children.translated_text: As in that same work, in the seventh and eighth acts, within the <s>vimarśa-sandhi</s> (deliberation juncture), the activities of <s>Nava-Vṛndā</s> and other groups constitute the <s>prakarī</s>.
Now the <s>kārya</s> (denouement) —

children.text: vastunas tu samastasya sādhyaṃ kāryam iti smṛtam |
children.translated_text: That which is the object to be accomplished of the entire subject matter is called <s>kārya</s> (denouement).
As in <s>Lalita-mādhava</s>, the union of <s>Rādhā</s> and <s>Mādhava</s>. || 36 ||

children.text:
yathātra navama-daśamayoḥ kalpite nirvahaḥaṇa-sandhau rādhā-mādhavayoḥ
punaḥ saṅgama-puraḥsara-krīḍādi ||
children.translated_text: As in that work, in the ninth and tenth acts, within the <s>nirvahaṇa-sandhi</s> (conclusion juncture), the love-play preceded by the reunion of <s>Rādhā</s> and <s>Mādhava</s>.

children.text: pradhānam aṅgam iti ca tat tu syād dvividhaṃ punaḥ |
children.translated_text: The principal and the subordinate — thus it is again twofold.
The principal is the conduct of the hero — the all-pervading activity of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>. || 37 ||
The subordinate element would be the activity of those other than the hero.

children.text: nityaṃ patākā prakarī cāṅgaṃ bījādayaḥ kvacit || 38 ||
children.translated_text: The <s>patākā</s> (episode), <s>prakarī</s> (sub-episode), and <s>aṅga</s> (limb), as well as <s>bīja</s> (seed) and others, are sometimes present. || 38 ||

children.text: bījatvād bījam ādau syāt phalatvāt kāryam antataḥ |
children.translated_text: The <s>bīja</s> (seed), being the origin, should come at the beginning; the <s>phala</s> (fruit), being the result, comes at the end;

children.text: tayoḥ sandhāna-hetutvāt madhye binduṃ muhuḥ kṣipet || 39 ||
children.translated_text: Since it serves as the cause of connecting those two, one should frequently introduce the <s>bindu</s> (drop) in the middle. || 39 ||
The placement of the <s>patākā</s> and <s>prakarī</s> is according to appropriateness. || 40 ||
Thus the <s>bindu</s>, as in the fifth act (<s>Lalita-Mādhava</s> 5.23) —
Radiant with gems surpassing all, dark as a fresh <s>tamāla</s> tree,
bearing fresh <s>kuṅkuma</s> (saffron), the enchanting chest of <s>Hari</s> is victorious;
always clustered with stars, bearing the splendor of <s>Lakṣmī</s> arising like lightning,

children.text: yad abhram iva līlayā sphuṇam adabhram udbhrājate ||
children.translated_text: which, like a cloud, playfully shines forth abundantly in its full glory.
Thus the <s>bindu</s> should be observed in the sixth, seventh, and other acts as well.
Now the stages (<s>avasthā</s>) —
The five stages of the dramatic action, dependent on the activities of the <s>nāyaka</s> (hero) and others, are:
<s>ārambha</s> (inception), <s>yatna</s> (effort), <s>prāpty-āśā</s> (hope of attainment), <s>niyatāpti</s> (certainty of attainment), and <s>phalāgama</s> (fruition). || 41 ||
Of these, <s>ārambha</s> (inception) —
The exertion toward the principal fruit is called <s>ārambha</s> (inception) by the learned;

children.text:
yathā lalita-mādhave mukha-sandhau rādhā-mādhavayor anyonya-saṅgamāya
vyavasāya ārambhaḥ |
children.translated_text: As in <s>Lalita-Mādhava</s>, in the <s>mukha-sandhi</s> (opening juncture), the resolve of <s>Rādhā</s> and <s>Mādhava</s> for mutual union is the <s>ārambha</s> (inception);
Now <s>yatna</s> (effort) —

children.text: yatnas tu tat-phala-prāptāv autsukyena tu vartanam || 42 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Yatna</s> (effort) is the state of eagerness in attaining that fruit. || 42 ||

children.text:
yathā tatraiva pratimukha-sandhau rādhayā kṛṣṇasyānveṣaṇe kṛṣṇena ca
gandharva-kṛta-nṛtyādau rādhāvalokāyodyamo yatnaḥ |
children.translated_text: As in that same [play], in the <s>pratimukha-sandhi</s> (progression juncture), the search for <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> by <s>Rādhā</s>, and <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s exertion to behold <s>Rādhā</s> through the dance performed by the <s>Gandharvas</s> and such — that is the <s>yatna</s> (effort);
Now <s>prāpty-āśā</s> (hope of attainment) —
<s>Prāpty-āśā</s> (hope of attainment) is considered to be the expectation of success regarding one's own objective.
*NOTE: <s>siddha-sad-bhāvanā matā</s>.
And thus the sage (<s>Bharata</s>) has also said (19.11) —

children.text: īṣat prāptir yadā kācit phalasya parikalpyate |
children.translated_text: When there is even a slight attainment of the fruit imagined,
those who know the rules call that expectation of attainment a mere feeling.

children.text:
yathā, tatraiva garbha-sandhau rādhāyāḥ satrājiti samarpaṇ kṛṣṇasya ca
lalitā-śaṅkhacūḍa-ratnādi-lābhādinā sambhāvanāyogyatvāt prāptyāśā |
children.translated_text: As in that same [play], in the <s>garbha-sandhi</s> (development juncture), the entrusting of <s>Rādhā</s> to <s>Satrājit</s>, and <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s suitability for expectation through gaining <s>Lalitā</s>, <s>Śaṅkhacūḍa</s>'s jewel, and so forth — that is the <s>prāpty-āśā</s> (hope of attainment);
Now <s>niyatāpti</s> (certainty of attainment) —
<s>Niyatāpti</s> (certainty of attainment) is the conviction of the accomplishment of the objective without obstruction;

children.text:
yathā, tatraiva vimarśa-sandhau rādhā-darśanād avighnena phala-saṃsiddhi-niśayān
niyatāptiḥ |
children.translated_text: As in that same [play], in the <s>vimarśa-sandhi</s> (pause juncture), from the sight of <s>Rādhā</s>, the conviction of the accomplishment of the fruit without obstruction — that is <s>niyatāpti</s> (certainty of attainment);
Now <s>phalāgama</s> (fruition) —
The attainment of one's desired fruit is indeed <s>phalāgama</s> (fruition). || 43 ||

As in that same [play], in the <s>nirvahaṇa-sandhi</s> (conclusion juncture), the reunion with the kinsmen of <s>Vraja</s>, the winning of <s>Rādhā</s>, the consecration with jewels, and so forth — that is <s>phalāgama</s> (fruition);

children.text: patākāyās tv avasthānaṃ kvacid asti na vā kvacit |
children.translated_text: The stages of the <s>patākā</s> (episode) may or may not be present in some cases;
When devoid of a <s>patākā</s>, one should introduce the <s>bīja</s> (seed) and <s>bindu</s> (drop). || 44 ||
Now the limbs of the junctures (<s>sandhy-aṅgāni</s>) —
In the coordination of the parts of the story according to the principal purpose,
the connection with subsidiary meaning constitutes the joining form of the juncture. || 45 ||
<s>Mukha</s> (opening), <s>pratimukha</s> (progression), <s>garbha</s> (development), <s>vimarśa</s> (pause), and <s>upasaṃhṛti</s> (conclusion) —
these are the five junctures; among them, the definition of <s>mukha</s> (opening) is now stated. || 46 ||
Now <s>mukha</s> (the opening) —
The <s>mukha</s> (opening) is the arising of the <s>bīja</s> (seed), giving rise to various meanings and <s>rasas</s> (aesthetic sentiments);
In this, there are twelve limbs in accordance with the inception of the <s>bīja</s> (seed). || 47 ||
Here, the arising of the seed of love between <s>Rādhā</s> and <s>Mādhava</s>
is indicated with elegance, as in <s>Lalita-Mādhava</s>. || 48 ||
<s>Upakṣepa</s> (suggestion), <s>parikara</s> (elaboration), <s>parinyāsa</s> (culmination), <s>vilobhana</s> (enticement),
<s>Yukti</s> (reasoning), <s>prāpti</s> (attainment), <s>samādhāna</s> (resolution), <s>vidhāna</s> (arrangement), <s>paribhāvanā</s> (astonishment), || 49 ||
<s>Udbheda</s> (disclosure), <s>bheda</s> (incitement), and <s>karaṇa</s> (action) — the definitions of these are now stated.

children.text: upakṣepas tu bījasya sūcanaṃ kathyate budhaiḥ || 50 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Upakṣepa</s> is said by the learned to be the hinting of the <s>bīja</s> (seed). || 50 ||
Of these, <s>upakṣepa</s> (suggestion) —
As in <s>Lalita-Mādhava</s>, in the first act (1.14) —

children.text: paurṇamāsī -- (hanta rādhā-mādhavayor iti paṭhitvā) vatse gārgi śrūyatām |
children.translated_text: <s>Paurṇamāsī</s> — (having read 'of <s>Rādhā</s> and <s>Mādhava</s>') Dear child <s>Gārgī</s>, listen.
In the stream of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s sidelong glances, with the radiant sun merged and braided together,
in the city of the celestial river of <s>Rādhā</s>'s smiling moonlight, drinking the nectar;
Within, the accumulated heat being licked away by the spreading frost of delight,

children.text: krāntvā sapta jaganti samprati vayaṃ sarvordhvam adhyāsmahe ||
children.translated_text: having traversed the seven worlds, we now sit at the very summit of all.
Here, the hinting of the seed of love between <s>Rādhā</s> and <s>Mādhava</s> is the <s>upakṣepa</s> (suggestion).
Now <s>parikara</s> (elaboration) —
The amplification of the <s>bīja</s> (seed) is known by the learned as <s>parikara</s> (elaboration);
As in that same [play] (1.24) —
<s>Gārgī</s> (in Sanskrit) —

children.text: hriyam avagṛhya gṛhebhyaḥ karṣati rādhāṃ vanāya yā nipuṇā |
children.translated_text: She who skillfully seizes modesty from the homes and draws <s>Rādhā</s> to the forest,
that messenger born of an excellent lineage, a <s>kākalī</s> (cuckoo-like voice), devoted to her purpose, is victorious.
Here, through drawing to the forest and such, the amplification of the seed of love constitutes the <s>parikara</s> (elaboration).
Now <s>parinyāsa</s> (culmination) —
The narration of the ripening of the <s>bīja</s> (seed) is called <s>parinyāsa</s> (culmination). || 52 ||
As in that same [play], in the first act —

children.text: rādhā (saromāñcam): lalide kā kkhu kahnatti sunīadi jeṇa kealaṃ kaṇṇassa jjea
children.translated_text: <s>Rādhā</s> (with horripilation): <s>Lalitā</s>, who indeed is this <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> that is heard of? By whom, merely by becoming a guest of the ear,

children.text: adidhīhonteṇa ummatīkijjahmi || [lalite, kaḥ khalu kṛṣṇa iti śrūyate? Yena kevalaṃ
children.translated_text: I am driven to madness! [<s>Lalitā</s>, who indeed is this <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> that is heard of? By whom, merely
by becoming a guest of the ear, I am driven to madness!]
Here, through the narration of the madness-inducing effect, being the declaration of the seed's ripening, it constitutes <s>parinyāsa</s> (culmination).
Now <s>vilobhana</s> (enticement) —
The description of the qualities of the <s>nāyaka</s> (hero) and others is <s>vilobhana</s> (enticement);
As in that same [play], in the first act —
There <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> (approaching) —
Having beheld your radiant face, O <s>Rādhikā</s>,
the moon, its mind overcome with a burden of shame, seeking to equal its beauty,
having grown thin, sprinkled by the waves of the celestial river,
performs austerities, stationed in the dense forest of matted locks of <s>Śiva</s>.
There, the description of the qualities of <s>Rādhā</s>'s beauty constitutes <s>vilobhana</s> (enticement).
Now <s>yukti</s> (reasoning) —

children.text: samyak prayojanānāṃ hi nirṇayo yuktir iṣyate || 54 ||
children.translated_text: The proper determination of purposes is considered <s>yukti</s> (reasoning). || 54 ||
As in that same [play] (para 1.111-2) —

children.text:
yaśodā -- bhaadi candāalī ṇomāliā rāhā māharia sabbāo maha āsāo
guṇāsohara-pūreṇa purei | tatthabi baccho bia baccā laiī ṇetta-bhiṅgaṃ
sondara-marandeṇa āṇandei || [bhagavati candrāvalī nava-mālikā rādhā mādhavī
ca sarvathā mama āśā guṇa-saurabha-pūreṇa pūrayati | tatrāpi vatsa iva vatsā
laghvī netra-bhṛṅgaṃ saundarya-makarandena ānandayati | ]
children.translated_text: <s>Yaśodā</s> — O revered one! <s>Candrāvalī</s> the new jasmine, <s>Rādhā</s> the <s>mādhavī</s> creeper, in every way fulfill my hopes with the fullness of their fragrant qualities; and moreover, like a calf, the young one delights the bee of the eyes with the honey of her beauty. [O revered one! <s>Candrāvalī</s> the new jasmine, <s>Rādhā</s> the <s>mādhavī</s> creeper, in every way fulfill my hopes with the fullness of their fragrant qualities; and moreover, like a calf, the young one delights the bee of the eyes with the honey of her beauty.]

children.text: bhagavatī: gokuleśvari | sarveṣāṃ gokula-vāsināṃ īdṛg eva samudācāra iti |
children.translated_text: <s>Bhagavatī</s>: O queen of <s>Gokula</s>! Such indeed is the conduct of all the residents of <s>Gokula</s>.

children.text: atra rādhāyāṃ sarvato'dhikānāṃ guṇotkarṣāṇāṃ nirṇayo yuktiḥ |
children.translated_text: Here, the determination of <s>Rādhā</s>'s qualities as surpassing all others constitutes the <s>yukti</s> (reasoning).
Now <s>prāpti</s> (attainment) —

children.text: prājñaiḥ sukhasya samprāptiḥ prāptir ity abhidhīyate || 55 ||
children.translated_text: The attainment of happiness is called <s>prāpti</s> (attainment) by the wise. || 55 ||

children.text:
yathā tatraiva (1.51) --
tatra kṛṣṇaḥ (punar utkarṇo bhavan sapulakam)
children.translated_text: As in that same [play] (1.51) — There <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> (again listening intently, with horripilation) —
She who, with waves of sweetness, arrests in the sky
the calls of the <s>sārasa</s> cranes intoxicated with the passion of love;
this tinkling of <s>Rādhā</s>'s anklet bells arises,
transforming in my heart a festival of agitations.
Here, from hearing the tinkling of <s>Rādhā</s>'s [anklet bells], the attainment of happiness for <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> constitutes <s>prāpti</s> (attainment).
Now <s>samādhāna</s> (resolution) —
The re-planting of the <s>bīja</s> (seed) is called <s>samādhāna</s> (resolution) here. || 56 ||
As in that same [play] —

children.text:
rādhā (sāsraṃ): kundalaie, abi ṇāma imassa ekassa bi hadaṇttassa maggaṃ kkhaṇaṃ
bi ārohissadi so maha dhaṇṇassa kaṇṇassa adidhī | [kundalate! api nāma
tasyaikasyāpi hata-netrasya mārgaṃ kṣaṇam api ārohiṣyati sa me dhanyasya
karṇasyātithiḥ |]
children.translated_text: <s>Rādhā</s> (tearfully): <s>Kundalatā</s>! If only that guest of my fortunate ear would mount the path of even this one eye, bereft of sight, even for a moment! [<s>Kundalatā</s>! If only that guest of my fortunate ear would mount the path of even this one eye, bereft of sight, even for a moment!]

children.text: atra svayaṃ rādhayā punar anurāga-bījasyādhānāt samādhānam |
children.translated_text: Here, since <s>Rādhā</s> herself re-plants the seed of love, it constitutes <s>samādhāna</s> (resolution).
Now <s>vidhāna</s> (arrangement) —

children.text: sukha-duḥkha-karaṃ yat tu tad-vidhānaṃ budhā viduḥ || 57 ||
children.translated_text: That which produces happiness and sorrow is known by the learned as <s>vidhāna</s> (arrangement). || 57 ||
As in that same [play], in the second act —

children.text: rādhikā - (dūrataḥ kṛṣṇam īṣad avalokya, janāntikaṃ saṃskṛtena)
children.translated_text: <s>Rādhikā</s> — (seeing <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> slightly from afar, aside, in Sanskrit) —
O companion, who is this fearless youth, dark as a rain cloud,
from where has he come to the land of <s>Vraja</s>, with the graceful gait of an intoxicated elephant?
Alas! With his charming, creeping, thievish sidelong glances,
he plunders the wealth of my composure from the treasury of my heart. (2.11)

children.text:
(punar avekṣya) haddhī haddhī ppamādo, lalide pekkha pekkha eṇaṃ bamhaāriṇaṃ
daṭṭhūṇa vikkhuhidaṃ maha hadahiaam | tā imassa mahāpābassa aggippaveso jebba
parāacittam | [ha dhik hā dhik pramādaḥ | lalite prekṣya prekṣya | etaṃ
brahmacāriṇaṃ dṛṣṭvā vikṣbdhaṃ me hata-hṛdayam | tad etasya mahā-pāpasya
agni-praveśa eva prāyaścittam |]
children.translated_text: (Looking again) Alas, alas, what a calamity! <s>Lalitā</s>, look, look! Seeing this <s>brahmacārin</s> (celibate student), my wretched heart is agitated. So entering fire is indeed the atonement for this great sin! [Alas, alas, what a calamity! <s>Lalitā</s>, look, look! Seeing this <s>brahmacārin</s>, my wretched heart is agitated. So entering fire is indeed the atonement for this great sin!]

children.text:
lalitā : halā, saccaṃ kadhesi | tā ṇūṇaṃ sabaṇṇataṇaṃ bhāmedi | [halā, satyaṃ
kathayasi, tan nūnaṃ savarṇatvaṃ bhramayati |]
children.translated_text: <s>Lalitā</s>: Friend, you speak truly. Then surely it is the similarity of complexion that confuses you. [Friend, you speak truly. Then surely it is the similarity of complexion that confuses you.]
<s>Rādhikā</s> — (looking again, in Sanskrit) —
O companion, this is <s>Hari</s> who has assumed the guise of a <s>brahmacārin</s>;

children.text: kim ayam itarathā me vidravaty antarātmā |
children.translated_text: how else would my inner soul melt so?
The moonstone platform exudes streams of perspiration —
surely not without the moonlight of the friend of the <s>kumuda</s> (night-lotus). (2.12)

children.text:
atra rādhāyāḥ kṛṣṇa-buddhyā viprabuddhyā ca sukha-duḥkha-kathanād vidhānam |
atha paribhāvanā -
children.translated_text: Here, the narration of happiness and sorrow through <s>Rādhā</s>'s recognizing <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> and then mistaking him for a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> constitutes <s>vidhāna</s> (arrangement). Now <s>paribhāvanā</s> (astonishment) —
The astonishment of the mind produced by praiseworthy assemblages of qualities is <s>paribhāvanā</s> (astonishment). || 58 ||
As in that same [play], in the first act —
<s>Rādhā</s> (with wonder, in Sanskrit) —
O fair-faced one, with his sharp, long, sidelong glance-chisels,

children.text: yugapad ayam apūrvaḥ kaḥ puro viśva-karmā
children.translated_text: who is this unprecedented <s>Viśvakarmā</s> (cosmic architect) before us
who constructs the precincts of the cow-pasture with millions of emerald gems? (1.52)
Splitting the boulders of family honor, bodily virtue, and dharma,

children.text: lalitā: halā, so eso de parāṇa-nādho | [halā, sa eṣa te prāṇanāthaḥ |]
children.translated_text: <s>Lalitā</s>: Friend, that is indeed your lord of life. [Friend, that is indeed your lord of life.]
<s>Rādhā</s> — (with ecstasy, again in Sanskrit) —
Is he the nectar-moonlight of the <s>gopikā</s>-lotus garden?
Is he the festival of the coronation of youth blossoming in <s>Gokula</s>?
Is he the spring season of delight for the cuckoo of my mind?
O slender-waisted one, he sprinkles the pair of eyes with waves of nectar. (1.53)

children.text:
atra kṛṣṇasya vaidagdha-saundaryādi-guṇa-nidarśanena ca
rādhā-camatkāra-kathanāt paribhāvanā |
children.translated_text: Here, through displaying the qualities of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s charm and beauty, and the narration of <s>Rādhā</s>'s astonishment, it constitutes <s>paribhāvanā</s> (astonishment).
Now <s>udbheda</s> (disclosure) —

children.text: bījasya tu ya udghātaḥ sa udbheda iti smṛtaḥ || 59 ||
children.translated_text: The disclosure of the <s>bīja</s> (seed) is known as <s>udbheda</s> (disclosure). || 59 ||
As in that same [play], in the second act —
<s>Rādhikā</s> (aside, in Sanskrit) —
The inner fear arising from the elders of the restless-eyed women flashes forth,

children.text: kula-sthitir alaṃ tu me manasi tāvad unmīlati |
children.translated_text: and the adherence to family tradition indeed awakens in my mind;
but as long as this lotus-face, with its trembling <s>makara</s>-earrings shining on blooming cheeks,

children.text: na yāvad aparokṣatām idam apaiti vaktrāmbujam || (2.26)
children.translated_text: does not pass from my direct sight — (2.26)
Here, since the seed of love that was previously concealed is disclosed by her own mouth, it constitutes <s>udbheda</s> (disclosure).
Now <s>bheda</s> (incitement) —
The stimulation of the <s>bīja</s> (seed), or the breaking through of resistance, is <s>bheda</s> (incitement). || 60 ||
As in that same [play] —

children.text:
kundalatā - rāhe, akkhalidaṃ tumha sadībbadaṃ, tā alaṃ saaṃ vikkhābideṇa | [rādhe,
jāne saskhalitaṃ tava satī-vrataṃ, tad alaṃ svayaṃ vikhyāpitena | ]
children.translated_text: <s>Kundalatā</s> — <s>Rādhā</s>, I know your vow of chastity has slipped; so enough with proclaiming it yourself! [<s>Rādhā</s>, I know your vow of chastity has slipped; so enough with proclaiming it yourself!]

children.text:
viśākhā - (sa-praṇayābhyasūyam) kundalade! kā kkhu abarā tumaṃ bia vaṃsīe
tiṇṇi-sañjhaṃ āaḍḍhīadi ? [rādhe, kā khalv aparā tvām iva vaṃśyā trisandhyam
ākṛṣyate |]
kundalatā (sanarma-smitaṃ, saṃskṛtena) -
children.translated_text: <s>Viśākhā</s> — (with affectionate jealousy) <s>Kundalatā</s>! Who else but you is drawn by the flute thrice daily? [<s>Rādhā</s>, who else but you is drawn by the flute thrice daily?] <s>Kundalatā</s> (with a playful smile, in Sanskrit) —
I compassionately offer hundreds of masses of clear wisdom —
may the unbroken vow of chastity stand firm in one such as you;
even when the sound of the flute, transformed into the essence of all sweetness, is heard

children.text: manaḥ sakhi manāg api tyajati vo na dhairyaṃ yathā || (2.20)
children.translated_text: O friend, your mind does not abandon its composure even slightly. (2.20)

children.text: atra kundalatayā rādhādi-premasyottejanād bhedanāc cātmanas tābhyo bhedaḥ |
children.translated_text: Here, through <s>Kundalatā</s>'s stimulating and breaking apart the love of <s>Rādhā</s> and others, her distinction from them is established.
Now, <s>karaṇa</s> (dramatic action) —
That which undertakes the matter at hand is called <s>karaṇa</s> (dramatic action). || 61 ||
For example, in that same [play] —
<s>Kundalatā</s> — (in Sanskrit)

children.text: trapāṃ tyaja kuḍaṅgakaṃ praviśa santu te maṅgalā-
children.translated_text: Abandon your shyness, enter the bower, may auspicious things be yours —
on the battlefield of <s>Anaṅga</s> (the god of love), become the supreme warrior.
At the rising of the sun, the string of victory-fame songs about you
shall be sung aloud before the enemy of <s>Mura</s> by his female companions. || 2.24 ||
Here, because of the narration of the undertaking of the matter at hand, namely the amorous sport, it is <s>karaṇa</s>.
Now, <s>pratimukha-sandhi</s> (the second juncture) —
The <s>pratimukha</s> (counter-opening) is the visible manifestation of the seed (<s>bīja</s>).
Through the effort of approaching the <s>bindu</s> (drop), its limbs are thirteen. || 62 ||
Due to the extreme and difficult separation of <s>Rādhā</s> and <s>Mādhava</s> here,
the seed of love, both visible and invisible, is as in <s>Lalita-Mādhava</s>. || 63 ||
<s>Vilāsa</s> (graceful play), <s>parisarpa</s> (recollection), <s>vidhuta</s> (distress), <s>śama</s> (pacification), <s>narma</s> (jest),
<s>narma-dyuti</s> (delight from jest), <s>pragamana</s> (progression), <s>virodha</s> (conflict), <s>paryupāsana</s> (conciliation),

children.text: puṣpaṃ vajram upanyāso varṇa-saṃhāra ity api || 64 ||
children.translated_text: <s>puṣpa</s> (flower/revelation), <s>vajra</s> (thunderbolt/harsh speech), <s>upanyāsa</s> (persuasion), and <s>varṇa-saṃhāra</s> (convergence of characters) — thus. || 64 ||
Of these, <s>vilāsa</s> (graceful play) —
<s>Vilāsa</s> is declared to be activity for the purpose of union. || 65 ||
For example, in the fourth act of that same [play] —
<s>Mādhava</s> — (placing the flute on his lips) —
O friend of the eyes, reveal the fresh brilliance of the sun,
which precedes the city of <s>Hari</s>'s horses, the green parrots.

children.text: cakrābhikhyaḥ kim api virahād ākulaḥ kākū-lakṣaṃ
children.translated_text: The one named <s>Cakra</s>, somehow agitated by separation, making gestures of entreaty,

children.text: kurvan mukhyas tvayi sa vayasām arthibhāvaṃ tanoti ||4.22||
children.translated_text: that chief one extends toward you the attitude of a supplicant among companions. ||4.22||
Here, because of the narration of <s>Mādhava</s>'s activity for the purpose of union, it is <s>vilāsa</s>.
Now, <s>parisarpa</s> (recollection) —

children.text: smṛtir naṣṭasya bījasya parisarpa iti smṛtaḥ || 66 ||
children.translated_text: The recollection of a lost seed is known as <s>parisarpa</s>. || 66 ||
For example, in that same [play] —

children.text: kṛṣṇaḥ - sakhe satyam āśayaiva kadarthyamāno'smi | yataḥ -
children.translated_text: <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> — Friend, truly I am being tormented by hope alone. For —
When the fierce-rayed one appeared from afar in a circle, out of compassion,

children.text: dūrān maṇḍalataḥ kṛpāturatayā yat prādurāsīt tadā |
children.translated_text: pointing toward the distressed and vocal one who was about to plunge into the water,

children.text: hā dhig vāg-amṛtena tena janitas tasyāḥ punaḥ saṅgama-
children.translated_text: alas! The sprout of hope for reunion with her, born from that nectar of speech,

children.text: pratyāśāṅkura uccakair mama sakhe svāntaṃ haṭhād vidhyati ||10||
children.translated_text: forcefully pierces my heart loudly, O friend! ||10||

children.text:
atra rādhā-tirodhānān naṣṭasyānurāga-bījasya punaḥ sūrya-vacanenānusmaraṇāt
parisarpaḥ |
children.translated_text: Here, because of the recollection — through <s>Sūrya</s>'s words — of the seed of love that was lost due to <s>Rādhā</s>'s disappearance, it is <s>parisarpa</s>.
Now, <s>vidhuta</s> (distress) —
<s>Vidhuta</s> is said to be the grief arising from non-attainment of the desired object,
or alternatively, <s>vidhuta</s> is the rejection of conciliation and such. || 67 ||
For example, in the third act of that same [play] —
<s>Rādhā</s> (with tears) —
The jesting words were not freely drunk by the cavity of my ears,
the beauty of <s>Hari</s>'s lotus-face was not gazed upon without fear, O fair-faced one,

children.text: harer vakṣaḥ-pīṭhaṃ na kila ghanam āliṅgitam abhūd
children.translated_text: the broad chest of <s>Hari</s> was certainly not closely embraced —

children.text: iti dhyāyaṃ dhyāyaṃ sphuṭati luṭhad antar mama manaḥ || (3.26)
children.translated_text: thinking and thinking thus, my heart, rolling within, bursts asunder. (3.26)

children.text: atra prakaṭam eva duḥkhaṃ vidhutam | yathā vā tatraiva -
children.translated_text: Here the grief is plainly <s>vidhuta</s>. Or alternatively, in that same [play] —
<s>Paurṇamāsī</s>: Listen to what the excellent fair-complexioned lady describes (offstage) —
Do not make this consolation, you are hopeless,
with drying face, extolling my virtues!
Even from afar, though bearing no tenderness, repeatedly the wheel of patience —
see, it tears open the belly of forbearance! || (3.17)
Here, because of <s>Rādhā</s>'s acceptance of the conciliation made by <s>Viśākhā</s>, it is <s>vidhuta</s>.
Now, <s>śama</s> (pacification) —

children.text: arateḥ śamanaṃ dhīraiḥ śama ity abhidhīyate || 68 ||
children.translated_text: The sages call the calming of displeasure <s>śama</s> (pacification). || 68 ||
For example, in the fourth act of that same [play] —

children.text:
vṛndā - nāgarendra! muñca vaimanasyam | sāmprataṃ bhavad-abhīṣṭa-siddhaye
śārikāmukhena lalitāṃ sandiśya viśākhayā bhavantaṃ nivedayiṣyāmi |
children.translated_text: <s>Vṛndā</s> — O lord of serpents! Abandon your despondency. Now, for the fulfillment of your desire, I shall send a message to <s>Lalitā</s> through the <s>śārikā</s> (mynah bird) and inform you through <s>Viśākhā</s>.

children.text: atra jaṭilayā rādhāyāṃ nītāyāṃ vṛndayā mādhavasyārati-śamanāc chamaḥ |
children.translated_text: Here, because <s>Vṛndā</s> calms <s>Mādhava</s>'s displeasure after <s>Rādhā</s> was taken away by <s>Jaṭilā</s>, it is <s>śama</s>.

children.text: apaṭhitvā śamaṃ kaścit sa paṭhaty atra tāpanam |
children.translated_text: Without reading <s>śama</s>, someone reads here <s>tāpana</s> (tormenting) instead.
Thus (<s>Sāhitya-darpaṇa</s> 6.91),

children.text: upāyādarśanaṃ yat tu tāpanaṃ nāma tad bhavet || iti |
children.translated_text: That which is the perception of a means [to achieve the goal] is called <s>tāpana</s>. Thus.
For example, in the third act —

children.text: vṛndā - hā dhik, hā hā dhik | paśya -
children.translated_text: <s>Vṛndā</s> — Alas, woe! Alas, alas, woe! Behold —
Neither able to tell nor not to tell <s>Murabhid</s>'s (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s) news of going to the city,
<s>Viśākhā</s> and the others somehow cannot bring themselves to tell <s>Rādhā</s>.
Completely overwhelmed by dense waves of numbness,
they only weakly manage whispered, ear-to-ear communication. || (3.12)
Here the perception of a means is quite evident.
Now, <s>narma</s> (jest) —

children.text: parihāsa-pradhānaṃ yad vacanaṃ narma tad viduḥ || 69 ||
children.translated_text: That speech which is predominantly humorous is known as <s>narma</s> (jest). || 69 ||
For example, in the fourth act of that same [play] —

children.text:
jaṭilā (nāsikāgre tarjanīṃ vinyasya sthitā dhunvantī sāścaryam) are
bāliā-bhujaṅga! kaṃ ḍaṃsiduṃ ettha bhammasi | [are bālikā-bhujaṅga! kāṃ
ḍaṃśitum atra bhrāmyasi |]
children.translated_text: <s>Jaṭilā</s> — (standing with her forefinger placed on the tip of her nose, shaking it, with amazement) Hey, you young-girl-snake! Whom are you looking to bite, roaming about here? [Sanskrit rendering of the Prakrit]
<s>Mādhava</s> — O thick-lipped one! You yourself, the ghost-woman of the cow-pen!
Here the jest is quite evident.
Now, <s>narma-dyuti</s> (delight from jest) —
The delight born from jest is called <s>narma-dyuti</s> by the learned. || 70 ||
For example, in that same [play] —

children.text:
lalitā (smitvā) api sarale, tujjha hiae katthūriāpattabhaṃgaṃ lihantīe mae
paccakkhīkidā siviṇa-saṃgiṇāara-kuṃjara bibbhamāsi | tā phuḍaṃ kadhehi,
taiajaṇasaṃgajogge tasmiṃ osare dīhasuttā nīvī-sahaarī jhatti ṇikkantā ṇa vetti | [ayi
sarale! tava hṛdaye kastūrikāpatra-bhaṅgaṃ likhantyā mayā pratyakṣīkṛtā
svapna-saṅgināgara-kuñjara-vibhramāsi | tat sphuṭaṃ kathaya | tṛtīya-jana-saṃyogye
tasminn avasare dīrgha-sūtrā nīvī-sahacarī jhaṭiti niṣkrāntā na veti ]
children.translated_text: <s>Lalitā</s> (smiling) — O simple one, while I was drawing a musk-leaf design on your heart, I witnessed your dream-lover elephant's play! So tell me clearly — at that moment suitable for a third person's company, did the slow-moving companion of the waist-cord suddenly slip out unknowing? [Sanskrit rendering of the Prakrit]

children.text:
rādhikā (svagatam) kadhaṃ takkidaṃ akkhidhuttāe | (prakāśam,
sa-bhrū-bhaṅgam) vāme, kitti aliaṃ āsaṃkasi? [kathaṃ tarkitam atidhūrtayā? vāme,
kim ity alīkam āśaṅkase?] (Act 4, paras. 92-93)
atra lalitā-narma-jātayā rādhāyā rucyā dhṛtyā vā narma-dyutiḥ |
children.translated_text:
<s>Rādhikā</s> (aside) — How did that cunning rogue guess it? (aloud, with a frown) O wicked one, why do you suspect falsehood? [Sanskrit rendering of the Prakrit] (Act 4, paras. 92-93)
Here, through the delight — or composure — of <s>Rādhā</s> born from <s>Lalitā</s>'s jest, it is <s>narma-dyuti</s>.
Now, <s>pragamana</s> (progression) —
A series of successive speeches constitutes <s>pragamana</s> (progression). || 71 ||
For example, in that same [play] —

children.text:
rādhā -
baa-ṇaravaī-ṇandaṇaṃ sabandhuṃ,
raha-pabarobari pekkhia phphurantam |
[vraja-nṛpati-nandanaṃ sabandhuṃ

children.translated_text: [seeing the son of the king of <s>Vraja</s> with his kinsmen, shining upon the top of the excellent chariot]
my body stumbles — how can the earth

children.text: bhramati kutaḥ kim amī naṭanti nīpāḥ || (3.14)
children.translated_text: be spinning? Why are these <s>nīpa</s> trees dancing? || (3.14)

<s>Rādhā</s> —
Seeing the son of the king of <s>Vraja</s> with his kinsmen,
shining upon the top of the excellent chariot, [Sanskrit rendering of the Prakrit]

children.text:
lalitā - sahi rāhe, mā visīda | pabbada-parikkamobakkamo eso | [sakhi rādhe, mā
viṣīda, parvata-parikramopakrama eṣaḥ |]
children.translated_text: <s>Lalitā</s> — Friend <s>Rādhā</s>, do not despair! This is the beginning of a circumambulation of the mountain. [Sanskrit rendering of the Prakrit]
<s>Rādhikā</s> —

children.text: sahacari, parijñātaṃ sadya samastam idaṃ mayā
children.translated_text: O companion, I have immediately understood all of this completely.
How long will you be able to conceal things with clever fabrications?

children.text: virama kṛpaṇe bhāvī nāyaṃ harer viraha-klamo
children.translated_text: Desist, O wretched one — this will not be <s>Hari</s>'s fatigue of separation;

children.text: mama kim abhavan kaṇṭhe prāṇā muhur nirapatrapāḥ || (3.15)
children.translated_text: why have my shameless life-breaths repeatedly remained in my throat? || (3.15)

children.text:
ity atra rādhā-lalitayor uttarottaraṃ pragamanam |
atha virodhaḥ -
children.translated_text:
Here, the successive exchanges between <s>Rādhā</s> and <s>Lalitā</s> constitute <s>pragamana</s>.
Now, <s>virodha</s> (conflict) —

children.text: yatra vyasanam āyāti virodhaḥ sa nigadyate || 72 ||
children.translated_text: Where calamity arises, that is called <s>virodha</s> (conflict). || 72 ||
For example, in that same [play] —
<s>Rādhikā</s> —
The heart of <s>Hari</s>, matured with waves of compassion toward the afflicted,
thus the expectation of seeing you arises among the bent-browed <s>Ābhīra</s> women.
But this cruel agony of separation, fond of cutting the knots of vital spots, a hostile enemy,
does not endure the festival of my good fortune! || (3.27)
Here the conflict is clearly evident through <s>Rādhā</s>'s arrival.
Now, <s>paryupāsana</s> (conciliation) —
The appeasement of one who is angered is called <s>paryupāsana</s> (conciliation) by the wise. || 73 ||
For example, in the fourth [act] of that same [play] —

children.text:
jaṭilā - ai ahisārasaggāvejjhāiṇi lalide, eṇhiṃ puttau me ahimaṇṇu bidūre gadotthi,
tā suṇṇaṃ gharaṃ mukkia kīsa tue āṇīdā bahuḍī | [ayi abhisāra-mārgopādhyāyini
lalite! idānīṃ putrako me'bhimanyur vidūre gato'sti | tat śūnyaṃ gṛhaṃ muktvā
kasmāt tvayā nītātra vadhūṭī ?]
children.translated_text: <s>Jaṭilā</s> — O <s>Lalitā</s>, teacher of the path of secret rendezvous! Now my son <s>Abhimanyu</s> has gone far away. So why have you brought the bride here, leaving the empty house? [Sanskrit rendering of the Prakrit]

children.text:
lalitā (saśaṅkam ātma-gatam) haddhī, ḍāinīe aḍāhiṇa-paidīe ḍdahiṭhammi
buṭhṭhiāe | (prakāśam) ayye gaggīe bhaṇidaṃ ajja māhabīpupphehiṃ pūido sūro
surahikoḍppado hodutti māhabī-maṇḍabaṃ laṃhikhadā mae rāhiā, tā ppasīda
ppasīda | [hā dhik! ḍākinyā dakṣiṇa-pravṛttyā dagdhāsmi vṛddhayā | ārye, gārgyā
bhaṇitam, adya mādhavī-puṣpaiḥ pūjitaḥ sūryaḥ surabhi-koṭi-prado bhavati | iti
mādhavī-maṇḍapaṃ lambhitā mayā rādhikā | tat prasīda prasīda |
children.translated_text: <s>Lalitā</s> (fearfully, aside) — Alas, I am burned by the old witch's rightward approach! (aloud) Noble lady, <s>Gārgī</s> said that today the sun, worshipped with <s>mādhavī</s> flowers, grants ten million fragrances. So I brought <s>Rādhikā</s> to the <s>mādhavī</s> bower. Please be appeased, be appeased! [Sanskrit rendering of the Prakrit]

children.text: atra ruṣṭāyā jaṭilāyā lalitayāpy anunayāt paryupāsanam |
children.translated_text: Here, because of <s>Lalitā</s>'s appeasement of the angered <s>Jaṭilā</s>, it is <s>paryupāsana</s>.
Now, <s>puṣpa</s> (flower/recognition) —

children.text: pariśeṣo vidhānaṃ yat puṣpaṃ tad iti saṃjñitam || 74 ||
children.translated_text: That arrangement which remains after elimination is called <s>puṣpa</s> (flower). || 74 ||
For example, in the third [act] of that same [play] —

children.text:
vidūre kaṃsārir mukuṭita-śikhaṇḍāvalir asau
pure gaurāṅgībhiḥ kalita-parirambho vilasati |
children.translated_text: The enemy of <s>Kaṃsa</s>, with a crown of peacock feathers, is there in the distance — in the city, he sports, embraced by fair-limbed women.
(thus, looking again with jealousy, with sorrow)
it is a cloud, stealing the lightning-streaks, that has descended upon the mountain. || (3.40)
No, I think this is not my beloved — sweet as the luster of <s>Indra</s>'s bow,
Here, through the subsequent recognition of it as a cloud, it is <s>puṣpa</s>.
Now, <s>vajra</s> (thunderbolt/harsh speech) —

children.text: vajraṃ tad iti vijñeyaṃ sākṣān niṣṭhura-bhāṣaṇam || 75 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Vajra</s> is to be known as directly harsh speech. || 75 ||
For example, in the fourth [act] of that same [play] —

children.text:
jaṭilā (pṛṣṭhataḥ parikramya putrasya hastam ākarṣantī sākṣepam) re
goula-kisorī-laṃpaḍao, are paraghara-laṇṭhanao | kahaṃ tumaṃ bi appaṇo puttaṃ
maṇṇissadi jaḍilā ? [re gokula-kiśorī-lampaṭa, are paragṛha-luṇṭhaka | kathaṃ
tvām apy ātmanaḥ putraṃ maṃsyati jaṭilā |]
children.translated_text: <s>Jaṭilā</s> (going around behind and pulling her son's hand, with reproach) — Hey, you who are lustful after cowherd girls! Hey, you plunderer of others' homes! How will <s>Jaṭilā</s> consider even you her own son? [Sanskrit rendering of the Prakrit]

children.text: atra jaṭilāyāḥ putraṃ prati niṣṭhura-bhāṣaṇaṃ vajram |
children.translated_text: Here <s>Jaṭilā</s>'s harsh speech toward her son is <s>vajra</s>.
Now, <s>upanyāsa</s> (persuasion) —

children.text: yuktibhiḥ sahito yo'rthaḥ upanyāsaḥ sa ucyate || 76 ||
children.translated_text: A statement accompanied by reasoning is called <s>upanyāsa</s> (persuasion). || 76 ||

For example, in the third [act] of that same [play] —
(offstage)

children.text: adya prāṇa-parārdhato'pi dayite dūraṃ prayāte harau
children.translated_text: Today, when <s>Hari</s>, dearer than life itself, has gone far away,

children.text: hā dhig duḥsaha-śoka-śaṅkubhir abhūd viddhāntarā rādhikā |
children.translated_text: alas! <s>Rādhikā</s> has been pierced within by the stakes of unbearable grief.

children.text: tenāsyāḥ pratiṣedham artha-carite tvaṃ mā kṛthā mā kṛthāḥ
children.translated_text: Therefore, do not, do not obstruct her distressed conduct —

children.text: kṣīṇeyaṃ kṣaṇam atra suṣṭhu viluṭhaty ārta-svaraṃ roditum || (3.29)
children.translated_text: she is exhausted, let her roll about here for a moment and weep aloud with an anguished voice! || (3.29)

children.text: atra yukti-sahitārthatā prakaṭaiva | kecit upanyāsaḥ prasādanam iti (SāhD 6.93)
children.translated_text: Here the statement accompanied by reasoning is quite evident. Some call <s>upanyāsa</s> as <s>prasādana</s> (propitiation) (<s>Sāhitya-darpaṇa</s> 6.93).
They say thus. An example of that is in the fourth [act] —

children.text: jaṭilā - kulaputti, sireṇa me sābidāsi | [kulaputri, śirasā me śāpitāsi |]
children.translated_text: <s>Jaṭilā</s> — Noble daughter-in-law, I adjure you by my head! [Sanskrit rendering of the Prakrit]
Here is <s>Jaṭilā</s>'s propitiation of <s>Rādhā</s>.
Now, <s>varṇa-saṃhāra</s> (convergence of characters) —
The coming together of similar characters is considered <s>varṇa-saṃhāra</s>. || 77 ||
For example, in the fourth [act] of that same [play] —

children.text: daityācāryas tad-āsye vikṛtim aruṇatāṃ malla-varyāḥ sakhāyo
children.translated_text: The preceptor of the <s>Daityas</s> [saw] distortion on his face, the chief wrestlers [saw] redness, the companions [saw]

children.text: gaṇḍaunnatyaṃ khaleśāḥ pralayam ṛṣi-gaṇā dhyāna-muñcāsram ambā |
children.translated_text: prominence of the cheeks, the wicked ones [saw] destruction, the sages [saw] meditation and shedding tears, the mother [saw]

children.text: romāñcaṃ sāṃyugīnāḥ kam api nava-camatkāram antaḥ surendrāḥ
children.translated_text: horripilation, the warriors [saw] some new and wondrous thing within, the lords of gods [saw]

children.text: lāsyaṃ dāsāḥ kaṭākṣaṃ yayur asita-dṛśāṃ prekṣya raṅge mukundam || (4.4)
children.translated_text: a dance, the servants [saw] a sidelong glance — thus seeing <s>Mukunda</s> in the arena, the dark-eyed women experienced [all these]. || (4.4)

children.text:
atra daityācārya-nāradādayaḥ brāhmaṇāḥ kṣitīśa-sāṃyugīnādayaḥ kṣatriyāḥ,
mallā dāsādayo vaiśyāḥ śūdrādayaś ca iti varṇa-saṃhāraḥ |
children.translated_text:
Here, the demon-preceptor, <s>Nārada</s> and others are <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>; the king, warriors and others are <s>Kṣatriyas</s>,
wrestlers, servants and others are <s>Vaiśyas</s>; and <s>Śūdras</s> and others — thus is the arrangement of <s>varṇas</s> (social classes).
Now the <s>garbha-sandhi</s> (development juncture) —
The <s>garbha</s> (development) arises from the pursuit of humor regarding the seed, whether seen or unseen;
This [juncture] has twelve limbs, following the subdivisions of the <s>patākā</s> (episodic plot). || 78 ||
The state of being supreme king [arises] incidentally; humor from the speech of bards;
A renewed search arose from the search for <s>Prasena</s>. || 79 ||
From the diminution arose a renewed search, which came about from the sight of <s>Lalitā</s>;
As in <s>Lalita-mādhava</s>, regarding <s>Hari</s>'s seed of love. || 80 ||
<s>Abhūtāharaṇa</s> (fabricated assertion), <s>mārga</s> (disclosure), <s>rūpa</s> (conjecture) — in this order are the illustrations;
<s>Saṅgraha</s> (conciliation) and <s>anumāna</s> (inference), likewise <s>toṭaka</s> (invective) and <s>adhibala</s> (stratagem). || 81 ||
<s>Udvega</s> (anxiety), <s>sambhrama</s> (alarm), <s>ākṣepa</s> (casting aside) — their definitions are now stated.
Of these, <s>abhūtāharaṇa</s> (fabricated assertion) —
<s>Abhūtāharaṇa</s> is that speech which resorts to deception. || 82 ||
As in the same [play], in the fifth act —
He who was born with four arms,
causing astonishment among the people;
That best of the <s>Yadus</s>, son of <s>Śūrasuta</s>,
will marry your sister <s>Rukmiṇī</s>. || (5.9)
Here this deceptive speech is the <s>abhūtāharaṇa</s> (fabricated assertion).
Now <s>mārga</s> (disclosure) —
<s>Mārga</s> is the statement of the true meaning...
As in the same [play] —

<s>Kṛṣṇa</s> (having read the letter)
[variant reading for <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>: <s>Nārada</s>]

children.text: nikhilā śikhini nayann api sukhāni jātyāsitāpāṅgī |
children.translated_text: She who has eyes dark as the <s>jātī</s> flower, though leading all pleasures to the fire-god,
<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, dense [with love], delights only in the fragrances of <s>Vṛndāvana</s>. || (5.10)
Here, by <s>Hari</s>'s revelation of his heart's [true feelings], it is <s>mārga</s> (disclosure).
Now <s>rūpa</s> (conjecture) —
...<s>Rūpa</s> is a speech involving speculation. || 83 ||
As in the same [play] —

children.text:
kṛṣṇaḥ (sānandam) - sakhe, katham anubhūta-pūrveva kāpi śiñjita-saraṇī prasahya
mām ādrīkaroti |
[*NOTE: kṛṣṇaḥsāśaṅkam]
children.translated_text:
<s>Kṛṣṇa</s> (joyfully) — Friend, how is it that a certain tinkling sound, as if experienced before, forcefully captivates me!
[Note: <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> (with apprehension)]
Here, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s speculation upon hearing the tinkling of <s>Candrāvalī</s>'s anklets and such is <s>rūpa</s> (conjecture).
Now <s>udāharaṇa</s> (illustration) —

children.text: sotkarṣaṃ vacanaṃ yat tu tad udāharaṇaṃ matam || 84 ||
children.translated_text: A speech of praise is considered <s>udāharaṇa</s> (illustration). || 84 ||
As in the same [play] —
<s>Suparṇā</s> (observing with wonder) —
Having churned, as it were through deceit, the ocean of beauty in the guise of the milk-ocean,

children.text: gīrvāṇair udahāri hāri parito yā sāra-sampan-mayī |
children.translated_text: by the gods was brought forth that which is all-pervading and full of essence, captivating all around;
Even that <s>Lakṣmī</s>, however, does not possess the skill of creating lasting wonder for the eyes

children.text: dhatte hanta tathā na kāntibhir iyaṃ rājñaḥ kumārī yathā || (5.30)
children.translated_text: with her radiance, as does this princess of the king. || (5.30)
Here, the narration of the excellence of <s>Candrāvalī</s>'s beauty is the <s>udāharaṇa</s> (illustration).
Now <s>krama</s> (sequence) —
<s>Krama</s> is the knowledge of emotions, or the connection of contemplated meaning. || 85 ||
As in the sixth [act] —
<s>Navavṛndā</s> (aside) —
When into the pathway of her eyes, which stirred the beauty of lotuses,
came, after a long time, the garment of the slayer of <s>Kaṃsa</s>;
Even with great efforts, impossible to conceal,
alas, <s>Rādhā</s> undergoes an extraordinary and unbearable transformation! || (6.25)

children.text:
atra nava-vṛndāyā rādhāyā bhāva-jñānāt citnyamāna-hari-cihnasya rādhayā
darśanād vā kramaḥ |
children.translated_text:
Here, from <s>Navavṛndā</s>'s knowledge of <s>Rādhā</s>'s emotions, and from <s>Rādhā</s>'s
seeing the sign of <s>Hari</s> that was being contemplated, it is <s>krama</s> (sequence).
Now <s>saṅgraha</s> (conciliation) —
<s>Saṅgraha</s> is declared to be the conjunction of conciliation and gifts. || 86 ||
As in the same [play], in the fifth [act] —

<s>Bhīṣma</s> (joyfully) —
[Note: <s>Bhīṣmaka</s> (with respect)]
He who, without being asked, leading my daughter away from misfortune,
has done me a favor — <s>Jāmbavān</s>;
whose lotus feet are to be meditated upon by the minds of sages —

children.text: tvam asi yena varo duhitur varaḥ || (5.37)
children.translated_text: you are indeed the best groom for my daughter. || (5.37)
Here, by the offering of the daughter motivated by conciliation, it is <s>saṅgraha</s> (conciliation).
Now <s>anumāna</s> (inference) —
Reasoning from signs is [called] <s>anumāna</s> (inference)...
As in the same [play], in the sixth [act] —
<s>Candrāvalī</s> (in Sanskrit) —
This slender-limbed one repeatedly manifests through her bodily signs
a resemblance to those who suffer separation from the enemy of <s>Madhu</s>;

children.text: ākṛtyā śriyam api mādhavīṃ kim enāṃ
children.translated_text: Can even her afflictions, through their form, proclaim
even the beauty of <s>Mādhavī</s> [the spring creeper], even in her wretchedness? || (6.23)

Here, the inference of her being one who suffers separation from <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>,
through the sign of seeing beauty even in her wretchedness, is <s>anumāna</s> (inference).
Now <s>toṭaka</s> (invective) —
...An angry speech is <s>toṭaka</s> (invective). || 87 ||
As in the same [play], in the sixth [act] —
<s>Nārada</s> —
The lord of lions stole the best of jewels and killed your son;

children.text: vinighnante taṃ ca prabalam atha bhallūka-nṛpatiḥ |
children.translated_text: they slew him too, the mighty one, and then the king of bears;

children.text: parābhūya svairī tam api mura-vairī tava dhanaṃ
children.translated_text: Having defeated him as well, the wanton enemy of <s>Mura</s>, your wealth —

children.text: tad-āhartā pāpa tvam asi patitas tāpa-jaladhau || (6.15)
children.translated_text: that thief, O sinful one, you have fallen into an ocean of torment! || (6.15)
Here the <s>toṭaka</s> (invective) through angry speech is self-evident.
Now <s>adhibala</s> (stratagem) —
The wise declare <s>adhibala</s> to be deception through artifice. || 88 ||
As in the same [play], in the fifth [act] —
<s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s> —
The one who was trained by me in the assembly of cowherd boys
for arranging sport and play;
He did well in the enemy's fortress,
displaying his role as minister in the guise of an actor. || (5.27)
Here, the deception of others through the artifice of an actor's disguise is <s>adhibala</s> (stratagem).
Now <s>udvega</s> (anxiety) —
Fear arising from enemies, hostility, and such is called <s>udvega</s> (anxiety). || 89 ||
As in the same [play], in the sixth [act] —

children.text:
candrāvalī (janāntikam) sahi māhavi ! pekkha | eso ajja-uttassa sacca-saṃkappidā
seibimaddaṇo saccabhāmāe sondera-pūro dhīraṃ bi maṃ āndoledi | [sakhi mādhavi,
paśya | eṣa āryaputrasya satya-saṅkalpitā setu-vimardanaḥ satyabhāmāyāḥ
saundarya-pūro dhīrām api mām āndolayati |]
children.translated_text: <s>Candrāvalī</s> (aside) — O friend <s>Mādhavī</s>, look! This one, the true resolve of the noble lord, the crusher of the bridge, full of <s>Satyabhāmā</s>'s beauty, agitates even steadfast me! [In Sanskrit: O friend <s>Mādhavī</s>, look! This one, the true resolve of the noble lord, the crusher of the bridge, full of <s>Satyabhāmā</s>'s beauty, agitates even steadfast me!]
Here, from the sight of the co-wife who has appeared, <s>Candrāvalī</s>'s <s>udvega</s> (anxiety) [arises].
Now <s>sambhrama</s> (alarm) —
Apprehension arising from enemies, tigers, and such is here <s>sambhrama</s> (alarm). || 90 ||
As in the same [play], in the fifth [act] —
(Behind the curtain)

children.text: saptiḥ saptī ratha iha rathaḥ kuñjaro me
children.translated_text: A horse! A horse! A chariot here! A chariot! An elephant for me!

children.text: tūṇas tūṇo dhanur uta dhanur bhoḥ kṛpāṇī kṛpāṇī |
children.translated_text: A quiver! A quiver! A bow! Or a bow! Ho, a sword! A sword!

children.text: kā bhĪḥ kā bhīr ayam ayam ahaṃ hā tvaradhvaṃ tvaradhvaṃ
children.translated_text: What fear? What fear? Here! Here I am! Ah, make haste! Make haste!

children.text: rājñaḥ putrī bata hṛta-hṛtā kāminā vallavena ||(5.30)
children.translated_text: The king's daughter, alas, has been abducted by the cowherd lover! || (5.30)
Here the <s>sambhrama</s> (alarm) is clearly evident.
Now <s>ākṣepa</s> (casting aside) —
The throwing up of the seed of the <s>garbha</s> (development) is called <s>ākṣepa</s> (casting aside). || 91 ||
As in the same [play], in the sixth [act] —
<s>Kṛṣṇa</s> (with agitation) —
With a mind delayed in undertaking the purpose of all friends,

children.text: masṛṇita-śikho yaḥ prāptodbhūd manāg iva mārdavam |
children.translated_text: the flame [of love] whose crest was softened, had attained a slight tenderness;
But that [flame], becoming dense through the occasion of <s>Lalitā</s>'s intense affection,

children.text: punar api balād indhe rādhā-viyoga-mayaḥ śikhī || (6.43)
children.translated_text: forcefully kindles again the fire of separation from <s>Rādhā</s>. || (6.43)

children.text: asya suhṛdartha-sampādane garbhitasya punaḥ lalitā-darśanenotkṣepād ākṣepaḥ |
children.translated_text: The <s>ākṣepa</s> (casting aside) occurs because the [purpose] embedded in accomplishing the friends' goal is cast up again by the sight of <s>Lalitā</s>.
Now the <s>vimarśa-sandhi</s> (deliberation juncture) —
Where the seed, having emerged from the development, is deliberated upon
through enticement, anger, adversity and such — that is called <s>vimarśa</s> (deliberation). || 92 ||
Here the arrangement of limbs is according to the suitability of the fixed sub-plots;
as through the enticement by <s>Bakulā</s>, <s>Navavṛndā</s> and others. || 93 ||
And here the deliberation on the seed of love through the queen's suspicion and such
is clearly stated regarding <s>Rādhā</s> and <s>Mādhava</s> in <s>Lalita-mādhava</s>. || 94 ||
<s>Avavāda</s> (reproach), <s>sampheṭa</s> (quarrel), <s>vidrava</s> (scattering), <s>drava</s> (fleeing), <s>śakti</s> (power),
<s>dyuti</s> (threat), <s>prasaṅga</s> (occasion), <s>chalana</s> (deceit), <s>vyavasāya</s> (resolve), <s>virodhana</s> (opposition),
<s>prarocanā</s> (incitement), <s>vivalana</s> (disclosure), and <s>ādāna</s> (seizure) — these are thirteen. || 95 ||

Now <s>avavāda</s> (reproach) —
The proclamation of faults is <s>avavāda</s> (reproach)...
As in the same [play], in the seventh [act] —
<s>Rādhikā</s> — (with anguish)

children.text: cirād adya svapne mama vividha-yatnād upagate
children.translated_text: After a long time, today in a dream, through various efforts, when he came,
<s>Govinda</s> attained, O friend, the realm of my eyes;

children.text: gṛhītvā hā hanta tvaritam atha tasminn api rathaṃ
children.translated_text: But alas, quickly seizing a chariot even in that [dream],

children.text: kathaṃ pratyāsannaḥ sa khalu puruṣo rāja-puruṣaḥ || (7.22)
children.translated_text: how has that person, a king's man, come so near! || (7.22)
Here, from the recounting of the beloved's cruelty, it is <s>avavāda</s> (reproach).
Now <s>sampheṭa</s> (quarrel) —
<s>Sampheṭa</s> is angry speech.
As in the same [play] —
<s>Rādhikā</s> (in Sanskrit)
Let the lord of <s>Dvāravatī</s> rule over the three worlds, honored for his beauty;

children.text: kiṃ nas tena viramyatāṃ katham asau śokāgnir ujjvālyate |
children.translated_text: what is he to us? Let it cease. Why is this fire of grief kindled?
By you all, who speak with the weight of clear reasoning,
we cannot be forcibly dragged to the lotus feet of the son of <s>Vraja</s>'s king. || 7.2 ||
Here, by the concealed reproach directed at <s>Bakulā</s>, it is <s>sampheṭa</s> (quarrel).
Now <s>vidrava</s> (scattering) —
<s>Vidrava</s> is killing, binding, and such...
As in the same [play], in the eighth [act] —

children.text:
kṛṣṇaḥ - priye, yuṣmākam adbhutam ākarṇyatāṃ sāmpratam ahaṃ
sūra-saugandhikam āhariṣyan pāṇḍavena saha khāṇḍavāḍavīṃ prāviśam | tatra
mṛgān āhaṇḍino gāṇḍīvinaḥ śyenābhyāṃ nigṛhītayoḥ pakṣiṇor ekaḥ prāhety ādi |
children.translated_text: <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> — Beloved, hear now your wonderful [tale]. I, wishing to bring the <s>Saugandhika</s> [flower], entered the <s>Khāṇḍava</s> forest with the <s>Pāṇḍava</s>. There, while the wielder of <s>Gāṇḍīva</s> was hunting deer, two birds were seized by hawks — one spoke thus, and so on.
Here, through the capture of the birds and such, it is <s>vidrava</s> (scattering).
Now <s>drava</s> (fleeing) —
...<s>Drava</s> is the disrespect of elders. || 96 ||
As in the same [play] —

children.text:
mādhavī - bhaṭṭo-dārie kāsāre pasāridaṇi abbadaṃ vagīṃ samaria hasāmi |
[bhartṛ-dārike kāsāre prasārita-nija-vratāṃ bakīṃ smṛtvā hasāmi |]
children.translated_text: <s>Mādhavī</s> — O noble lady's daughter, remembering the crane with its vow spread out in the pond, I laugh constantly. [In Sanskrit: O noble lady's daughter, remembering the crane with its vow spread out in the pond, I laugh.]
Here, through the mockery of the mistress <s>Rādhā</s>, it is <s>drava</s> (fleeing/disrespect).
Now <s>śakti</s> (power) —
<s>Śakti</s> is the pacification of conflict...
As in the same [play] —

children.text:
nava-vṛndā (latāntare sthitvā) hanta katham aṅgīkṛta-rādhā-prasādhanā devīyam
upalabdhā | tad eṣa mādhavo yāvad enāṃ rādhikāṃ pratītya na pramādam
ādadhāti tāvad ahaṃ padyam ekaṃ hārītena hārayāmīti |
children.translated_text: <s>Navavṛndā</s> (standing behind the creeper) — Alas, how has this queen, who had undertaken the adornment of <s>Rādhā</s>, been discovered! So, before <s>Mādhava</s>, having recognized her as <s>Rādhikā</s>, becomes careless, I shall have <s>Hārīta</s> deliver one verse.

children.text: atra rādhātvena candrāvalī-jñānād utpannasya virodhasya śamanāt śaktiḥ |
children.translated_text: Here, from the pacification of the conflict that arose from the recognition of <s>Candrāvalī</s> as <s>Rādhā</s>, it is <s>śakti</s> (power).
Now <s>dyuti</s> (threat) —
...<s>Dyuti</s> is alarming through threatening. || 97 ||
As in the same [play] —

children.text:
rādhā (sabhayam) hanta, caṃcala caṃcarīa ciṭṭha ciṭṭha | esā līlā-kamaleṇa
tāḍemi tumaṃ dhiṭhṭhaṃ | [cañcala cañcarīka tiṣṭha tiṣṭha | eṣā līlā-kamalena
tāḍayāmi tvāṃ dhṛṣṭam |]
children.translated_text: <s>Rādhā</s> (fearfully) — Alas, fickle bee, stop, stop! I shall strike you boldly with this play-lotus! [In Sanskrit: O fickle bee, stop, stop! I shall strike you boldly with this play-lotus!]

children.text: ity atra bhramarādy-udvegena bhramaraṃ prati tarjanena ca dyutiḥ |
children.translated_text: Here, through the alarm caused by the bee and such, and through the threatening of the bee, it is <s>dyuti</s> (threat).
Now <s>prasaṅga</s> (occasion) —
<s>Prasaṅga</s> is declared to be the calming of the matter at hand.
Others say <s>prasaṅga</s> is the glorification of elders. || 98 ||
Of these, the first; as in the same [play], in the eighth [act] —

children.text: carcāṃ siñcati śoṣayaty api mitho vispardhate vāsakṛt
children.translated_text: She who anoints and also dries, and who vies with the rain-cloud

children.text: netra-dvandvam uraś ca yad-virahato bāṣpāyamāṇaṃ mama |
children.translated_text: — my pair of eyes and chest, weeping from separation from whom;
Alas, she whose festival of sight is rarer than in a hundred dreams, my beloved —

children.text: prāpyotsaṅgam atarkitaṃ mama kathaṃ sā rādhikā vartate || 8.3 ||
children.translated_text: having unexpectedly reached my lap, how does that <s>Rādhikā</s> fare? || 8.3 ||
Here, from the calming of the current suffering of separation, it is <s>prasaṅga</s> (occasion).
The second, as in the seventh [act] —
<s>Rādhā</s> (in Sanskrit) —
With a face adorned by a charming, playful flute, with eyes glancing sideways,
O innocent one, with a peacock feather on her head, her body a triple-bend posture;
In youth, keeping company, by the command of the divine sage, she is worshipped
by us — in our father's house — that deity dark as a rain-cloud. || 7.24 ||
Here, from the glorification of the beloved deity <s>Nārada</s> and of the father, it is the glorification of elders.
Now <s>chalana</s> (deceit) —
<s>Chalana</s> is declared to be the infliction of insult and such. || 99 ||
As in the eighth [act] —

children.text:
kṛṣṇaḥ - hanta kali-kaṇḍūla-tuṇḍa-mātra-sarvasve tamomayi mādhavike!
viramyatām | dvayoḥ paraṃ jetum aśakyeyaṃ candrāvalī |
children.translated_text: <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> — Alas, O <s>Mādhavikā</s>, you who are the embodiment of darkness with merely a quarrel-itching beak, whose everything is that alone — cease! Neither of you two can defeat this <s>Candrāvalī</s>!
Here, from the insult of reproaching <s>Mādhavī</s>, it is <s>chalana</s> (deceit).
Now <s>vyavasāya</s> (resolve) —
<s>Vyavasāya</s> is said to be the declaration of one's capability. || 100 ||
As in the seventh [act] —
<s>Rādhikā</s> (turning back, with bashfulness, in Sanskrit) —
O enemy of <s>Kaṃsa</s>, since there is an absence of the auspiciousness of your glance, I am now unfortunate,

children.text: bibhrāṇā hata-jīvite praṇayitāṃ nāhaṃ sakhi prāṇimi |
children.translated_text: Bearing a life that is destroyed, I do not live as your beloved, O friend.

children.text: krūreyaṃ na virodhinī yadi bhaved āśāmayī śṛṅkhalā
children.translated_text: If this cruel chain made of hope were not an obstruction,

children.text: prāṇānāṃ dhruvam arbudāny api tasya tyaktuṃ sukhenotsahe || 7.13 ||
children.translated_text: I would certainly be able to happily abandon even billions of lives for his sake. || 7.13 ||
Here, because of the general statement of the purpose of abandoning billions of lives, this is <s>vyavasāya</s> (resolve).

children.text: kaścit tu, vyavasāyas tu vijñeyaḥ pratijñā-hetu-sambhavaḥ || ity āha (SāhD 6.103) |
children.translated_text: However, some say: "<s>Vyavasāya</s> (resolve) should be understood as arising from a declaration and reason" — thus states (<s>Sāhityadarpaṇa</s> 6.103).
As in the seventh [act] of the same [play] —
He whose crest-ornament fashioned from a peacock feather gleams in his hair,
Whose necklace made of large <s>guñjā</s> berries rolls upon his neck,

children.text: veṇur vaktre racayati ruciṃ hanta cetas tato me
children.translated_text: Whose flute at his lips creates enchantment — alas, therefore my heart

children.text: rūpaṃ viśvottaram api harer nānyad aṅgīkaroti || (7.6)
children.translated_text: Does not accept any other form, even though <s>Hari's</s> form surpasses all the world. || (7.6)
Now, <s>virodhanam</s> (contradiction) —
<s>Virodhanam</s> (contradiction) is contentious speech among those who are mutually angered. || 101 ||
As in the eighth [act] —

children.text:
candrāvalī (solluṇṭha-smitam) ai loluhe āli, kīsa maṃ anāpekkhia taṃ
ṇiamahābbadaṃ tue suṭṭhu paḍiṭṭhidam | [ayi lolupe āli, kasmān mām anāpṛcchya
tan nija-mahā-vrataṃ tvayā suṣṭhu pratiṣṭhitam |]
rādhikā - dei, saraṇṇassa jaṇassa saṃrakkhaṇe akkhamāsi tahabi parihasesi | ṇūṇaṃ
īsarīṇāṃ kkhu juttaṃ edaṃ | [devi, śaraṇyasya janasya saṃrakṣaṇe akṣamāsi tathāpi
parihasasi | nūnaṃ īśvarīṇāṃ khalu yuktam etat |]
children.translated_text: <s>Candrāvalī</s> (with a haughty smile): O greedy friend, why have you, without consulting me, so well established that great vow of yours? <s>Rādhikā</s>: O queen, you are unable to protect one who seeks refuge, yet still you jest. Surely this is fitting for sovereigns.
Here, the contentious speech between <s>Candrāvalī</s> and <s>Rādhā</s>, who conceal their anger, constitutes <s>virodhanam</s> (contradiction).
<s>Prarocanā</s> (foreshadowing) occurs from indicating a future event as if it were already accomplished. || 102 ||
Now, <s>prarocanā</s> (foreshadowing) —
As in the seventh [act] of the same [play] —
Enough of lamentations! The courses of time's sequence
Are of unfathomable nature.
See, at the onset of autumn, on the banks of the lake,
The wagtails suddenly sport about! || 7.5 ||
<s>Nava-Vṛndā</s> —

children.text: ity atra kañjarīṭa-dṛṣṭāntena bhāvi-kṛṣṇa-saṅgamasya sūcanāt prarocanā |
children.translated_text: Here, through the example of the wagtails indicating the future union with <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, this is <s>prarocanā</s> (foreshadowing).
Or alternatively, in the same [play] —
<s>Rādhā</s> (in Sanskrit) —
O companion, the toil that was undergone by me in maintaining this body

children.text: sahacari parikleśo yo'bhūn mayā kila sevitaḥ |
children.translated_text: Has become fruitful, yielding great happiness,

children.text: ahaha yad imāḥ śyāma-śyāmā puro mama vallavī-
children.translated_text: For, ah! before me now flash those dark-hued rays
Of him who is the moon to the water-lily family of cowherd maidens! || 7.27 ||

children.text:
atra pratimā-sandarśanānandena bhāvi-kṛṣṇa-saṅgamanasya siddhavat sūcanāt
prarocanā |
children.translated_text: Here, through the joy of seeing the image, indicating the future union with <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> as if already accomplished, this is <s>prarocanā</s> (foreshadowing).
Now, <s>vivalanam</s> (self-praise) —
<s>Vivalanam</s> is self-praise.
As in the eighth [act] of the same [play] —

children.text:
kṛṣṇaḥ (savismayam) ko'yaṃ mādhuryeṇa mamāpi mano haran maṇi-kuḍyam
avaṣṭambya puro virājate | (punar nibhālya) hanta katham atrāham eva
pratibimbito'smi | (iti sautsukyam)
children.translated_text: <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> (with astonishment): Who is this one that steals even my mind with his sweetness, standing resplendent before me, leaning against the jeweled wall? (Looking again) Ah! How is it that I myself am reflected here! (Thus, with eagerness) —

children.text:
aparikalita-pūrvaḥ kaś camatkāra-kārī
sphurati mama garīyān eṣa mādhurya-pūraḥ |
ayam aham api hanta prekṣya yaṃ lubdha-cetāḥ
