children.translated_text: Manifests in me most magnificently — seeing which, even I, with a captivated heart, ardently desire to enjoy it, like <s>Rādhikā</s>! || 8.34 ||
Never before perceived, this flood of sweetness that causes great wonder
Here, the praising of one's own beauty through astonishment is <s>vivalanam</s> (self-praise).
Now, <s>ādānam</s> (accumulation) —
<s>Ādānam</s> (accumulation) is the gathering together of activities. || 103 ||
As in the eighth [act] of the same [play] —
<s>Navavṛndā</s> (observing <s>Rādhā</s>): Alas, alas!

children.text: āloke kamaleṣaṇasya sajalāsāre dṛśau na kṣame
children.translated_text: At the sight of the lotus-eyed one, her tear-filled eyes cannot endure,
In embrace, her arm-creeper, with exceedingly stiff limbs, has no share of strength,
Her speech is not capable of responding, choked with stammering,

children.text: vṛttiḥ kāpi babhūva saṅgamanaye vighnaḥ kuraṅgī-dṛśaḥ || 8.11 ||
children.translated_text: Some state has arisen for the doe-eyed one that is an obstacle to union, despite his long-awaited arrival. || 8.11 ||
Here, because of the gathering together of activities such as seeing <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, this is <s>ādānam</s> (accumulation).

children.text:
kaścit tu vidrava-vivalana-chalanādy atra na paṭhitvā kheda-pratiṣedha-chādanāni
paṭhanti lakṣayanti ca |
children.translated_text: However, some do not include <s>vidrava</s> (fleeing), <s>vivalana</s> (self-praise), <s>chalana</s> (deception), etc. here, but instead read and define <s>kheda</s> (fatigue), <s>pratiṣedha</s> (obstruction), and <s>chādana</s> (concealment).
Among those, <s>kheda</s> (fatigue) —
<s>Kheda</s> (fatigue) is said to be the weariness arising from mental exertion. || 104 ||
As in the seventh [act] of the same [play] —
<s>Rādhikā</s> (in Sanskrit) —
Even the direction favorable to union with <s>Hari</s> has become far from me,
Due to sorrow, even a moment has attained the duration of a great cosmic age.
The clarified butter of hope, having created a fire that burns life at every step,

children.text: balān māṃ durlīlaḥ kam iva karavai hanta śaraṇam || 7.1 ||
children.translated_text: Forcibly burns me — alas, O wicked one, to whom shall I turn for refuge? || 7.1 ||
Now, <s>pratiṣedha</s> (obstruction) —
<s>Pratiṣedha</s> (obstruction) is said to be the thwarting of a desired object. || 105 ||
As in the same [play] —

children.text:
rādhā (samīkṣya sakhedam ātmagatam) - kahaṃ iṃdīareṇa rahaṃgīe
saṃgamiṭṭhaṃ ahiṇaṃdide maccharā kalahaṃsī milidā | [kathaṃ indīvareṇa
rahaṅgyā saṅgamituṃ abhinandite matsarā kalahaṃsī militā |
children.translated_text: <s>Rādhā</s> (looking, with sorrow, aside): How has an envious <s>kalahaṃsī</s> (quarrelsome swan-maiden) come to meet, when the union with the blue lotus in the secluded place was being welcomed!
Here, the thwarting of union with <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> due to the arrival of the rival is <s>pratiṣedha</s> (obstruction).
Now, <s>chādanam</s> (concealment) —
<s>Chādanam</s> (concealment) is considered to be the endurance of insult and the like for the sake of one's purpose.

children.text: yathā saptame nava-vṛndā (praviśya) sakhi, mā viṣādaṃ kṛthāḥ paśya -
children.translated_text: As in the seventh [act], <s>Nava-Vṛndā</s> (entering): Friend, do not despair! See —
Falling at the feet and clinging to the <s>badarī</s> (jujube) tree,
The <s>mādhavī</s> (spring creeper) finds her beloved mango tree.
A virtuous woman, with her mind fixed on union with her lord,
Does not regard the torment of being under another's power. || (7.3)
This is clearly <s>chādanam</s> (concealment).
Now, the <s>nirvahaṇa-sandhi</s> (concluding juncture) —
That in which the elements of the opening juncture and others, connected with the seed, are scattered about
And come to their great purpose — that is called <s>nirvahaṇa</s> (conclusion). || 107 ||
Here, from the coming together of the limbs, plot, fruit, and arrival,
And from the attainment by all the maidens such as <s>Rādhā</s> and others, || 108 ||
The festivity of marriage and so forth is declared, as in <s>Lalita-Mādhava</s>.
<s>Sandhi</s> (juncture), <s>virodha</s> (conflict), <s>grathana</s> (weaving), <s>nirṇaya</s> (resolution), <s>paribhāṣaṇa</s> (dialogue), || 109 ||
<s>Prasāda</s> (grace), <s>ānanda</s> (bliss), <s>samaya</s> (occasion), <s>kṛti</s> (achievement), <s>bhāṣa</s> (speech), and <s>upagūhana</s> (embrace),
<s>Pūrvabhāva</s> (prior state), <s>upasaṃhāra</s> (conclusion), and <s>praśasti</s> (eulogy) — thus say the wise. || 110 ||

children.text:
iti nirvahaṇasyāṅgāny uktāny asya caturdaśa |
tatra sandhiḥ -
children.translated_text: Thus the fourteen limbs of the <s>nirvahaṇa</s> (conclusion) have been stated. Among those, <s>sandhi</s> (juncture) —
<s>Sandhi</s> (juncture) is the approach of the seed...
As in the ninth act of the same [play] —
O auspicious one, your lips conceal the fragrance of nectar's sweetness,
Your face has the fragrance of a lotus, your words surpass the praise of the <s>kokila's</s> cooing,
Your lap is cool as sandalwood, this body of yours is the treasury of all beauty —

children.text: tvām āsādya mamedam indriya-kulaṃ rādhe muhur modate || (9.9)
children.translated_text: Having attained you, O <s>Rādhā</s>, this entire host of my senses rejoices again and again! || (9.9)
Here, from the approach of the seed of love, this is <s>sandhi</s> (juncture).
Now, <s>virodha</s> (conflict) —
... <s>Virodha</s> (conflict) is the pursuit of one's purpose. || 111 ||
As in the ninth act of the same [play], <s>Nava-Vṛndā</s> —
The hero of the <s>Madhus</s>, seeing the daughter of <s>Kuṇḍineśvara</s>
Bereft of <s>Mādhavī</s>,
Delighting her with brilliant and graceful sports,
Said with a face radiant with playful laughter — || (9.7)
"Having been requested by <s>Brahmā</s>, for the sake of seeing the world
Named <s>Satya</s>, I shall depart, O goddess — let permission be granted for that." || (9.8)
Here, from the impediment to the purpose of union with <s>Rādhā</s>, this is <s>virodha</s> (conflict).
Now, <s>grathanam</s> (weaving) —
<s>Grathanam</s> (weaving) is the introduction of a good [subject]...
As in the same [play], <s>Rādhikā</s> (seeing <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) —
When a small fish desires merely a handful of water,
A fresh rain-cloud of its own accord rains down streams upon it. || 9.19
[When a small fish desires merely a handful of water,
A fresh rain-cloud of its own accord rains down streams upon it.]

children.text: atra punaḥ sahasā kṛṣṇa-darśana-rūpasya sad-arthasyopakṣepād grathanam |
children.translated_text: Here, from the sudden introduction of the good subject of seeing <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> again, this is <s>grathanam</s> (weaving).
Now, <s>nirṇaya</s> (resolution) —
<s>Nirṇaya</s> (resolution) is indeed the statement of what has been experienced. || 112 ||
As in the same [play], <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> —
O <s>Rādhe</s>, do you remember those autumn nights
When time passed like a moment for those who had come together,
With fresh amorous sports in the pleasure groves,

children.text: smarasi kim iva tāsāṃ śāradīnāṃ kṣapāṇām || (9.47)
children.translated_text: Their modesty abandoned through the fullness of their satisfaction? || (9.47)
Here, the <s>nirṇaya</s> (resolution) is evident.
Now, <s>paribhāṣaṇam</s> (dialogue) —
<s>Paribhāṣā</s> (dialogue) may be mutual conversation or mutual reproach. || 113 ||
Of these, the first, as in the same [play] —

children.text: madhumaṅgalaḥ -bhodi kiṃ ti āadāsi? [bhavati kim ity āgatāsi?]
children.translated_text: <s>Madhumaṅgala</s>: Lady, why have you come?

children.text:
sukaṇṭhī - imassa paṇhottarassa sadikkhaṃ aṇṇaṃ bi mahuraṃ suṇidum | [asya
praśnottarasya sadṛkṣam anyad api madhuraṃ śrotum |]
children.translated_text: <s>Sukaṇṭhī</s>: To hear something else as sweet as the answer to this question.

children.text:
madhumaṅgalaḥ -bhodi paṇṇottaraṃ bi tue suṇidam? [bhavati praśnottaram api
tvayā śrutam]
children.translated_text: <s>Madhumaṅgala</s>: Lady, have you also heard the question and answer?

children.text: sukaṇṭhī - ṇa keaṇaṃ idaṃ jjeba | [na kevalam idam eva |]
children.translated_text: <s>Sukaṇṭhī</s>: Not only this much.
<s>Madhumaṅgala</s>: What else?

children.text:
sukaṇṭhī - jā kiṃ pi diṭhṭhaṃ taṃ gadua deie ṇivedissaṃ | [yat kim api dṛṣṭaṃ tad
gatvā devyai nivedayiṣyāmi |]
children.translated_text: <s>Sukaṇṭhī</s>: Whatever I have seen, I shall go and report to the queen.

children.text: atra vidūṣaka-sukaṇṭhyor mitho jalpaḥ | dvitīyo yathā tatraiva -
children.translated_text: Here is the mutual conversation between the <s>vidūṣaka</s> (jester) and <s>Sukaṇṭhī</s>. The second, as in the same [play] —
<s>Madhumaṅgala</s> — (in Sanskrit)

children.text: asi viṣakaṇṭhī-kaṭhine kim iti sukaṇṭhīti bhaṇyate ceṭi |
children.translated_text: Why are you, who are harsh like <s>Viṣakaṇṭhī</s> (poison-throated), called <s>Sukaṇṭhī</s> (sweet-throated), O maidservant?

children.text: athavā kā mama śastā bhadrety abhidhīyate viṣṭiḥ || 9.21
children.translated_text: Or rather, what praise is there for me? The word 'auspicious' is applied to forced labor! || 9.21
Here, from the fault-finding of <s>Sukaṇṭhī</s>, this is <s>parivāda</s> (reproach).
Now, <s>prasāda</s> (grace) —
<s>Prasāda</s> (grace) is the satisfaction that arises from devoted service and the like. || 114 ||
As in the ninth [act] —

children.text:
kṛṣṇaḥ (saharṣam) sukaṇṭhike! bāḍham asminn arthe duṣkaras te mayā
niṣkrayaḥ |
children.translated_text: <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> (with delight): O <s>Sukaṇṭhikā</s>! Indeed, in this matter the recompense for your service is difficult for me to repay.
Here, <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa's</s> grace is clearly evident.
Now, <s>ānanda</s> (bliss) —
<s>Ānanda</s> (bliss) is the attainment of the desired object...
As in the tenth [act] of the same [play] —
From both her eyes and from her pair of breasts,
With streams of tears and milk falling,
Ah! The mistress of the cowherd king's household
Lovingly anoints her own son! || (10.14) ||
Here is the <s>ānanda</s> (bliss) of <s>Yaśodā</s>.
Or alternatively, in the same [play] —

children.text:
kṛṣṇaḥ (sānandam) cireṇādya gokula-vāsinām ivātmānam abhimanyamānaḥ
pramoda-mugdho'smi |
children.translated_text: <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> (joyfully): After a long time, today, considering myself as belonging to the residents of <s>Gokula</s>, I am bewildered with delight!
Here is the <s>ānanda</s> (bliss) of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>.
Now, <s>samaya</s> (occasion) —
<s>Samaya</s> (occasion) is the diminution of sorrow. || 115 ||
As in the tenth [act] of the same [play] —

children.text:
rādhikā (mukhād añcalam apāsya, savikrośam) hā hā kadhaṃ piasahī me lalidā |
hā kadhaṃ baccalā bhaavadī | hā kadhaṃ ajjiā muharā | [hā hā kathaṃ priyasakhī
me lalitā | hā kathaṃ vatsahā bhagavatī | hā kathaṃ āryā mukharā |] (ity ānandena
ghūrṇantī bhūmau skhalati |)
children.translated_text: <s>Rādhikā</s> (removing the veil from her face, with a cry): Alas, alas! Where is my dear friend <s>Lalitā</s>? Alas, where is dear <s>Bhagavatī</s>? Alas, where is revered <s>Mukharā</s>? (Thus, whirling with joy, she stumbles to the ground.)
Here, from seeing her friends, there is the diminution of <s>Rādhā's</s> sorrow.
Now, <s>kṛti</s> (achievement) — the steadiness of one who has obtained the desired object...
As in the same [play], <s>Candrāvalī</s> (aside) —

children.text:
bhaavadi bahiṇīe karaṃ geṇhiduṃ maha baaṇeṇa abbhatthīadu... ajja-utto |
[bhagavati bhaginyāḥ karaṃ grahītuṃ mama vacanena abhyarthyatām āryaputraḥ |]
children.translated_text: "O revered lady, let the noble lord be requested by my words to accept the hand of his sister."

children.text:
atra yaśodādi-samāgamāl labdhyasya rādhikā-rūpārthasya candrāvalī-prārthanena
sthairya-kṛtiḥ |
children.translated_text: Here, through <s>Candrāvalī's</s> request, the steadiness regarding the object in the form of <s>Rādhikā</s>, obtained through the gathering of <s>Yaśodā</s> and others, constitutes <s>kṛti</s> (achievement).
Now, <s>bhāṣaṇam</s> (speech) —
The attainment of honor and the like is <s>bhāṣaṇam</s> (speech). || 116 ||
As in the same [play] —
(The two sisters, placing <s>Paurṇamāsī</s> between them, bow to the chief of the cowherds.)

children.text: nandaḥ - vatse, parasparasya prāṇādhikyaṃ bhajantyau saubhāgyavatyau bhūyāsam |
children.translated_text: <s>Nanda</s>: O daughters, may you be blessed, cherishing supreme love for each other!
Here, from the attainment of honor through <s>Nanda's</s> blessing, this is <s>bhāṣaṇam</s> (speech).
Now, <s>upagūhanam</s> (embrace) —
<s>Upagūhanam</s> (embrace) is said to be the attainment of a wondrous object. || 117 ||

children.text:
yatha tatraiva -
rādhā (sarvāsāṃ pādān abhivādya sotkaṇṭham) -- kusaliṇī kiṃ me bahiṇī
candāalī | [kuśalinī kiṃ me bhaginī candrāvalī |]
children.translated_text:
As in the same [play] —
<s>Rādhā</s> (bowing at the feet of all, with longing) — Is my sister <s>Candrāvalī</s> well? [Sanskrit rendering of the Prakrit]

children.text:
candrāvalī (gāḍhaṃ pariṣvajya) - bahiṇī esāmhi dujjaṇī-hata-candāaliā | [bhaginī,
eṣāsmi durjanī hata-candrāvalikā |] (iti roditi)
children.translated_text: <s>Candrāvalī</s> (embracing tightly) — Sister, here I am, <s>Candrāvalī</s>, struck down by the wicked! [Sanskrit rendering of the Prakrit] (thus she weeps)

children.text:
rādhikā (sānandaṃ sasambhramaṃ pādayoḥ patantī) haddhi haddhi, biḍambidahmi
hada-debbeṇa | [hā dhik! hā dhik!, viḍambitāsmi hata-daivena |]
children.translated_text: <s>Rādhikā</s> (falling at her feet with joy and agitation) — Alas, alas! I am mocked by cruel fate! [Sanskrit rendering of the Prakrit]
Here, the attainment of the wondrous object — namely the mutual embrace and such of the two sisters who had never seen each other before — constitutes <s>upagūhanam</s> (embrace).
Now, <s>pūrva-bhāva</s> (preliminary sentiment) —
The association with the principal objective is called <s>pūrva-bhāva</s> (preliminary sentiment). || 118 ||
As in the same [play] —

children.text:
paurṇamāsī - yaśodā-mātaḥ, upasthito'yaṃ sarvo'bhiṣeka-sambhāraḥ | tad
alaṅkriyatāṃ prathamaṃ rādhayā saha parva-vedī tataḥ krameṇa kumārībhiś ca |
children.translated_text: <s>Paurṇamāsī</s> — O mother <s>Yaśodā</s>, all the requisites for the consecration are ready. So first let the ceremonial platform be adorned with <s>Rādhā</s>, and then in order with the other maidens as well.

children.text:
atra mukhya-kāryasya rādhā-mādhavayoḥ pariṇaya-mahotsavasya saṃsargāt
pūrva-bhāvaḥ | kecit pūrva-vākyaṃ kecit pūrva-bhāṣām iti paṭhanto lakṣayanti
(SāhD 6.113) - pūrva-vākyaṃ tu vijñeyaṃ yathoktārthopadarśanam | yathā tatraiva
(nepathye) -
children.translated_text: Here, because of the association with the principal objective — the great wedding festival of <s>Rādhā</s> and <s>Mādhava</s> — it is <s>pūrva-bhāva</s>. Some read <s>pūrva-vākya</s> (prior statement), others <s>pūrva-bhāṣā</s> (prior speech), and define it (<s>Sāhitya-darpaṇa</s> 6.113) — <s>pūrva-vākya</s> is to be known as the demonstration of what was previously stated. As in the same [play] (offstage) —
With the permissions for the wedding rites of <s>Rādhā</s>,

children.text: svayaṃ devyā tasmin pitur iha nibandhe muditayā |
children.translated_text: joyfully granted by the goddess herself in that bond of her father,

children.text: kumārīṇāṃ tāsām ayam upanayan ṣoḍaśa kṛtī
children.translated_text: this accomplished one, leading those sixteen
thousand maidens, smiling, <s>Garuḍa</s> enters, enriched by hundreds. || (10.31)

children.text:
atra pūrvaṃ kṛṣṇena tṛtīyāṅke yad uktaṃ etās tūrṇaṃ nayata kiyatīr ity ādinā
punaḥ svayaṃ gamanaṃ tasyaivopadarśanam |
children.translated_text: Here, what was previously said by <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> in the third act with the words 'Take these quickly, however many' — the demonstration of that same [promise] through his own going again.
Now, <s>upasaṃhāra</s> (conclusion) —
<s>Upasaṃhāra</s> (conclusion) is characterized by the fulfillment of all desires, marking the attainment of the goal. || 119 ||
As in the tenth [act] of the same [play] —

children.text:
kṛṣṇaḥ (sarvam abhinandya janāntikam) prāṇeśvari rādhe prārthayasva kim ataḥ
paraṃ te priyaṃ karavāṇi | (ity ārabhya)
children.translated_text: <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> (applauding everything, in private): O <s>Rādhā</s>, mistress of my life! Ask — what more dear can I do for you beyond this? (and so forth)
<s>Rādhikā</s> (joyfully, in Sanskrit) —
Those friends have been reunited, made delightful by naturally sweet love,

children.text: yāmī me samagaṃs tu saṃstavavatī śvaśrūś ca goṣṭheśvarī |
children.translated_text: my <s>Yāmī</s> (the night) has come together with me, and the praiseworthy mother-in-law, the queen of the cowherds.
This joyful union with you in the bower-abode of <s>Vṛndāraṇya</s>

children.text: saṃvṛttaḥ kim ataḥ paraṃ priyataraṃ kartavyam atrāsmi me || (10.36) ||
children.translated_text: has come about — what more dear than this remains to be done? Here I am content. || (10.36) ||
Here the <s>upasaṃhāra</s> (conclusion) is quite evident.
Now, <s>praśasti</s> (benediction) —
A proper invocation of auspiciousness is called <s>praśasti</s> (benediction). || 120 ||
As in the same [play] —
Nevertheless, let this be —
May those of steady intellect who for long place their hopes solely in you,
who would take up residence in the deeply sweet city of <s>Mathurā</s>,
bearing the friendship of the lord of <s>Gokula</s> in the age of youth —
may you certainly come within the range of their eyes! || 10.37 ||

Here, because of the invocation of auspiciousness in the form of attaining <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> within the sight of those who have made their dwelling in lovely <s>Mathurā</s>, it is <s>praśasti</s> (benediction).

children.text: pañcānām eva sandhīnāṃ catuṣaṣṭiḥ kramād iha |
children.translated_text: Of the five <s>sandhis</s> (junctures) alone, sixty-four in sequence here
are the limbs that have been enumerated by me properly in <s>Lalita-Mādhava</s>. || 121 ||
Through the understanding of <s>rasa</s> (aesthetic sentiment) and <s>bhāva</s> (emotion), and considering the purpose,

children.text: sāphalyaṃ kāryam aṅgānām ity ācāryāḥ pracakṣate || 122 ||
children.translated_text: the fruitful application of the limbs should be made — thus the teachers declare. || 122 ||

children.text: keṣāṃcid eṣām aṅgānāṃ vaiphalyaṃ kecid ūcire |
children.translated_text: Some have stated that certain of these limbs are fruitless,
such as the author of the <s>Daśarūpaka</s> and others — but that is not accepted by all. || 123 ||
This order of the limbs in the <s>mukha</s> and other <s>sandhis</s> is not insisted upon,
since the earlier authorities disregarded order, and in the exemplary works too there is deviation. || 124 ||
The protagonist or the antagonist should accomplish these limbs;
in their absence, the <s>patākā</s> (subsidiary) characters, and in their absence, others. || 125 ||
Now, the <s>sandhy-antarāṇi</s> (sub-junctures) —
In the <s>mukha</s> and other <s>sandhis</s>, to prevent the slackening of the limbs,
<s>sandhy-antarāṇi</s> (sub-junctures) should always be employed — and they are twenty-one in number. || 126 ||
<s>Sāma</s> (conciliation), <s>dāna</s> (gift), <s>bheda</s> (division), <s>daṇḍa</s> (punishment), <s>pratyutpanna-mati</s> (presence of mind), <s>vadha</s> (killing),

children.text: gotra-skhalitam ojaś ca dhīḥ krodhaḥ sāhasaṃ bhayam || 127 ||
children.translated_text: <s>gotra-skhalita</s> (slip of name), <s>ojas</s> (vigor), <s>dhī</s> (wit), <s>krodha</s> (anger), <s>sāhasa</s> (daring), <s>bhaya</s> (fear), || 127 ||

children.text: māyā ca saṃvṛtir bhrāntir dūtyaṃ hetv-avadhāraṇam |
children.translated_text: <s>māyā</s> (illusion), <s>saṃvṛti</s> (concealment), <s>bhrānti</s> (delusion), <s>dūtya</s> (messenger activity), <s>hetv-avadhāraṇa</s> (ascertainment of cause),

children.text: svapna-lekhau madaś citram eṣāṃ lakṣaṇam ucyate || 128 ||
children.translated_text: <s>svapna</s> (dream), <s>lekha</s> (letter), <s>mada</s> (intoxication), and <s>citra</s> (wonder) — the definitions of these are now stated. || 128 ||
Of these, <s>sāma</s> (conciliation) —
<s>Sāma</s> is affectionate speech that reveals compliance with oneself. || 129 ||
As in <s>Lalita-Mādhava</s>, in the tenth act —
<s>Kṛṣṇa</s> — Beloved, do not speak thus —
Let there be beautiful-browed women whose playful, rolling sidelong glances create sport;

children.text: svasti syān madirekṣaṇe kṣaṇam api tvām antarā me kutaḥ |
children.translated_text: may there be well-being for the wine-eyed one — but without you, even for a moment, how could there be any for me?
Even when the moon, surrounded by a cluster of stars, is embraced through the grace of <s>Soma</s>,

children.text: nākāśe vṛṣabhānujāṃ śriyam ṛte niṣpadyate svaś-chaṭā || (10.10)
children.translated_text: without the splendor of the daughter of <s>Vṛṣabhānu</s>, no moonbeam manifests in the sky. || (10.10)
Now, <s>dāna</s> (gift) —
<s>Dāna</s> (gift) is said by the wise to be the offering of a beloved object. || 130 ||

children.text:
yathā tatraiva aṣṭame -
mādhavī - bhaṭṭi-dārie sahattheṇa tue gaṃṭhidā esā sūrasoaṃdhia-mālā |

children.translated_text: Noble daughter of my lord, this garland of <s>sūra-saugandhika</s> flowers was strung by your own hand!

As in the eighth [act] of the same [play] —
<s>Mādhavī</s> — O daughter of my lord, this garland of <s>sūra-saugandhika</s> flowers was strung by your own hand! [Sanskrit rendering of the Prakrit] 21

children.text:
candrāvalī (mālām ādāya) ajja-utta, esā kautthuhassa sahabāsiṇī hodu |
[ārya-putra, eṣā kaustubhasya saha-vāsinī bhavatu |] (iti vakṣasi vinyasyati |) 22
children.translated_text: <s>Candrāvalī</s> (taking the garland) — Noble lord, let this be the companion of the <s>Kaustubha</s> gem! [Sanskrit rendering of the Prakrit] (thus she places it on his chest.) 22
Now, <s>bheda</s> (division) —
<s>Bheda</s> (division) is the creation of a rift among friends through deceitful speech. || 131 ||
As in the fourth [act] —

children.text:
jaṭilā - (apavārya, sālīka-sneham) ayi bacche, sadā maṃ palohia lalidā ahisāredi tti
maha puttassa purado bahūḍiā aliaṃ jebba tumaṃ sandūsedi | tā kitti lāhavaṃ sahesi |
[ayi vatse, sadā māṃ pralobhya lalitā abhisārayati iti mama putrasya purato
vadhūṭikālīkam eva tvāṃ dūṣayati | tat kim iti lāghavaṃ sahase? |] 105
children.translated_text: <s>Jaṭilā</s> — (aside, with feigned affection) O child, <s>Lalitā</s> always lures me and leads me on secret rendezvous — thus she falsely defames you, the bride, before my son. So why do you endure such disgrace? [Sanskrit rendering of the Prakrit] 105

children.text: atra jaṭilayā kapaṭena lalitāyā bhedaḥ kṛtaḥ |
children.translated_text: Here, <s>Jaṭilā</s> has created a rift in <s>Lalitā</s> through deceit.
Now, <s>daṇḍa</s> (punishment) —

children.text: daṇḍas tv avinayādīnāṃ dṛṣṭyā śrutyā ca tarjanam || 132 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Daṇḍa</s> (punishment) is the threatening of transgressions and the like, whether seen or heard. || 132 ||
As in the second [act] —
<s>Kṛṣṇa</s> (with indignation) — Hey, hey, wicked one!

children.text: rādhāparādhini muhus tvayi yan na śastaṃ
children.translated_text: That which I could not do to you, an offender against <s>Rādhā</s>, repeatedly —

children.text: śakṣyāmi kartum akhilāṃ gurur eṣa khedaḥ |
children.translated_text: all this is my great vexation.
This night of your release-time, lawless,
rushes toward you with all its limbs — alas, what shall I do? || 2.28 ||
Here the threatening of <s>Śaṅkhacūḍa</s> constitutes <s>daṇḍa</s> (punishment).
Now, <s>pratyutpanna-mati</s> (presence of mind) —
Spontaneous wit is considered <s>pratyutpanna-mati</s> (presence of mind). || 133 ||
As in the second [act] of the same [play] —

children.text:
lalitā - kundalade, assudapubbā esā kīrisī ricā bahueṇa paḍijjai | [kundalate,
aśruta-pūrvaiṣā kīdṛśī ṛg baḍukena paṭhyate |]
children.translated_text: <s>Lalitā</s> — <s>Kundalatā</s>, what kind of unprecedented Vedic verse is this young boy reciting? [Sanskrit rendering of the Prakrit]

children.text:
madhumaṅgalaḥ (sāṭṭahāsam) buṭṭie, āhīrīmuddhiā tumaṃ rī rī gīdaṃ ccea
jāṇāsi | amhaa vedassa tumaṃ kāsi | tā suṇāhi kosum esvaīe sāhāe taia vaggassa
lalaṇāsuhaarī ricā esā | [vṛddhe, ābhīrī-mugdhikā tvam, rī rī gītam eva jānāsi |
asmad-vedasya tvaṃ kāsi | tat śṛṇu kausumeṣavyāḥ śākhāyās tṛtīya-vargasya
lalanāśubhakarī ṛg eṣā |]
children.translated_text: <s>Madhumaṅgala</s> (with a loud laugh) — Old woman, you ignorant cowherd girl, you only know the 'rī rī' song! What do you know of our Veda? So listen — this is a verse from the third chapter of the branch of <s>Kusumēśvarī</s>, bringing fortune to women! [Sanskrit rendering of the Prakrit]
Here is the presence of mind of <s>Madhumaṅgala</s>.
Now, <s>vadha</s> (killing) —
<s>Vadha</s> (killing) is the act of threatening the life of an assailant. || 134 ||
As in the second [act] — (offstage)
This sinful one, with evil intentions fixed,
was swiftly struck with a fist — alas!
By the lotus-eyed one, playfully
was he punished, [losing] his entire life-wealth. || (2.30)
Now, <s>gotra-skhalita</s> (slip of name) —
<s>Gotra-skhalita</s> is the erroneous utterance of a different name. || 135 ||
As in the seventh [act] —
<s>Candrāvalī</s> — <s>Kaṇha</s>— (breaking off mid-word, with embarrassment) Noble lord!

children.text:
kṛṣṇaḥ (sānanda-smitam) priye! diṣṭyā sudhādhārāṃ pāyito'smi | tad alam
āryaputreti kūpāmbunā |
children.translated_text: <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> (with a joyful smile) — Beloved! By good fortune I have been made to drink a stream of nectar! So enough with the well-water of 'noble lord'!
Here, because of <s>Candrāvalī</s>'s transgression of propriety, it is <s>gotra-skhalita</s> (slip of name).
Now, <s>ojas</s> (vigor) —
<s>Ojas</s> (vigor) is a verbal declaration that reveals one's own power. || 136 ||
As in the fifth [act] —

children.text:
suparṇaḥ - deva bāḍham ātapatra-phaṇāpaṭalīla-dhīyasaḥ kiṅkarasyāsya
garutmataḥ sakṛt-pakṣa-vikṣepa-kelaye'pi na paryāptim eṣyati, dūre viśrāmyatu
sakhā me sudarśanaḥ kalpānta-kuśalaḥ |
children.translated_text: <s>Suparṇa</s> (<s>Garuḍa</s>) — O Lord, indeed! For a mere playful flap of a wing by this servant <s>Garutmat</s>, who holds the parasol-canopy as sport, even that would not be sufficient [to exhaust his power]. Let my friend <s>Sudarśana</s>, skilled in cosmic dissolution, rest far away.
Here, because <s>Garuḍa</s> reveals his own power, it is <s>ojas</s> (vigor).
Now, <s>dhī</s> (wit) —
Deliberation leading to the accomplishment of the desired goal is called <s>dhī</s> (wit). || 137 ||
As in the second [act] —

children.text:
rādhikā - kundalade! ppasīda anukampehi | ajja sā kkhu sāmalā komudī jeṇa
pīdā | tā jebba puṇṇavantaṃ appaṇo vāmaloaṇaṃcalaṃ ettha khiṇṇe manda-bhāiṇi
jaṇe khaṇaṃ appehi | [kundalate! prasīda anukampaya | adya sā khalu śyāmalā
kaumudī yena pītā | tam eva puṇyavantam ātmano vāmalocanāñcalam etasmin

children.translated_text: [...upon this afflicted, ill-fated person, for just a moment, bestow it.] 38

<s>Rādhikā</s> — <s>Kundalatā</s>! Please, have compassion! Today that dark moonlight has been drunk by someone. So please bestow upon this afflicted, ill-fated person, for just a moment, the blessed corner of your left eye. [Sanskrit rendering of the Prakrit]

children.text:
kundalatā - (sāsūyam ivālokya) alaṃ para-purise giñcantīhiṃ tumhehiṃ
saṃbhāsaṇeṇa (iti dhāvantī jaṭilām upetya) ajje! kahaṃ paḍhamaṃ brahmaṇaṃ ṇa
maggesi, jo kkhu suraṃ puābaissadi | [alaṃ para-puruṣe gṛdhyantībhir yuṣmābhiḥ
sambhāṣaṇena | ārye kathaṃ prathamaṃ brāhmaṇaṃ na mṛgayase, yaḥ khalu sūryaṃ

children.translated_text: [...who will conduct the worship of the sun?] 39

<s>Kundalatā</s> — (looking with seeming jealousy) Enough of conversation with you who lust after another's man! (thus, running to approach <s>Jaṭilā</s>) Noble lady! Why do you not first seek a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> who will conduct the worship of the sun? [Sanskrit rendering of the Prakrit]

children.text:
jaṭilā - bacche, saccaṃ kahesi | tā pasīda | āṇehi ekkaṃ biakkhaṇaṃ bamhaṇam |
[vatse, satyaṃ kathayasi | tasmāt prasīda | ānayaikaṃ vicakṣaṇaṃ brāhmaṇam |] 40
children.translated_text: <s>Jaṭilā</s> — Child, you speak the truth. So please, bring one wise <s>brāhmaṇa</s>. [Sanskrit rendering of the Prakrit] 40

children.text:
atra rādhikotkaṇṭhātiśaya-darśanena jaṭilā-samaksam eva vipraveśena
kṛṣṇa-praveśa-cintanaṃ kundalatāyāḥ dhīḥ |
children.translated_text: Here, <s>Kundalatā</s>'s planning to bring <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> in disguise as a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> right before <s>Jaṭilā</s>'s eyes, having seen <s>Rādhikā</s>'s extreme longing, constitutes <s>dhī</s> (wit).
Now, <s>krodha</s> (anger) —
<s>Krodha</s> (anger) is the blazing of the mind upon seeing an offense and the like. || 138 ||
In the pleasure-groves, freshly sprouted and lush, the <s>śephālikā</s> flowers blossom far and wide;

children.text: śephālīnāṃ skhalati kusume hanta caskhāla bālā |
children.translated_text: on the blossoms of <s>śephālikā</s>, alas, the young girl stumbled!
In the grove of <s>kuvalaya</s> lotuses, with eyes closed, she was apparently dozing —

children.text: vācyaṃ kiṃ vā param upahasīr mā praṇāma-cchalena || (2.7)
children.translated_text: what more is there to say? Or are you mocking her? Do not do so under the pretext of bowing! || (2.7)
As in the second [act] (offstage) —
Here is the anger of <s>Padmā</s>'s friends toward <s>Hari</s>.
Now, <s>sāhasa</s> (daring) —
An act performed without regard for one's own life is <s>sāhasa</s> (daring). || 139 ||
As in the tenth [act] —

children.text:
rādhikā (sakhedam ātmagatam) sāhu re kīra sāhu | bāṭṭhaṃ aṇuggahidamhi, tā
dāṇiṃ dullahā-hiṭṭhadāṇadacchiṇaṃ titthavaraṃ kāliadehaṃ ppavisiya appāṇaṃ
sappāṇaṃ turiaṃ ubahirassam | [sādhu re kīra sādhu | bāḍhaṃ anugṛhītāsmi, tad
idānīṃ durlabhābhīṣṭha-dāna-dakṣiṇaṃ tīrtha-varaṃ kāliya-hradaṃ praviśya

children.translated_text: [...I shall quickly offer myself to the serpents.] 98

<s>Rādhikā</s> (with sorrow, aside) — Well done, O parrot, well done! Indeed I am favored. So now, as an offering of gratitude for the gift of the unattainable desire, I shall quickly enter the sacred pool of <s>Kāliya</s> and offer myself, together with my life-breaths, to the serpents! [Sanskrit rendering of the Prakrit]
Here, <s>Rādhā</s>'s entering the pool of <s>Kāliya</s> constitutes <s>sāhasa</s> (daring).
Now, <s>bhaya</s> (fear) —
<s>Bhaya</s> (fear) is sudden terror...
As in the ninth [act], at the viewing of the painting —
<s>Madhumaṅgala</s> — This is <s>Śaṅkhacūḍa</s>! [Sanskrit rendering of the Prakrit]
<s>Rādhā</s> (fearfully): Save me, save me! (Thus she embraces <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>.)
Here, the terror of <s>Rādhā</s> due to the incident with <s>Śaṅkhacūḍa</s> constitutes <s>bhaya</s> (fear).
Now, <s>māyā</s> (deception) —
... <s>Māyā</s> (deception) is a fraudulent contrivance. || 140 ||
As in the fourth [act] —

children.text: vṛndā (sānandam) kiṃ nāma rādhā-sakhīnāṃ dhiyām akṣuṇṇaṃ paśya paśya |
children.translated_text: <s>Vṛndā</s> (joyfully): How undiminished is the intelligence of <s>Rādhā's</s> friends! See, see!
That same body of <s>Abhimanyu</s>, with a dull luster like the brother of an evening cloud,

children.text: vaktraṃ hanta tad eva kharvaṭa-ghaṭī-ghoṇaṃ vigāḍhekṣaṇam |
children.translated_text: That same face, alas, with deeply sunken eyes like the mouth of a village pot,

children.text: vyastā saiva gatiḥ karīra-kusuma-cchāyaṃ tad evāmbaraṃ
children.translated_text: That same awkward gait, that same garment with the hue of <s>karīra</s> flowers —

children.text: mudrā kāpi tathāpy asau piśunayaty asya svarūpa-cchaṭām || (4.33)
children.translated_text: Yet despite all this, some mark betrays the radiance of his true form! || (4.33)
Now, <s>saṃvṛtti</s> (concealment) —

children.text: saṃvṛttiḥ svayam uktasya svayam ācchādanā bhavet || 141 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Saṃvṛtti</s> (concealment) is the covering up by oneself of what one has oneself said. || 141 ||
As in the ninth [act] —

children.text:
kṛṣṇaḥ (vṛndām avalokya) satyabhāmā, mayi katham (ity ardhokteḥ | navavṛndā
dṛśaṃ kūṇayati |)
children.translated_text: <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> (looking at <s>Vṛndā</s>): <s>Satyabhāmā</s>, how is it that towards me — (thus half-spoken; <s>Navavṛndā</s> narrows her eyes.)
<s>Candrāvalī</s> (sorrowfully, in a low voice): The gravity of love is understood.

children.text:
kṛṣṇaḥ (vibhāvya, svagatam) hanta, katham asau devī | bhavatu saṃvarītuṃ
prayatiṣye | (prakāśam)
children.translated_text: <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> (realizing, aside): Alas, how is that queen here! Very well, I shall try to conceal it. (Aloud:)

children.text: satī katham asau bhāmā devī nādya prasīdati |
children.translated_text: How is it that the virtuous and illustrious queen is not pleased today?

children.text: nidānam avidaṃ sadyaḥ khidyate hṛdayaṃ mama || (9.59)
children.translated_text: Not knowing the cause, my heart is immediately distressed. || (9.59)

children.text:
atra svayam uktasya satyabhāmety asya śabdasya satī katham abhāmā ity
arthāntareṇa saṃvaraṇāt saṃvṛttiḥ |
children.translated_text: Here, the concealment of the word '<s>Satyabhāmā</s>' that he himself had uttered, by reinterpreting it as 'the virtuous one who is not illustrious' — this is <s>saṃvṛtti</s> (concealment).
Now, <s>bhrānti</s> (delusion) —
<s>Bhrānti</s> (delusion) is erroneous knowledge, arising from certainty even in an irrelevant context. || 142 ||
As in the ninth [act], <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> —

children.text: atra bhāvi nirātaṅka-māro me ramaṇaṃ mama |
children.translated_text: Here shall be my fearless love-play, my beloved,
If this is the land of <s>Kuśasthalī</s>, the land free of <s>darbha</s> grass. || (9.58)

children.text:
candrāvalī - māhavi, ṇūṇaṃ diṭṭhahmi jaṃ vidabbhaṃgabhutti bāharīadi |
[mādhavi nūnaṃ dṛṣṭāsmi, yad vidarbhaāṅga-bhūr iti vyāhriyate |]
children.translated_text: <s>Candrāvalī</s>: O <s>Mādhavī</s>, surely I have been seen, since he speaks of 'the land of <s>Vidarbha</s>.'

children.text: atra vidarbhāṅgabhūr ity asya vigata-darbha-bhūmitvājñānaṃ devyāḥ bhrāntiḥ |
children.translated_text: Here, the queen's erroneous understanding of '<s>vidarbhāṅgabhū</s>' as meaning 'the land of <s>Vidarbha</s>' instead of 'land devoid of <s>darbha</s> grass' constitutes <s>bhrānti</s> (delusion).
However, some hold that <s>bhrānti</s> (delusion) is the agitated behavior caused by the harassment of bees.
Now, <s>dūtya</s> (embassy) —
<s>Dūtya</s> (embassy) is assisting in a matter that is difficult to accomplish. || 143 ||
As in the first [act], <s>Kundalatā</s> —
The <s>cakorī</s> bird, tormented by thirst and confined to a cage, burns for a long time.
O lord of the stars, extend your foot into the <s>bañjula</s> bower! || (1.58)
[The <s>cakorī</s> bird, tormented by thirst and confined to a cage, burns for a long time.
O lord of the stars, extend your foot into the <s>bañjula</s> bower!]

children.text:
atra jaṭilā-prātikūlyena kundalatāyā durghaṭe rādhā-saṅgama-kārye sahakāritvaṃ
dūtyam |
children.translated_text: Here, <s>Kundalatā's</s> assistance in the difficult task of <s>Rādhā's</s> union, despite <s>Jaṭilā's</s> opposition, constitutes <s>dūtya</s> (embassy).
Now, <s>hetv-avadhāraṇam</s> (ascertainment of cause) —
<s>Hetv-avadhāraṇam</s> (ascertainment of cause) is considered to be the determination of a matter through reasoning. || 144 ||
As in the second [act] —

children.text:
vṛndā - sthāne khalv iyaṃ tava cintā | tathyam eṣā duṣṭenākrāntā trilokīm eva
santāpayet | yataḥ -
children.translated_text: <s>Vṛndā</s>: Indeed, this concern of yours is well-founded. Truly, she being seized by that wicked one would torment the three worlds. For —
Those young women who shine above all with the fragrance of their virtues,

children.text: tāḥ kasyārtaṃ dadhati na khal-sparśa-dagdhās taruṇyaḥ |
children.translated_text: When scorched by the touch of a villain, how do they not cause distress?

children.text: bhūyo bhūyaḥ svayam anupamāṃ klāntim āsādayantī
children.translated_text: Anxiety, itself repeatedly reaching an incomparable state of exhaustion,

children.text: mandākrāntā bhavati jagataḥ kleśa-dātrī hi cintā || (2.9)
children.translated_text: Advancing slowly, indeed becomes the giver of suffering to the world. || (2.9)

children.text:
atra citra-nidarśanopabṛṃhitena sarva-guṇottama-strī-duḥkha-rūpeṇa hetunā
sarva-jana-duḥkhasya niścayād dhetv-avadhāraṇam |
children.translated_text: Here, from the determination of the suffering of all people through the cause in the form of the suffering of the woman of highest virtues, supported by a vivid illustration, this is <s>hetv-avadhāraṇam</s> (ascertainment of cause).
Now, <s>svapna</s> (dream) —
<s>Svapna</s> (dream) describes some utterance made during sleep. || 145 ||
As in the seventh [act] —
<s>Nava-Vṛndā</s> —
"O <s>Lalitā</s>, the creeper of heart's longing of <s>Śvāphalki's</s> descendant has borne fruit!

children.text: hā dhik paśya murāntako'yam urarīcakre rathārohaṇam |
children.translated_text: Alas, look! The slayer of <s>Mura</s> has mounted the chariot!"
Hearing your dream-speech thus clustered with sounds of compassion,

children.text: manye tanvi patat tuṣāra-kapaṭāc cakranda yāminy api || (7.10)
children.translated_text: I think, O slender one, the night itself cried out from the pretense of frost. || (7.10)
Here is the dream-speech of <s>Rādhā</s>.
Now, <s>lekha</s> (letter) —
<s>Lekha</s> (letter) is said to be a written message conveying the intended meaning. || 146 ||
As in the fifth [act] —
<s>Paurṇamāsī</s> —
Quickly dispersing the flock of royal swans, your rival, with your calls,

children.text: kṛṣṇa-ghanas tvām amṛtais tṛṣitāṃ candrakavatīṃ siñca || (5.7)
children.translated_text: O dark cloud <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, sprinkle with your nectar the thirsty <s>Candrakāvatī</s> (peahen)! || (5.7)
This is the letter addressed to <s>Candrāvalī</s>.
Now, <s>mada</s> (intoxication) —
<s>Mada</s> (intoxication) is that which is caused by liquor...
As in the fifth [act] —
<s>Bhīṣma</s> (observing again, with a smile):

children.text: bile kva nu vililyire nṛpa-pipīlikāḥ pīḍitāḥ
children.translated_text: "Into what hole have the ant-like kings hidden themselves, being crushed?

children.text: pinasmi jagadaṇḍakaṃ nanu hariḥ krudhaṃ dhāsyati |
children.translated_text: I shall grind the cosmic egg — surely <s>Hari</s> will become angry!

children.text: śacī-gṛha-kuraṅga re hasasi kiṃ tvam ity unnadann
children.translated_text: O you deer in <s>Śacī's</s> garden, why do you laugh?" — thus roaring,
<s>Halī</s> (<s>Balarāma</s>) rises forth, his crest-jewel slipping from the tumult of his intoxication! || (5.41) ||
Here is the <s>mada</s> (intoxication) of <s>Baladeva</s>.
Now, <s>citra</s> (painting) —
<s>Citra</s> (painting) is the viewing of images. || 147 ||
As in the ninth [act] —
<s>Nava-Vṛndā</s> (entering): Behold this wonderfully painted picture!
Here, the adventures in <s>Mathurā</s> are depicted in a painting.
The application of the intermediate junctures should be understood as without fixed division,
Since these are observed without regularity in the junctures. || 148 ||
Now, the ornaments (<s>vibhūṣaṇas</s>) —

children.text: evam aṅgair upāṅgaiś ca suśliṣṭaṃ rūpaka-śriyaḥ |
children.translated_text: Thus, through the limbs and sub-limbs, the well-joined body of the dramatic art's splendor

children.text: śarīraṃ vas tv alaṅkuryāt ṣaḍ-triṃśad bhūṣaṇaiḥ sphuṭam || 149 ||
children.translated_text: Should be clearly adorned with thirty-six ornaments. || 149 ||
<s>Bhūṣaṇa</s> (ornament), <s>akṣara-saṅghāta</s> (syllable-combination), <s>hetu</s> (cause), <s>prāpti</s> (attainment), <s>udāhṛti</s> (illustration),
<s>Śobhā</s> (beauty), <s>saṃśaya</s> (doubt), <s>dṛṣṭānta</s> (example), <s>abhiprāya</s> (intention), <s>nidarśana</s> (demonstration), || 150 ||
<s>Siddhi</s> (accomplishment), <s>prasiddhi</s> (well-known saying), <s>dākṣiṇya</s> (courtesy), <s>arthāpatti</s> (presumption), <s>vibhūṣaṇa</s> (adornment),
<s>Padoccaya</s> (collection of words), <s>tulyatarka</s> (analogical reasoning), <s>vicāra</s> (deliberation), and its opposite, || 151 ||
<s>Guṇātipāta</s> (surpassing of virtues), <s>atiśaya</s> (excellence), <s>nirukta</s> (etymology), <s>guṇa-kīrtana</s> (praise of virtues),
<s>Garhaṇa</s> (blame), <s>anunaya</s> (conciliation), <s>bhraṃśa</s> (downfall), <s>leśa</s> (trace), <s>kṣobha</s> (agitation), <s>manoratha</s> (desire), || 152 ||
<s>Anukti-siddhi</s> (accomplishment through silence), <s>sārūpya</s> (resemblance), <s>mālā</s> (garland), <s>madhura-bhāṣaṇa</s> (sweet speech),
<s>Pṛcchā</s> (question), <s>upadiṣṭa</s> (instruction), and <s>dṛṣṭa</s> (what is seen) — these are the thirty-six ornaments. || 153 ||
Among those, <s>bhūṣaṇam</s> (ornament) —
Speech abounding in virtues and figures of speech is considered <s>bhūṣaṇam</s> (ornament). || 154 ||
As in the ninth [act] —
<s>Kṛṣṇa</s> (looking all around):
Splendor shines in the pure groves of white lotuses all around,
Among the entire host of darkness, hostile to the true path, waning appears,
Among the stars, diminution arises — generally among the mean-spirited —

children.text: śaṅke śaṅkara-maulir abhyudayate rājā purastād diśi ||9.10||
children.translated_text: I suspect that the crown-jewel of <s>Śaṅkara</s> (the moon) rises in the eastern direction! || 9.10 ||

children.text:
atra prasāda-mādhuryādi-guṇānām anuprāsa-śleṣānumānādy-alaṅkārāṇāṃ ca
sattayā bhūṣaṇam |
children.translated_text: Here, due to the presence of qualities such as <s>prasāda</s> (clarity) and <s>mādhurya</s> (sweetness), and figures of speech such as <s>anuprāsa</s> (alliteration), <s>śleṣa</s> (pun), and <s>anumāna</s> (inference), this is <s>bhūṣaṇam</s> (ornament).
Now, <s>akṣara-saṅghāta</s> (syllable-combination) —
<s>Akṣara-saṅghāta</s> (syllable-combination) is a sentence with a different meaning through homophonous words. || 155 ||
As in the fifth [act] —
<s>Suparṇa</s> (<s>Garuḍa</s>): Lord! See, see —
All around shine the faces of the doe-eyed women
Who have climbed to the tops of mansions to gaze upon you.
By those faces, O lotus-eyed one, there have been swiftly created
Expanses of sky adorned with rows of moons! || (5.32)

children.text:
atra candrāṇām āvalyā paricitānīty atra candrāvalī nāma pratibhānād
akṣara-saṅghātaḥ |
children.translated_text: Here, from the word '<s>candrāvalī</s>' suggesting both 'a row of moons' and the name <s>Candrāvalī</s>, this is <s>akṣara-saṅghāta</s> (syllable-combination).
Now, <s>hetu</s> (cause) —

children.text: sa hetur iti nirdiṣṭo yat sādhyārtha-prasādhakam || 156 ||
children.translated_text: That which accomplishes the intended meaning is designated as <s>hetu</s> (cause). || 156 ||
As in the seventh [act] —

children.text:
madhumaṅgalaḥ (nirīkṣya) piabaassa! pekkha kāe bi aṇurāiṇīe sevā kidatthi |
[priya-vayasya, paśya kayāpy anurāgiṇyā sevā kṛtāsti |]
children.translated_text: <s>Madhumaṅgala</s> (observing): Dear friend! See, some loving woman has performed devotional service.
<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>: Friend, well observed!
This garland, with its arrangement displaced, reveals her helplessness;
This unevenly applied cosmetic paste tells of a shower of tears from her eyes;

children.text: karotkampaṃ tasyā vadati tilakaṃ kuñcitam idaṃ
children.translated_text: The trembling of her hands is declared by this crooked <s>tilaka</s> mark —
All this manifests the love diligently cultivated by this slender-bodied maiden. || (7.32)
Here, from the statement of causes such as helplessness for establishing love, this is <s>hetu</s> (cause).
Now, <s>prāpti</s> (attainment) —
<s>Prāpti</s> (attainment) is the inference of the remainder from seeing a single part. || 157 ||
As in the ninth [act] —
<s>Kṛṣṇa</s> (walking about):
O doe, a new golden creeper that moves has been found,
Clearly <s>Rādhikā</s> herself, beautiful on the forest boundary!

children.text: asyās tvayā sakhi guror yad iyaṃ gṛhītā
children.translated_text: From you, O friend, who belong to the guru, she has received
This initiation into the sport of eyes curved with sweetness. || 9.17 ||

children.text:
atra locanasaundarya-dīkṣā-lālasasya ekadeśasya tvayi vilokanena sālaṃ tvayā
labdheti viśeṣārthasya yojanāt prāptiḥ |
children.translated_text: Here, from seeing the single aspect of the eagerness for the initiation of the beauty of the eyes in you, the inference of the particular meaning 'she has been found through you' constitutes <s>prāpti</s> (attainment).
Now, <s>udāharaṇam</s> (illustration) —
A statement whose hidden meaning is equivalent [to the surface meaning] is considered <s>udāharaṇam</s> (illustration). || 158 ||
As in the second [act] —

children.text:
kundalatā (sasmitam) rāhi, dehi me pāritosiaṃ, yaṃ suṭṭhu dullahaṃ de
abbhatthidaṃ mae ṇibbāhidam | [rādhe, dehi me pāritoṣikam | yat suṣṭhu durlabhaṃ
children.translated_text: <s>Kundalatā</s> (with a smile): O <s>Rādhā</s>, give me a reward, for the very difficult thing you desired has been accomplished by me!

children.text:
rādhikā (vakram avekṣya) kundaladie, kiṃ me abbhatthidaṃ? [kundalate, kiṃ
me'bhyarthitam?] 81
children.translated_text: <s>Rādhikā</s> (looking askance): O <s>Kundalatā</s>, what was desired by me?

children.text: kundalatā - aī, kīsa bhuaṃ bhaṃguresi, jaa sūrārāhaṇaṃ bhaṇāmi | [ayi, kasmād
children.translated_text: <s>Kundalatā</s>: O dear, why do you arch your brow? I speak of sun-worship!
Here, due to the hidden intentional meaning of <s>Kundalatā's</s> words, this is <s>udāharaṇam</s> (illustration).
Where through a statement with an equivalent meaning, by demonstration,
The desired meaning is accomplished — that is considered <s>udāharaṇam</s> (illustration). Thus states (<s>Sāhityadarpaṇa</s> 6.117).
That is to say, in the sixth [act] —
<s>Nārada</s>: Then he said —

children.text: jvalito janaḥ kṛśānau śāmyati taptaḥ kṛśānunaivāyam |
children.translated_text: A person set ablaze in fire is extinguished by fire itself when heated;

children.text: bhagavati kṛtāgaso me bhagavān evādhunā śaraṇam || (6.17)
children.translated_text: O Lord, for one who has offended against the Lord, the Lord alone is now the refuge. || (6.17)
Now, <s>śobhā</s> (beauty) —
<s>Śobhā</s> (beauty) is said to be the mutual revelation of the natural qualities of the young couple.
As in the fourth [act] —

children.text:
rādhikā (mādhavam avalokya, sānandam ātmagatam) bho bhaavaṃ,
āṇanda-pajjaṇṇa, ṇa kkhu rundhīai jalāsāreṇa ukkaṃṭhidā tavassiṇīhi me
diṭṭhīcaurī | kkhaṇaṃ pibedu esā dullahaṃ imassa muhacandassa joṇham | [bho
bhagavan, ānanda-parjanya, na khalu rundhyatāṃ jalāsāreṇotkaṇṭhitā tapasvinī me
dṛṣṭ-cakorī | kṣaṇaṃ pibatv eṣā durlabhām asya mukha-candrasya jyotsnam |] 99
children.translated_text: <s>Rādhikā</s> (seeing <s>Mādhava</s>, joyfully, aside): O Lord, O cloud of bliss, do not obstruct with a shower of rain my longing gaze-<s>cakorī</s> bird! Let it drink for a moment the rare moonlight of this moon-face!
<s>Kṛṣṇa</s> (looking at <s>Rādhā</s>, with delight) —

children.text: dhāvaty ākramituṃ muhuḥ śravaṇayoḥ sīmānam akṣṇor dvayī
children.translated_text: The pair of her eyes rushes repeatedly to cross the boundary of her ears;

children.text: pauṣkalyaṃ harataḥ kucau bali-guṇair ārabdhamānaṃ tataḥ |
children.translated_text: Her breasts steal the fullness that was being commenced with lines of offering;

children.text: muṣṇītaś calatāṃ bhruvau caraṇayor udyad-dhanur bibhrame
children.translated_text: Her moving eyebrows rob the bow-like grace of her feet —
In the bodily realm of <s>Rādhā</s>, the king called Youth overthrows order! || (4.27)
Here, from the mutual revelation of their states, this is <s>śobhā</s> (beauty). However, some say —

children.text:
siddhair arthaiḥ samaṃ yatrāprasiddho'rthaḥ prakāśate |
śliṣṭa-lakṣaṇa-citrārthā sā śobhety abhidhīyate || ity āha | (SāhD 6.176)
children.translated_text: "Where an unknown meaning shines forth together with established meanings, with closely connected characteristics and wonderful sense — that is called <s>śobhā</s> (beauty)." Thus states (<s>Sāhityadarpaṇa</s> 6.176).
As in the ninth [act] —
<s>Navavṛndā</s> (looking ahead, with delight):
The Creator, purifier of the world, skilled in producing a sweet appearance,
This autumn, with supreme swans appearing, meets [us] like <s>bhakti</s> (devotion) itself! || 9.1 ||
Now, <s>saṃśaya</s> (doubt) —

children.text: aniścayāt tu yad vākyaṃ sandehasya nigadyate || 159 ||
children.translated_text: A statement expressing uncertainty is called <s>saṃśaya</s> (doubt). || 159 ||
As in the second [act] (from behind the stage) —
Tall as a palm tree with raised arms, with a chest like a mountain slope — where is that lowest of <s>Yakṣas</s>?
And where is this child, soft as a young <s>tamāla</s> shoot, beautiful as <s>Kandarpa</s> (the god of love)?

children.text: nāsty anyaḥ sahakāritā-paṭur iha prāṇī na jānīmahe
children.translated_text: There is no other being here skilled in being an ally — we do not know

children.text: hā goṣṭheśvari kīdṛg adya tapasāṃ pākas tavonmīlati || (2.29)
children.translated_text: Alas, O queen of the cowherd settlement, what manner of ripening of austerities is blossoming forth today! || (2.29)
Here, since the sentence concludes with doubt itself, this is <s>saṃśaya</s> (doubt).
Now <s>dṛṣṭānta</s> (illustration) —
The showing of a reason in one's own case, for the establishment of what is to be proved, is <s>dṛṣṭānta</s> (illustration). || 160 ||
As in the ninth [act] —
<s>Kṛṣṇa</s> (reflecting): Or rather —
Even a person who is steadfast by nature sometimes
undergoes agitation due to the pressure of circumstance;
for the all-enduring earth herself, forsaking patience,
has been widely seen to tremble violently. || (9.20)

children.text:
atra dhīre'pi jane vikāra-sad-bhāve sādhye tat-sādhakasya calana-rūpa-vikārasya
hetoḥ sarvaṃsahāyāṃ bhuvi darśitatvād dṛṣṭāntaḥ |
children.translated_text: Here, since the cause in the form of trembling-agitation is shown in the all-enduring earth, to prove the existence of agitation even in a steadfast person, this is <s>dṛṣṭānta</s> (illustration).
Now <s>abhiprāya</s> (intention) —

children.text: abhiprāyas tv abhūtārtho hṛdyaḥ sāmyena kalpitaḥ |
children.translated_text: <s>Abhiprāya</s> (intention) is a charming idea, though not factual, imagined through analogy;

children.text: abhiprāyaṃ pare prāhur mamatāṃ hṛdy avastuni || 161 ||
children.translated_text: Others define <s>abhiprāya</s> as attachment in the heart toward an unreal object. || 161 ||
As in the fourth [act] —
<s>Kṛṣṇa</s> (eagerly revealing horripilation) —
This actor, who overflows with wondrous sweetness and fragrance, embodying the sport of a cowherd,

children.text: dvaitaṃ hanta samakṣayan muhur asau citrīyate cāraṇaḥ |
children.translated_text: alas, repeatedly dissolving my sense of duality, astonishes me;
O friend, my mind, agitated with curiosity for amorous play,
upon seeing his surpassing beauty, at once seeks identity with the women of <s>Vraja</s>. || (4.19)

children.text:
atrābhūtārtha-rūpasya bhagavad-dvitīyatvasya naṭe kalpanam abhiprāyaḥ | hṛdy
avastuni sva-saundarye bhogecchayā mamatā vā |
children.translated_text: Here, the imagining that the actor is a second form of the Lord, which is an unreal idea, constitutes <s>abhiprāya</s> (intention). Or, the attachment in the heart toward one's own beauty, with desire for enjoyment, is also [abhiprāya].
Now <s>nidarśana</s> (exemplification) —
When well-known established facts are proclaimed
for the purpose of dispelling another's disregard, that is called <s>nidarśana</s> (exemplification). || 162 ||
As in the fourth [act] —
<s>Gārgī</s> (in Sanskrit) —
She who, though <s>Mukunda</s> is the root of all desires,
forcibly sent him out to gather firewood —
that teacher's wife indeed makes a commodity
of the lord of <s>cintāmaṇi</s> (wish-fulfilling gems) for the sake of oil-cake! || (4.6)
Here, through the illustration of the original and reflected objects, this is <s>nidarśana</s> (exemplification).
Now <s>siddhi</s> (unexpected fulfillment) —
<s>Siddhi</s> (unexpected fulfillment) is the encounter with a desired object that occurs unexpectedly.
As in the sixth [act] —
<s>Kṛṣṇa</s> (having done so, with a choked voice) —
Having immediately recognized that <s>Lalitā</s> near the tree,
and having seen the form of <s>Rādhā</s>, naturally sweet in appearance,
and also examining the jewel, the crest-ornament of <s>Śaṅkhacūḍa</s>,
I am repeatedly whirling with immense agitation. || (6.40)

children.text:
atra iṣṭasya lalitā-darśanasyātarkitopapannatvāt siddhiḥ | kaścit tu bahūnāṃ
kīrtanaṃ siddhir abhipretārtha-siddhaye ity (SāhD 6.186) āha | tad yathā daśame
children.translated_text: Here, since the desired sight of <s>Lalitā</s> occurred unexpectedly, this is <s>siddhi</s> (unexpected fulfillment). Some, however, say that <s>siddhi</s> is 'the enumeration of many things for the accomplishment of the intended purpose' (<s>Sāhityadarpaṇa</s> 6.186). That is, as in the tenth [act] —

children.text:
kṛṣṇaḥ - priye tvad-āsyaṃ paśyato me nopamāna-vastūni hṛdayam ārohanti naḥ |
yataḥ -
children.translated_text: <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> — Beloved, when I behold your face, no objects of comparison enter my heart. Because —

children.text: dhatte na sthiti-yogyatāṃ caraṇayor aṅke'pi paṅkeruhaṃ
children.translated_text: The lotus does not attain the fitness to stand even at [your] feet,
nor does the jeweled mirror prove competent in the region of [your] toenails;
O passionate one, even in wiping the circumference of your face,
even <s>Candrāvalī</s> (the full moon), though radiant and complete in all digits, does not attain propriety. || (10.11)
Here, the enumeration of qualities is evident.
Now <s>prasiddhi</s> (celebrity) —
<s>Prasiddhi</s> (celebrity) is the accomplishment of one's own purpose through universally famous facts. || 163 ||
As in the sixth [act] —
<s>Vasantī</s>, dwelling in the inner chambers, pervaded by the sweetness of the enemy of <s>Madhu</s>,

children.text: iyaṃ tanvī sadyaḥ svayam iha bhavitrī karagatā |
children.translated_text: this slender one will soon come into hand of her own accord;
when encircled by the lofty, complete fragrance of <s>madhūlī</s> (spring blossoms),
who can describe the new lotus pond in full bloom that the swarm of bees [approaches]? || (6.28)
<s>Nava-Vṛndā</s> (to herself) —

children.text:
atra loka-vikhyātasya praphulla-kamalinī-rolamba-saṅgamasya kathanena svārthasya
rādhā-mādhavayoḥ saṅgamasya sādhanaṃ prasiddhiḥ |
children.translated_text: Here, through the narration of the universally known encounter of bees with a blossoming lotus pond, the accomplishment of one's own purpose — the union of <s>Rādhā</s> and <s>Mādhava</s> — is implied; this is <s>prasiddhi</s> (celebrity).
Now <s>dākṣiṇya</s> (courteousness) —
<s>Dākṣiṇya</s> (courteousness) is the verbal compliance with another's mind. || 164 ||
As in the second [act] —

children.text:
lalitā (sālīkam) ajje, pekkha | eso kaṇho moṭṭimaṃ ahma viḍambaṇaṃ karedi |
[ārye, paśya | eṣa kṛṣṇaḥ balād asmad-viḍambanaṃ karoti |] 117
children.translated_text: <s>Lalitā</s> (with annoyance): Lady, look! This <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> is forcibly mocking us! [Lady, look! This <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> is forcibly mocking us!]
Here, <s>Lalitā</s>'s compliance with <s>Mukharā</s>'s mind constitutes <s>dākṣiṇya</s> (courteousness).
Now <s>arthāpatti</s> (presumption) —
When, due to the impossibility of the stated meaning, another meaning is inferred,
from a statement endowed with sweetness, it is called <s>arthāpatti</s> (presumption). || 165 ||
As in the ninth [act] —
<s>Navavṛndā</s> —
O you of jasmine-white teeth, the pair of your eyes is made of moonstone;
when the moon of <s>Hari</s>'s face rises, how else would they melt? || 9.13

children.text:
atra syandanānyathānupapattyā netrasya candrakāntamayatvaa-kalpanād iyam
arthāpattiḥ | yathā vā daśame -
children.translated_text: Here, since the melting cannot be explained otherwise, the imagining that the eyes are made of moonstone constitutes this <s>arthāpatti</s> (presumption). Or alternatively, as in the tenth [act] —

children.text:
candrāvalī - dea! tuhma vilāsa sokkhāṇaṃ bāhādeṇa kida mahāparāhamhi | tā
kāruṇṇeṇa āṇabehi jadhā goṭhṭhabaiṇo goṭṭhaṃ gadua basaṃtī tumaṃ suhiṇaṃ
karemi | [deva! tava vilāsasaukhyānāṃ vyāghātena kṛta-mahāparādhāsmi | tat
kāruṇyena ājñāpaya yathā goṣṭhapater goṣṭhaṃ gatvā vasantī tvāṃ sukhinaṃ
children.translated_text: <s>Candrāvalī</s> — O Lord! I have committed a great offense by obstructing your pleasure and enjoyment. So, mercifully command that, having gone to the cowherd chief's settlement as <s>Vasantī</s>, I may make you happy. [O Lord! I have committed a great offense by obstructing your pleasure and enjoyment. So, mercifully command that, having gone to the cowherd chief's settlement as <s>Vasantī</s>, I may make you happy.]
Here, due to the impossibility of the stated purpose of going to the settlement, the prohibition of union with <s>Satyā</s> is inferred.
Now <s>viśeṣaṇa</s> (qualification) —

children.text: siddhān bahūn pradhānārthān uktvā yatra prayuñjate |
children.translated_text: When, after stating many established principal meanings, one employs
a statement endowed with distinction, that is to be known as <s>viśeṣaṇa</s> (qualification). || 166 ||
As in the fourth [act], <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> —

children.text: lakṣmīvān iha dakṣiṇānila-sakhaḥ sākṣān madhur modate
children.translated_text: Here, the auspicious southern breeze, a friend, truly rejoices in <s>Madhu</s> (spring);
here too, <s>Vṛndāvana</s> laughs charmingly, outshining the intoxicated bees and birds;

children.text: rādhā yady abhisāram atra kurute so'yaṃ mahān eva me
children.translated_text: if <s>Rādhā</s> undertakes her amorous journey here, then indeed this is for me
a great tumultuous festival of swinging on the waves of the ocean of intense bliss! || (4.17)

children.text:
atra prasiddhārthān madhu-vṛndāvanādīn uktvā rādhābhisārasya
vaiśiṣya-kathanād viśeṣaṇam | kaścit tu lekhiṣyamāṇaṃ
nava-nava-sudhā-sambandho'pi (1.33)
 ity ādi-padyam atrodāharati |
[*NOTE: Full verse given below, at 171 (atiśayaḥ).]
children.translated_text: Here, after stating the well-known things like spring and <s>Vṛndāvana</s>, the narration of the distinction of <s>Rādhā</s>'s amorous journey constitutes <s>viśeṣaṇa</s> (qualification). Some, however, cite the verse to be written below, 'nava-nava-sudhā-sambandho'pi' (1.33), as the example here. [*NOTE: Full verse given below, at 171 (<s>atiśaya</s>).]
Now <s>padoccaya</s> (accumulation of words) —

children.text: bahūnāṃ tu prayuktānāṃ padānāṃ bahubhiḥ padaiḥ |
children.translated_text: When many employed words are gathered with many [other] words

children.text: uccayaḥ sadṛśārtho yaḥ sa vijñeyaḥ padoccayaḥ || 167 ||
children.translated_text: of similar meaning, that is to be known as <s>padoccaya</s> (accumulation of words). || 167 ||
As in the fourth [act], <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> —
My mind whirled together with swarms of bees,
my composure, along with the honey, became lost;
longing blossomed forth along with the clusters of buds —
all this for me, separated from my beloved, here. || (4.21)

children.text:
atra matyādīnāṃ ghūrṇādi-kriyāsu alivrajādibhiḥ samāveśād ayaṃ padoccayaḥ |
kaścit tu uccayo'rthānurūpo yaḥ padānāṃ sa padoccayaḥ ity (SāhD 6.180) āha |
yathā daśame -
[*NOTE: saṃcayo]
children.translated_text: Here, the involvement of bee-swarms and such in the actions of whirling and so forth of the mind and other [faculties] constitutes this <s>padoccaya</s> (accumulation of words). Some, however, say '<s>padoccaya</s> is the accumulation of words conforming to meaning' (<s>Sāhityadarpaṇa</s> 6.180). As in the tenth [act] — [*NOTE: <s>saṃcaya</s>]
O slender one, raise your eyes a little,
kissing the wonder of the trembling <s>cakora</s> birds;
and the nectar of your smile, a <s>mādhavī</s> creeper of the moon,
bestow here, bearing it unfailingly from the moon. || 10.8 ||
Now <s>tulyatarka</s> (analogical reasoning) —
An expression employed with metaphors or similes of equal meaning,
touching upon an imperceptible meaning, is called <s>tulyatarka</s> (analogical reasoning). || 168 ||
As in that same [play], in the ninth [act], <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> —
Even from harsh treatment, with great childish impetuosity,
surging with a flood of affection, distressed —
as I behold my mother today,
my heart melts like an oblation of ghee. || (9.26)

children.text:
atra havir vilāyam iti luptopamayā'pratyakṣasya citta-dravasya kathanaṃ
tulya-tarkaḥ | kaścit tu tulyatarko yad arthena tarkaḥ prakṛta-gāminā ity (SāhD
6.180) āha | yathā caturthe -
children.translated_text: Here, through the truncated simile 'like an oblation of ghee,' the expression of the imperceptible melting of the heart constitutes <s>tulyatarka</s> (analogical reasoning). Some, however, say '<s>tulyatarka</s> is reasoning about the subject through an analogous meaning' (<s>Sāhityadarpaṇa</s> 6.180). As in the fourth [act] —

children.text:
jaṭilā - ṇūṇaṃ nūurasahena āhaḍiṭṭā ede haṃsā haṃsaṇaṃdi-ṇījalādo vaṇe
dhāanti | tā bahūḍiā ṇādidūre habissadi | [nūnaṃ nūpura-śabdena ākarṣitā ete
haṃsā haṃsa-nandinī-jalāt vane dhāvanti | tad vadhūṭikā nātidūre bhaviṣyati |]
children.translated_text: <s>Jaṭilā</s> — Surely, attracted by the sound of anklet bells, these swans are running from the water of <s>Haṃsanandī</s> into the forest. So the young bride must not be far away. [Surely, attracted by the sound of anklet bells, these swans are running from the water of <s>Haṃsanandī</s> into the forest. So the young bride must not be far away.]
Now <s>vicāra</s> (deliberation) —
<s>Vicāra</s> (deliberation) is the description of many means for a single end.
As in the first [act], <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> —
Friend, <s>Madhumaṅgala</s>, behold —
With their chewing of abundant grass and shoots becoming slack,
their faces turning downward with the onset of increasingly frequent lowing,
the beauty of their restless eyes enhanced, the row of cows
on the path, with beautifully curved necks, has become longing for <s>Gokula</s>. || (1.28)

children.text:
atrotkaṇṭhitasyaa sādhyasya sādhanāni tṛṇāsvāda-śaithilyādīni | yad vā agre
lekhyaṃ śaraṇam iha yo bhrātuḥ (5.25) ity ādi padyam atrodāharaṇaṃ jñeyam |
kaścit tu vicāro yukti-vākyair yad apratyakṣārtha-darśanam ity (SāhD 6.182) āha |
atroktam udāharaṇam api saṅgacchate |
children.translated_text: Here, the means for the end of longing are the slackening of grass-chewing and so forth. Or, the verse to be written ahead, 'śaraṇam iha yo bhrātuḥ' (5.25), should be known as the example here. Some, however, say '<s>vicāra</s> is the perception of an imperceptible meaning through statements of reasoning' (<s>Sāhityadarpaṇa</s> 6.182). The example given here also applies to that.
Now <s>tadviparyaya</s> (reversal) —
The opposite condition of deliberation is to be known as <s>tadviparyaya</s> (reversal). || 169 ||
As in the sixth [act] —
<s>Rādhā</s> (with agitation, addressing the sky, in Sanskrit) —

children.text: vicitrāyāṃ kṣauṇyām ajaniṣata kanyāḥ kati na vā
children.translated_text: On this varied earth, how many maidens have not been born?

children.text: kaṭhorāṅgī nānyā nivasati mayā kāpi sadṛśī |
children.translated_text: No other harsh-limbed woman dwells who is like me;

children.text: mukundaṃ yan muktvā samayam aham adyāpi gamaye
children.translated_text: that even now, having abandoned <s>Mukunda</s>, I pass my time —

children.text: dhig astu pratyāśām ahaha dhig asūn dhiṅ mama dhiyam || (6.21)
children.translated_text: shame on my hope, alas, shame on my life-breaths, shame on my mind! || (6.21)
Here, through the excess of anguish, the censure of hope constitutes <s>viparyaya</s> (reversal).
Now <s>guṇātipāta</s> (transgression of qualities) —
<s>Guṇātipāta</s> (transgression of qualities) is defined as the inverted narration of qualities. || 170 ||
As in the fourth [act] —
<s>Jaṭilā</s> (laughing boisterously, in Sanskrit) —
Who on earth does not know this quality of the son of the lord of <s>Vraja</s>,
adorned with the weight of his fame in the sport of dallying with others' wives?

children.text: yad eṣa rati-taskaraḥ pathi nirudhya sādhvīr balāt
children.translated_text: For this thief of love, forcibly accosting virtuous women on the path,
[places] his nails on their breast-buds — Om, salutations to <s>Viṣṇu</s>! || (4.31)

children.text:
atra prakaṭaś ca guṇātipātaḥ | kaścit tu guṇātipātaḥ kārye yad viparītaṃ guṇān
prati ity āha (SāhD 6.184), yathā pañcame candrāvalī (saṃskṛtena) -
children.translated_text: Here, the <s>guṇātipāta</s> (transgression of qualities) is evident. Some, however, say '<s>guṇātipāta</s> is that which is contrary to qualities in the result' (<s>Sāhityadarpaṇa</s> 6.184). As in the fifth [act], <s>Candrāvalī</s> (in Sanskrit) —

children.text: śaraṇam iha yo bhrātus tasya pratīpa-vidhāyinā
children.translated_text: He who was my refuge here, by his brother's antagonist,

children.text: hita-kṛd api tā devyās tasyāḥ samagram upekṣaṇam |
children.translated_text: even she who was beneficent, by that goddess, complete disregard;

children.text: gatir avikalo yo me tasya priyasya ca vismṛtir
children.translated_text: he who was my unfailing resort, and forgetfulness of that beloved —

children.text: bata hatavidho vāme sarvaṃ prayāti viparyayam || (5.25)
children.translated_text: alas, in this ill-fated, perverse fate, everything goes to the opposite! || (5.25)
Now <s>atiśaya</s> (excellence) —

children.text: bahūn guṇān kīrtayitvā sāmānyena ca saṃśritān |
children.translated_text: After enumerating many qualities held in common,

children.text: viśeṣaḥ kīrtyate yatra jñeyaḥ so'tiśayo budhaiḥ || 171 ||
children.translated_text: where a distinction is proclaimed, that is to be known by the learned as <s>atiśaya</s> (excellence). || 171 ||
As in the first [act], <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> —
Though ever connected with fresh nectar, though always dear to the eyes,

children.text: sarasija-vanīṃ mlānāṃ kurvann api prabhayā svayā |
children.translated_text: though causing the lotus pond to wilt by its own radiance,

children.text: vidhur api kalā-pūrṇo'py uccaiḥ kuraṅga-dharaḥ śaśī
children.translated_text: even the moon, though full of all digits and bearing the deer mark,
is conquered by these faces of the doe-eyed women of <s>Vraja</s>, bearing beautiful complexions. || 1.33

Here, after the enumeration of common qualities of the moon and the faces, such as connection with nectar, the proclamation of the distinction of beautiful complexion in the faces is the <s>viśeṣa</s> (distinction).
Now <s>nirukta</s> (etymology) —
<s>Nirukta</s> (etymology) is a faultless statement of names for the elucidation of meaning. || 172 ||
As in the first [act], <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> (approaching <s>Candrāvalī</s>, joyfully) —

children.text: nītas tanvi mukhena te paribhavaṃ bhrū-kṣepaivikrīḍayā
children.translated_text: O slender one, humiliated by your face through the sport of eyebrow-play,

children.text: bibhyad viṣṇu-padaṃ jagāma śaraṇaṃ tatrāpy adhairyaṃ gataḥ |
children.translated_text: the moon, terrified, took refuge in the abode of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, but even there became unsteady;
reaching the victorious one adorned with stars, for the purpose of service, this shining
moon went to the station of the king of stars — therefore you are <s>Candrāvalī</s> (surrounded by moons)! || (1.40)
Here, the name <s>Candrāvalī</s> is etymologically explained.
Now <s>guṇa-kīrtana</s> (praise of qualities) —
Where in the world one among many who are exceedingly endowed with qualities

children.text: ekaḥ saṃśabdyate tat tu vijñeyaṃ guṇa-kīrtanam || 173 ||
children.translated_text: is addressed by their names — that is to be known as <s>guṇa-kīrtana</s> (praise of qualities). || 173 ||

children.text: yathā dvitīye, kṛṣṇaḥ (puro rādhāṃ paśyann apavārya) -
children.translated_text: As in the second [act], <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> (looking at <s>Rādhā</s> before him, aside) —
She who is the pleasure-lake of the lordly elephant that is my mind,
the slow autumnal moonlight for the <s>cakora</s>-birds that are my eyes;
the beautiful row of stars that adorns the bank of heaven that is my chest —
she has been attained through my exalted desires — that <s>Rādhikā</s>! || 2.10 ||
Here, the addressing of <s>Rādhā</s> with words such as 'pleasure-lake' [of the gods] is <s>guṇa-kīrtana</s> (praise of qualities).
Now <s>garhaṇa</s> (censure) —

children.text: yatra saṅkīrtayan doṣān guṇam arthena darśayet |
children.translated_text: Where, while enumerating faults, one reveals a virtue through the meaning;

children.text: guṇān vā kīrtayan doṣaṃ darśayed garhaṇaṃ hi tat || 174 ||
children.translated_text: or while praising virtues, one reveals a fault — that indeed is <s>garhaṇa</s> (censure). || 174 ||
Of these, the first; as in the seventh [act],

children.text:
mādhavī - dea, kaṭorappā esā bhaṭṭi-dāriā suṭṭhu tābaṃ soḍhuṃ pāredi jaṃ
tumha paccakkhaṃ ccea caṃdabhāāmaṃdire jalaṃtaṃ jalana-kuṃḍaṃ jala-keli-kuṇḍaṃ
biṇṇādabadī | [deva, kaṭhorātmaiṣā bhartṛdārikā suṣṭhu tāpaṃ soḍhuṃ pārayati
tat tava pratyakṣam eva candrabhāgā-mandire jvalantaṃ jvalanta-kuṇḍaṃ

children.translated_text: [Sanskrit rendering of the same] 149

<s>Mādhavī</s> — Lord, this hard-hearted noble lady is well able to endure the heat, for in your very presence she has recognized the burning fire-pit at the <s>Candrabhāgā</s> temple as a water-sport pool!

children.text: kṛṣṇaḥ (svagatam) - mādhavi, sādhu sādhu yad atra snehātirekaṃ sūcayantī samaye

children.translated_text: perform the service of friendship. 150
<s>Kṛṣṇa</s> (aside) — O <s>Mādhavī</s>, well done, well done! For you, indicating an excess of affection, at the right moment

children.text:
atra kaṭhorādi-rūpasya doṣasya kathanam api
kṛṣṇa-viṣayānurāga-guṇa-kīrtanatayā paryavasitam | dvitīyaṃ yathā caturthe -
children.translated_text:
Here, although the speech describes the fault of hard-heartedness and such,
it ultimately amounts to praise of the virtue of love directed toward <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>. The second, as in the fourth [act] —

children.text:
kundalatā - bīrāhimaṇṇo, puṇṇabadī me sahī rāhā | jāe dakkhiṇā saccabādiṇī
siṇiddhā tumha mādā sussū laddhā | [vīrābhimanyo! puṇyavatī me sakhī rādhā,
yayā dakṣiṇā satyavādinī snigdhā tava mātā śvaśrūr labdhā |] 133
children.translated_text: you have obtained as mother-in-law one who is generous, truthful, and affectionate! [Sanskrit rendering] 133
<s>Kundalatā</s> — O <s>Vīrābhimanyu</s>! My friend <s>Rādhā</s> is fortunate, for through her

children.text: atra guṇakīrtanam apy arthato doṣa iti garhaṇam |
children.translated_text: Here, though there is praise of virtues, it amounts to censure in meaning — thus it is <s>garhaṇa</s> (censure).
Now <s>anunaya</s> (supplication) —
A speech whose chief purpose is entreaty is to be known by the wise as <s>anunaya</s> (supplication).
As in the fifth [act], <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, tearfully —

children.text: ayaṃ kaṇṭhe lagnaḥ śaśimukhi janas te praṇayavān
children.translated_text: This loving person clings to your neck, O moon-faced one,
for whose unattainment you treat your blessed and beautiful body as mere straw;
Be gracious today, O mistress of my life, desist — upon this devoted one

children.text: kṛthāḥ patyāvatyāhitam idam uro me vidalati || 5.35 ||
children.translated_text: do not inflict this calamity; my heart is splitting apart! || 5.35 ||
Here, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s entreaty to <s>Candrāvalī</s> is <s>anunaya</s> (supplication).
Now <s>bhraṃśa</s> (deflection) —

children.text: patanāt prakṛtād arthād anyasmin bhraṃśa īritaḥ || 175 ||
children.translated_text: A fall from the natural meaning to another is called <s>bhraṃśa</s> (deflection). || 175 ||
As in the ninth [act], <s>Mādhavī</s> —

children.text:
dea, imāṇaṃ pemma-komalāṇaṃ akkharāṇaṃ mā kkhu ṇaṃ ahirūbaṃ jāṇāhi | jaṃ
esā ṇa hodi | [deva, eṣā prema-komalānām akṣarāṇāṃ mā khalv etām abhirūpāṃ
jānīhi | yad eṣā satyā na bhavati |] 194
children.translated_text: Lord, do not consider these love-tender letters as representing her true form, for she does not exist [in that way]. [Sanskrit rendering: Lord, do not consider these love-tender letters as representing her true form, for she is not real.] 194

children.text:
kṛṣṇaḥ - sādhu mādhavike! sādhu | madīya-hṛdayāśaṅkā tvayā nirastā | tad
indra-jālābhijñayā nava-vṛndayaiva nirmiteyaṃ māyikī devī rasālamūla-vartinī
khalu satyā |
children.translated_text: <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> — Well done, <s>Mādhavikā</s>! Well done! My heart's suspicion has been dispelled by you. Then this illusory queen, created by <s>Navavṛndā</s> who is skilled in magic, stationed at the base of the mango tree, is indeed real (<s>Satyā</s>)!

children.text:
atra satyā-śabdasya prakṛtārthaṃ satyabhāmā-rūpaṃ parityajya tathārtha-lakṣaṇasya
kathanād bhraṃśaḥ | kaścit tu kathayanti budhāḥ bhraṃśaṃ vācyād anyatarad-vacaḥ
ity āha | yathā prathame, kṛṣṇaḥ -
[*NOTE: SāhD 6.187 has dṛptādīnāṃ bhavad bhraṃśo vācyād anyatarad vacaḥ |]
children.translated_text:
Here, the word <s>Satyā</s>, abandoning its natural meaning referring to <s>Satyabhāmā</s>, and
expressing the meaning 'real' — this deflection of meaning constitutes <s>bhraṃśa</s>. However, some wise ones say that <s>bhraṃśa</s> is speech conveying something other than what is stated, and cite as follows. As in the first [act], <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> —
[Note: <s>Sāhityadarpaṇa</s> 6.187 has 'the deflection of the proud and others is speech conveying something other than what is stated']

children.text: sarojākṣi parokṣaṃ te kadāpi hṛdayaṃ mama |
children.translated_text: O lotus-eyed one, your heart is beyond my reach, even unseen;

children.text: na spraṣṭum apy alaṃ bādhā rādhā tvākramya gāhate || 1.42
children.translated_text: the affliction that is <s>Rādhā</s>, overcoming you, plunges deep — I cannot even touch it. || 1.42

children.text: atra vācyād rādhāyā asparśād anyad bādhākramaṇaṃ bhraṃśaḥ |
children.translated_text: Here, the <s>bhraṃśa</s> (deflection) consists in the stated meaning of <s>Rādhā</s>'s untouchability being deflected to mean the overcoming by affliction.
Now <s>leśa</s> (hint) —
<s>Leśa</s> is a speech that, like an adjective, produces knowledge of a gesture.
As in the fifth [act], <s>Bhīṣmaka</s> —
This indeed is the bond here among the relatives of the bride;
I inform you that it is fitting, O beloved of <s>Lakṣmī</s>;
Since my daughter is a woman, by transgressing her consent,

children.text: katham api na parasyāḥ pāṇisaṅgo vidheyaḥ || 5.38||
children.translated_text: the giving of her hand to another is by no means to be done. || 5.38 ||
(Having said this and such, <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s> looks at the face of <s>Paurṇamāsī</s>.)

children.text:
paurṇamāsī - mukunda! gokula-kumārī-kulāni candrāvalī-mātrāvaśeṣāṇi
durvidagdhena vidhinā kṛtāni | tad atra kā kṣatiḥ?
children.translated_text: <s>Paurṇamāsī</s> — O <s>Mukunda</s>! The groups of maidens of <s>Gokula</s> have been reduced by the malicious creator to nothing but <s>Candrāvalī</s> alone. So what loss is there in this?

children.text:
atra candrāvalī-mātrāvaśeṣāṇīti viśeṣaṇavad vacaḥ kṛṣṇeṅgita-jñāpakatayā
saṃvṛttam iti leśaḥ |
children.translated_text: Here, the speech containing the qualifier 'nothing but <s>Candrāvalī</s> remaining' functions as indicating <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s intention — thus it is <s>leśa</s> (hint).
Now <s>kṣobha</s> (agitation) —

children.text: kṣobhas tv anya-gate hetāv anyasmin kārya-kalpanaṃ || 176 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Kṣobha</s> is the attribution to one thing of an effect caused by another. || 176 ||
As in the seventh [act], <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> —
I am scorched by these sunbeams that have touched your body;
O goddess, finding shade in the <s>vandana</s> tree, cool me! || 7.37 ||

children.text:
atra sūryātapeṣu candrāvaly-aṅga-saṅgateṣu tat-kārya-bhūtasya tāpasya kṛṣṇena
svasmin kalpanāt kṣobhaḥ | kaścit tu kṣobha-sthāne saṅkṣepaṃ pañhan lakṣayanti -
saṅkṣepo yat tu saṅkṣepād ātmāny arthe prayujyate | (SāhD 6.192) yathāṣṭame -
children.translated_text: <s>Saṅkṣepa</s> is when a meaning is applied to oneself in condensed form. (<s>Sāhityadarpaṇa</s> 6.192) As in the eighth [act] —

Here, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s attribution to himself of the heat — which is actually the effect of
contact with <s>Candrāvalī</s>'s body — as though caused by sunbeams, constitutes <s>kṣobha</s> (agitation). However, some identify <s>saṅkṣepa</s> (condensation) in place of <s>kṣobha</s> —

children.text:
kṛṣṇaḥ - devi, triloka-kakṣāsu kiṃ tavābhīṣṭaṃ? tad abhivyajya
nija-nideśa-bhājanam anyatayaiva paryāpta-samasta-niśreyase preyasi vidhehi
prasāda-mādhurīm |
children.translated_text: <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> — O queen, what is your desire among the three worlds? Express it, and bestow the sweetness of your grace upon this beloved who, even without being directed, is self-sufficient in all supreme good.
Now <s>manoratha</s> (desire) —
<s>Manoratha</s> is the communication of what one wishes to say through a pretext. || 177 ||
As in the fourth [act] —

children.text:
rādhikā - (sautsukyaṃ puro dṛṣṭvā) halā lalide, pekkha pekha dhaṇṇā esā
taraṃga-lehā jā khu sevāla-ballī ṇibaddha-pāaṃ ṇaṃ haṃsiaṃ moābedi | tā phuḍaṃ
bhisiṇīpattantarideṇa kalahaṃseṇa saṃghaḍaissadi | [halā lalite, paśya paśya dhanyā
eṣā taraṅga-lekhā yā khalu śaivāla-vallī-nibaddha-pādām enāṃ haṃsikāṃ
mocayati | tat sphuṭaṃ bisinī-patrāntaritena kalahaṃsena saṃghaṭṭiṣyati |] 71
children.translated_text: <s>Rādhikā</s> — (looking ahead eagerly) Dear <s>Lalitā</s>, look, look! Fortunate is this wave-line which frees this female swan whose feet are bound by the <s>śaivāla</s> (moss) creeper. Clearly she will be united with the <s>kalahaṃsa</s> (swan) hidden behind the lotus leaf! [Sanskrit rendering] 71
Here, <s>Rādhā</s>'s expression of her desire for union with <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> through the pretext of the female swan is <s>manoratha</s> (desire).
Now <s>anukta-siddhi</s> (implied meaning) —
Where even an unstated remaining meaning is understood through the introduction alone,

children.text: anukta-siddhir eṣā syād ity āha bharato muniḥ || 178 ||
children.translated_text: that is <s>anukta-siddhi</s> (implied meaning) — thus says the sage <s>Bharata</s>. || 178 ||

children.text:
*NOTE: First reference to Bharata, whom he has not been following very closely.
Nāṭ 16.169 = prastāvenaiva śeṣo'rthaḥ kṛtsno yan na pratīyate | vacanena
vinānukta-siddhiḥ sā parikīrtitā ||
children.translated_text:
Note: First reference to <s>Bharata</s>, whom he has not been following very closely.
<s>Nāṭyaśāstra</s> 16.169 = 'Where the remaining meaning is not fully understood through the introduction alone, and without words — that is declared to be <s>anukta-siddhi</s>.'
As in the fourth [act] — <s>Rādhā</s>

children.text:
halā labaṃga-kuḍuṅge āharantī tumaṃ buṃdāaṇa-bāsiṇā matta-kalahindeṇa āadua
hattheṇa gahīdahatthāsi saṃbuttā | tado saṃbhamena ghusmantīe tuha haḍheṇa
oṭṭha-pallaaṃ ḍaṃsanteṇa tinā bāme tthabaasmi phurantatikkhakāmaṅkusaṃ
kara-pukkharaṃ | [halā lavaṅga-kuñje āharantī tvaṃ vṛndāvana-vāsinā
matta-kalabhendreṇa āgatya hastena gṛhīta-hastāsi saṃvṛttā | tataḥ sambhramena
ghūrṇantyas tava haṭheṇa oṣṭha-pallavaṃ daṃśatā tena vāme stavake

children.translated_text: the lotus of his hand with its sharp, trembling goad of desire! [Sanskrit rendering] 91

Dear one, while you were gathering [flowers] in the clove grove, a wild young elephant dwelling in <s>Vṛndāvana</s> came and seized your hand with his trunk. Then, as you whirled about in alarm, he, forcefully biting the sprout of your lip, [placed] on your left breast
Here, even though it is unstated, the understanding of the scratching of the breast with nails constitutes <s>anukta-siddhi</s> (implied meaning).
Now <s>sārūpya</s> (resemblance) —
Where, arising from the narration of things seen, heard, or experienced,

children.text: sādṛśyaṃ yatra saṅkṣobhāt tat sārūpyaṃ nirūpyate || 179 ||
