children.translated_text: there is a resemblance due to agitation — that is defined as <s>sārūpya</s> (resemblance). || 179 ||
As in the fourth [act] —

children.text:
jaṭilā - are āhiṇḍiā kīsa mukhaṃ ḍhakesi? jaṃ de bijjā na bikkāidā | [are āhiṇḍika"
kasmān mukham ācchādayasi? yat te vidyā na vikrītā |] (iti prasahya
sammukhayati) 126
children.translated_text: <s>Jaṭilā</s> — Hey, peddler, why do you cover your face? Since your goods have not been sold! (Thus forcibly making him face forward) 126

children.text:
abhimanyuḥ - (svagatam) haddhī haddhī bāuliaāe ammāe lajjāpajjāulo kidamhi |
tā ido abakkamissam | [hā dhik, hā dhik! bātūlikayā ambayā lajjā-paryākulaḥ
kṛto'smi | tad ito'pakramiṣyāmi |] 127
children.translated_text: <s>Abhimanyu</s> — (aside) Alas, alas! I have been put to shame by my chattering mother! So I shall depart from here. [Sanskrit rendering] 127

Here, from the agitation caused by hearing through the <s>sārikā</s> (myna bird) about <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s arrival, <s>Jaṭilā</s>'s perceiving her own son as <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> constitutes <s>sārūpya</s> (resemblance).
Now <s>mālā</s> (garland) —

children.text: bahūni kāraṇāny eva sā mālety abhidhīyate || 180 ||
children.translated_text: That which has many causes is called <s>mālā</s> (garland). || 180 ||
As in the second [act] —

children.text:
rādhā - lalide ppasīda ppasīda suṭhṭhu saṃkaulamhi | [lalite prasīda prasīda
suṣṭhu śaṅkākulāsmi |] (punaḥ saṃskṛtena)
children.translated_text: <s>Rādhā</s> — <s>Lalitā</s>, be gracious, be gracious! I am greatly troubled by doubt! (Again, in Sanskrit)
The evening is nearly gone; the elders are suspicious of conduct;
gossip runs high in the world; I am a straightforward woman of good family;
your friend is fickle, being a companion of all the cowherd women —

children.text: tadā namraṃ yāce sakhi rahasi saṅcāraya na mām || 2.19
children.translated_text: therefore I humbly beg you, friend, do not make me go to a secret meeting! || 2.19

children.text: atra sāyaṃ gamanādi-bahu-kāraṇānāṃ sveṣṭa-sañcāraṇābhāvāya kathitatvāt mālā |
children.translated_text: Here, since many reasons such as the lateness of evening are stated for the non-fulfillment of her own desire for the rendezvous, it is <s>mālā</s> (garland).
Now <s>madhura-bhāṣaṇa</s> (sweet speech) —

children.text: yat prasannena manasā pūjyaṃ pūjayitur vacaḥ |
children.translated_text: That speech of one who honors one worthy of honor with a pleased mind,
which is a manifestation of praise — that is to be known as <s>madhura-bhāṣaṇa</s> (sweet speech). || 181 ||
As in the fifth [act] —
The two kings (respectfully) —
He in a single hair-follicle of whose body the array of cosmic eggs
is seen like motes revolving in a window's sunbeam;

children.text: keyaṃ tasya samṛddhaye tava vibho rājendratā-grāmaṭī
children.translated_text: What is this petty chieftainship of kings for his enrichment, O Lord?

children.text: śauṭīryeṇa camatkṛtiṃ tad api naḥ kām apy asau puṣyati ||(5.17)
children.translated_text: Yet even that, by its boldness, produces in us some ineffable wonder! || (5.17)
Here the <s>madhura-bhāṣaṇa</s> (sweet speech) is clearly evident.
Now <s>pṛcchā</s> (query) —

children.text: praśna evottare yatra sā pṛcchā parikīrtitā ||
children.translated_text: Where a question itself serves as the answer — that is declared to be <s>pṛcchā</s> (query).
As in the ninth [act] —
<s>Kṛṣṇa</s> (approaching <s>Dāḍimī</s> before him)
She who bears a radiance enhanced by yellow garments was seen in the forest;
the doe-eyed one whom I was seeking today — has she been sought by you? || (9.18)

children.text:
atra he śuka, pītāṃ kāntiṃ bibhratī mayā mṛgyamāṇā sā dṛṣṭeti praścne, he
pītāṃśuka, tvayā mṛgyamāṇā sā mayā dṛṣṭety uttareṇa pṛcchā |
children.translated_text: Here, in the question 'O parrot, has she who bears yellow radiance and is sought by me been seen?', the answer is 'O wearer of yellow garments, she whom you seek has been seen by me' — thus it is <s>pṛcchā</s> (query).
Now <s>upadiṣṭa</s> (instruction) —

children.text: śāstrānusāri yad vākyam upadiṣṭaṃ tad ucyate || 182 ||
children.translated_text: A speech that follows scripture is called <s>upadiṣṭa</s> (instruction). || 182 ||
As in the sixth [act] — <s>Nārada</s> —

children.text: preyasyaḥ paśupālikā viharato yās tatra vṛndāvane
children.translated_text: The beloveds who are the cowherd women, sporting there in <s>Vṛndāvana</s>,
the buds of wondrous amorous play rare even for <s>Lakṣmī</s>, of the beloved enemy of <s>Kaṃsa</s> —

children.text: rādhā tatra varīyasīti nagarīṃ tām āśritāyāṃ kṣitau
children.translated_text: <s>Rādhā</s> is the foremost among them; and since she has taken refuge in that city,

children.text: sevāṃ devi samasta-maṅgala-karī yasyās tvam aṅgīkuru || (6.19)
children.translated_text: O queen, accept the service of her, which brings all auspiciousness! || (6.19)
Here, the [statement] that service to those dear to <s>Hari</s> brings all auspiciousness follows scripture — hence it is <s>upadiṣṭa</s> (instruction).
Now <s>dṛṣṭa</s> (description) —
The description of birth, nature, and such is called <s>dṛṣṭa</s> (description) by the wise. || 183 ||
As in the second [act] —
<s>Vṛndā</s> (casting her gaze forward) —
She churns the yogurt, with clusters of spreading foam
decorating the courtyard of the house, with deep sounds of the churning-rod;
with both hands curving and extending in the process of pulling the rope back and forth,
her bangles jingling — <s>Mālatī</s>! || (2.3)
Here, the description of the natural activity of churning yogurt constitutes <s>dṛṣṭa</s> (description).
Without stating the inter-junctural elements, the ornament known as <s>lakṣaṇa</s> (characteristic)
is described separately; some count thirty-three ornaments. || 184 ||

children.text: muner asammattatvena tat tu sarvam upekṣitam |
children.translated_text: Since these are not accepted by the sage [<s>Bharata</s>], all of them have been disregarded;
by some, the characteristics of the <s>sandhi-aṅga</s> (juncture-limbs) as qualities and ornaments || 185 ||
have been enumerated even within [the junctures], with effort, for the sake of completeness.
Now the <s>patākā-sthānas</s> (banner-stations) —
that which indicates the future state of the principal matter || 186 ||
through a seeming incidental occurrence — that is indeed a <s>patākā-sthānaka</s> (banner-station).
This is twofold: <s>tulya-saṃvidhāna</s> (equal arrangement) and <s>tulya-viśeṣaṇa</s> (equal qualification). || 187 ||

children.text: tatrādyaṃ triprakāraṃ syād dvitīyaṃ tv ekam eva hi |
children.translated_text: Of these, the first is of three kinds, while the second is only one;
thus the <s>patākā-sthānaka</s> should be known by the wise as fourfold. || 188 ||
Therein, the first —
The sudden attainment of meaning in a virtuous [character] through figurative usage —
this is declared as the first <s>patākā-sthānaka</s>. || 189 ||
As in <s>Lalita-mādhava</s>, seventh [act] —
<s>Rādhikā</s> (walking about, tremblingly grasping the edge of a yellow upper garment) —

children.text: dagdhaṃ hanta dadhānayā vapur idaṃ yasyāvalokāśayā
children.translated_text: Alas! This body of mine is burned by the one whose mere glance carries such intent,

children.text: soḍhā marma-vipāṭane paṭur iyaṃ pīḍātivṛṣṭir mayā |
children.translated_text: I have endured this excessive downpour of pain, skilled at tearing open vital spots;
he who has vowed to make love-excursions to the bower-caves on the bank of the <s>Kālindī</s> —
that friend of my life, O moon-faced one, is embraced once more! || 7.18 ||

children.text:
atra pratibimbe so'yaṃ jīvita-bandhur ity upacāra-prayogeṇa bhāvinaḥ kṛṣṇasya
sūcanāt sahasārtha-sampatti-rūpam idaṃ patākā-sthānakam |
children.translated_text: Here, in the reflection, through the figurative use of 'that friend of my life,' because it indicates the future <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, this is a <s>patākā-sthānaka</s> in the form of sudden attainment of meaning.
Now the second —
That which is excellently punned, resting upon the substance of poetry —
this is declared as the second <s>patākā-sthānaka</s>. || 190 ||
As in the second act — <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> [says] —
Accompanied by the restraint of love, born of gradually expanded artistic play,
like the lord of night, the company of <s>Rādhikā</s> is seen as a giver of moments. || (2.17)
(From behind the curtain) 'O lotus-eyed one, your custom of remaining distant is difficult to obtain!' 90
<s>Kṛṣṇa</s> (with agitation, loudly): What! What is this 'difficult to obtain'? 91
'The cattle-herd, though being sought with effort by the cowherds' || (2.18) 92
(Again from behind the curtain)

children.text:
atra bhaviṣyato rādhā-saṅgama-durlabhatvasya sūcanād idaṃ śliṣṭaṃ nāma
dvitīyaṃ patākā-sthānakam |
children.translated_text: Here, because it indicates the future difficulty of obtaining <s>Rādhā's</s> company, this is the punned type — the second <s>patākā-sthānaka</s>.
Now the third —

children.text: arthopakṣepaṇaṃ yat tu līnaṃ savinayaṃ bhavet |
children.translated_text: That which introduces a meaning in a hidden and modest manner,
accompanied by a punned reply — that is designated as the third. || 191 ||
As in the seventh [act], <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> —

children.text: (sarvataḥ prekṣya) priya-vayasya! kiyad dūre sā vṛndāṭavī ?
children.translated_text: (Looking all around) Dear friend! How far is that <s>Vṛndā</s> forest?
<s>Madhumaṅgala</s> (in Sanskrit) —

children.text:
sphuṭac-caṭula-campaka-prakara-rocir ullāsinī
madottarala-kokilāvali-kala-svarālāpinī |
marāla-gati-śālinī kalaya kṛṣṇa-sārādhikā
(ity ardhokte)
children.translated_text: 'Radiant with clusters of blossoming, trembling <s>campaka</s> flowers, resounding with the melodious notes of rows of intoxicated cuckoos, graced with the gait of swans — behold, O <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, the doe-like one—' (speaking only half)
<s>Kṛṣṇa</s> (with flustered eagerness): Dear boy, where is she?
<s>Madhumaṅgala</s> (showing with his finger) —
'Before you shines your beloved—'

children.text:
kṛṣṇaḥ (savyagram) vayasya! nāhaṃ paśyāmi | tad āśu darśaya | kva sā me
rādhikā ?
children.translated_text: <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> (anxiously): Friend! I do not see her. Show me quickly! Where is my <s>Rādhikā</s>?
<s>Madhumaṅgala</s> — ... O <s>Mukunda</s>, the <s>Vṛndā</s> forest! || (7.17)

children.text:
atra sajjalpitena madhu-maṅgala-vākyena bhāvino rādhā-darśanasya
sūcanācchliṣṭottaraṃ nāma tṛtīyaṃ patākā-sthānam |
children.translated_text: Here, through the cleverly spoken words of <s>Madhumaṅgala</s>, because they indicate the future sight of <s>Rādhā</s>, this is the punned-reply type — the third <s>patākā-sthānaka</s>.
Now the <s>darśana</s> (showing) —
A well-punned arrangement of words with double meaning, connected with poetry,
accompanied by a proposition — that is declared as the fourth. || 192 ||
As in the fifth [act], <s>Suparṇa</s> (<s>Garuḍa</s>) —
Praised in the sky by the impetuous great sages,
honored, with lotus eyes and a face white as the moon of fame,
abandoning the royal dynasty here, headed by the <s>Cedi</s> king,
O slayer of <s>Mura</s>, the goddess of victory will come to you eagerly! || (5.28)
Here, through <s>Suparṇa's</s> double-meaning words, because they indicate the attainment of <s>Candrāvalī</s>, this is <s>tulya-viśeṣaṇa</s> (equal qualification).
Now the <s>arthopakṣepakas</s> (expository devices) —

children.text: vastu sarvaṃ dvidhā sūcyam asūcyam iti bhedataḥ |
children.translated_text: All subject matter is twofold: that which is to be indicated and that which is not, by way of distinction.

children.text: rasa-hīnaṃ bhaved atra vastu tat sūcyam ucyate || 193 ||
children.translated_text: That subject matter which would be devoid of <s>rasa</s> (aesthetic sentiment) is here called 'to be indicated.' || 193 ||

children.text: adarśanīyam aṅke tad avaśyaṃ vācyam eva cet |
children.translated_text: That which is not fit to be shown on stage, yet must necessarily be expressed,
the wise should skillfully indicate through <s>arthopakṣepakas</s> (expository devices). || 194 ||
These are: <s>viṣkambha</s> (interlude), <s>cūlikā</s> (prologue-insert), <s>aṅkāsya</s> (act-face), <s>aṅkāvatāra</s> (act-descent), and <s>praveśaka</s> (entrance-scene).
Now the <s>viṣkambha</s> (interlude) —
A <s>viṣkambha</s> indicates portions of past and future events. || 195 ||
Shown briefly at the beginning of an act by non-principal characters,

children.text: sa śuddho miśra ity u kto miśraḥ syān nīca-madhyamaiḥ || 196 ||
children.translated_text: it is called pure or mixed; the mixed is performed by low and middling characters. || 196 ||
As in <s>Vidagdha-mādhava</s>, where it is placed at the opening of the second act;
that one, involving <s>Mukharā</s> and others who are non-principal, is designated as mixed. || 197 ||
The pure one is composed of middling characters only, and may be performed by one or many;
it is composed in many places in that <s>Lalita-mādhava</s>. || 198 ||
Now the <s>cūlikā</s> (prologue-insert) —

children.text: prājñair yavanikāntaḥsthair adṛśyair yā tu nirmitāḥ |
children.translated_text: That which is composed by wise persons standing behind the curtain, unseen,

children.text: ādāv aṅkasya madhye vā cūlikā nāma sā bhavet || 199 ||
children.translated_text: at the beginning or middle of an act — that is called <s>cūlikā</s>. || 199 ||
Examples are clearly found in many places.
Now the <s>aṅkāsya</s> (act-face) —

children.text: yatra syād aṅka ekasminn aṅkānāṃ sūcanākhilā |
children.translated_text: Where, in a single act, there is an indication of all [subsequent] acts —

children.text: tad-aṅkāsyam iti prāhur bījārtha-khyāpakaṃ ca yat || 200 ||
children.translated_text: that is called <s>aṅkāsya</s> (act-face), which also reveals the meaning of the <s>bīja</s> (seed). || 200 ||
In <s>Lalita-mādhava</s>, in the first act, through <s>Paurṇamāsī</s> accompanied by <s>Gārgī</s>,

children.text: prathamāṅke yathā suṣṭhu suhitaṃ nikhilaṃ sphuṭam || 201 ||
children.translated_text: everything is clearly and properly indicated. || 201 ||
But some [say] —
When characters who have entered at the end of the previous act indicate

children.text: sūcanaṃ tad avicchedyair yat tad aṅkāsyam īritam || 202 ||
children.translated_text: the subject matter of the coming act without interruption — that is called <s>aṅkāsya</s>. || 202 ||
Thus they define it.
Because this is already covered by the <s>aṅkāvatāra</s>,
some learned ones say this [term] refers only to the meaning stated first. || 203 ||
Now the <s>aṅkāvatāra</s> (act-descent) —
The <s>aṅkāvatāra</s> is the entrance of all characters
who continue the subject of the previous act, without distinction, into the coming act. || 204 ||
The example is self-evident.
Now the <s>praveśaka</s> (entrance-scene) —
That which indicates past or future events solely through low characters,

children.text: aṅkayor ubhayor madhye sa vijñeyaḥ praveśakaḥ || 205 ||
children.translated_text: between two acts — that should be known as a <s>praveśaka</s>. || 205 ||

children.text: yadā syān nīrasaṃ sūcyam āmukhānantaraṃ tadā |
children.translated_text: When what is to be indicated would be devoid of <s>rasa</s> [and follows] after the prelude, then
a <s>viṣkambha</s> or <s>aṅkāsyaka</s> should be used, with characters introduced by the prelude. || 206 ||

children.text: yadā tu sarasaṃ vastu mūlād eva pravartate |
children.translated_text: But when the subject matter is full of <s>rasa</s> and proceeds from the source itself,
then the act itself should begin at the very start, supported by the introduction's hint. || 207 ||
That which is not to be indicated is what is replete with beauty, grandeur, <s>rasa</s>, and <s>bhāva</s> (emotion);

children.text: prārambhe yady asūcyaṃ syād aṅkam evātra kalpayet || 208 ||
children.translated_text: if at the beginning there is nothing to be indicated, one should compose the act itself directly. || 208 ||

children.text: asūcyaṃ tu dvidhā dṛśyaṃ śravyaṃ cādyaṃ tu darśayet |
children.translated_text: That which is not to be indicated is twofold: the visible and the audible. The first should be shown;

children.text: dvedhā dvitīyaṃ svagataṃ prakāśaṃ ceti bhedataḥ || 209 ||
children.translated_text: the second is again twofold: <s>svagata</s> (aside) and <s>prakāśa</s> (open speech), by way of distinction. || 209 ||

children.text: svagataṃ svaika-vijñeyaṃ prakāśaṃ tad dvidhā bhavet |
children.translated_text: <s>Svagata</s> (aside) is to be understood by oneself alone; <s>prakāśa</s> (open speech) is again twofold:
<s>sarva-prakāśa</s> (addressed to all) and <s>niyata-prakāśa</s> (addressed to specific persons). || 210 ||
<s>Sarva-prakāśa</s> is that which is suitable to be heard by all present;

children.text: dvidhā vibhajyate tac ca janāntam apavāritam || 211 ||
children.translated_text: it is divided into two: <s>janānta</s> (confidential) and <s>apavārita</s> (screened aside). || 211 ||
That conversation which is conducted between two persons, screening others

children.text: yā mithaḥ kriyate dvābhyāṃ taj janāntikam ucyate || 212 ||
children.translated_text: with the <s>tripatāka</s> hand-gesture, in the middle — that is called <s>janāntika</s> (confidential aside). || 212 ||
When a secret is told to another by turning away — that is <s>apavārita</s> (screened aside).
Having the hero's conduct directly visible, furnished with minor songs and powder-play, || 213 ||
Now the nature of the act —
not having overly obscure words and meanings, not having excessive verses,
not burdened with many affairs nor with the gathering of the seed, || 214 ||
free from a narrative that would take many days to complete,
composed with subject matter suitable for half a day or a full day, || 215 ||
without killing, distant summoning, battle, loss of kingdom and the like,
without curses, renunciation, excursions, sexual union, eating, and death, || 216 ||
without bathing, anointing, sleeping, and the like, without kissing, embracing, and so on,

children.text: vrīḍā-heturbhir anyaiś ca bībhataiś ca vinā kṛtaḥ || 217 ||
children.translated_text: and without causes of shame and other disgusting things — || 217 ||
with all characters having exited at the end — such is described as an act.
In connection with the act, the definition of <s>garbhāṅka</s> will now be stated by me. || 218 ||
Now the <s>garbhāṅka</s> (interlude act) —

children.text: aṅkasya madhye yo'ṅkaḥ syād asau garbhāṅka īritaḥ |
children.translated_text: An act within the middle of an act is called <s>garbhāṅka</s> (interlude act);
it has a <s>nāndī</s> (benediction) that indicates the subject matter, with only a brief opening section, || 219 ||

children.text: arthopakṣepakair hīno yutaḥ pātrais tu pañcaṣaiḥ |
children.translated_text: devoid of expository devices, furnished with five or six characters,
concerned with a subject matter that is being sought, adorned at the end with its supporting act. || 220 ||
it should not be placed in the first act — so say those skilled in poetry. || 221 ||
Not having an overly elaborate plot, connected with the main subject,
The <s>garbhāṅka</s> is in the fourth act, as in <s>Lalita-mādhava</s>.
In a <s>nāṭaka</s>, the acts should be no fewer than five and no more than ten. || 222 ||
Now general rules —
Even through <s>viṣkambhas</s> and the like, the death of a principal character should not be described.
One should not allow the mutual concealment of <s>rasa</s> and subject matter. || 223 ||

children.text: yat syād anucitaṃ vastu nāyakasya rasasya vā |
children.translated_text: Whatever subject matter would be unfitting for the hero or the <s>rasa</s>,

children.text: viruddhaṃ tat parityājyam anyathā vā prakalpayet || 224 ||
children.translated_text: being contradictory, that should be abandoned, or else devised differently. || 224 ||
And that narrative which, though not contradictory, would excessively [impede] the manifestation of <s>rasa</s>,

children.text: tad apy anyathayed dhīmān na vaded vā kadācana || 225 ||
children.translated_text: the wise person should alter it, or not speak of it at all. || 225 ||
Ten <s>lāsyāṅgas</s> (dance elements) and thirteen <s>vīthy-aṅgas</s> (one-act sub-elements) —

children.text: aṅkeṣv api nibadhyāni kecid evaṃ pracaksate || 226 ||
children.translated_text: some say these should also be incorporated into the acts. || 226 ||

children.text: prāyas tāny api santy eva tasmin lalita-mādhave |
children.translated_text: Generally these too are present in that <s>Lalita-mādhava</s>.
Sometimes here, <s>ākāśa-bhāṣita</s> (speech to the sky) should be accomplished by the wise. || 227 ||

children.text: anyenānuktam apy anyo vacaḥ śrutvaiva yad vadet |
children.translated_text: When one person, though not spoken to by another, responds as if having heard speech —

children.text: iti kiṃ bhaṇasīty etad bhaved ākāśa-bhāṣitam || 228 ||
children.translated_text: saying 'What do you say?' — that is <s>ākāśa-bhāṣita</s> (speech to the sky). || 228 ||
Now the rules regarding language —
In drama, the linguistic forms of the characters are determined here.

children.text: tatra bhāṣā dvidhā bhāṣā vibhāṣā ceti bhedataḥ || 229 ||
children.translated_text: Language is twofold: <s>bhāṣā</s> (language proper) and <s>vibhāṣā</s> (dialect). || 229 ||
There are fourteen <s>vibhāṣās</s> (dialects), beginning with the eastern, defined by sentence patterns;
because of their lack of refinement, their application is not discussed. || 230 ||

children.text: bhāṣā dvidhā saṃskṛtā ca prākṛtī ceti bhedataḥ |
children.translated_text: <s>Bhāṣā</s> (language) is twofold: <s>Saṃskṛta</s> (Sanskrit) and <s>Prākṛta</s> (Prakrit).
<s>Saṃskṛta</s> is [the language] of deities and others, of sages, and of the hero, || 231 ||
Therein, <s>Saṃskṛta</s> (Sanskrit) —
of ascetics, brahmins, merchants, warriors, ministers, and chamberlains,
of forest goddesses, courtesans, daughters of ministers, and educated women, || 232 ||
and it is also declared for <s>yoginīs</s>, <s>apsarases</s> (celestial nymphs), and craftswomen.

children.text: ṣoḍhāntimā prākṛtī syāc chaurasenī ca māgadhī || 233 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Prākṛta</s> is sixfold at the most: <s>Śaurasenī</s> and <s>Māgadhī</s>, || 233 ||
Therein, <s>Prākṛta</s> (Prakrit) —
<s>Paiśācī</s>, <s>Cūlikā-paiśācī</s>, and <s>Apabhraṃśa</s>, in that order.

children.text: atra tu prākṛtaṃ strīṇāṃ sarvāsāṃ niyataṃ bhavet || 234 ||
children.translated_text: Here, <s>Prākṛta</s> is invariably the language of all women. || 234 ||
Of those intoxicated with power, of those whose spirit is afflicted by poverty,

children.text: ye nīcāḥ karmaṇā jātyā teṣāṃ ca prākṛtaṃ smṛtam || 235 ||
children.translated_text: and of those who are low by deed or by birth — for these, <s>Prākṛta</s> is prescribed. || 235 ||
Among these, for heroines and others, <s>Śaurasenī</s> is declared;

children.text: āsām eva tu gāthāsu mahārāṣṭrī smṛtā budhaiḥ || 236 ||
children.translated_text: for their songs, <s>Māhārāṣṭrī</s> is recognized by the wise. || 236 ||
Here, <s>Māgadhī</s> is stated as the language of those who frequent the royal harem,
and likewise of the <s>vidūṣaka</s> (jester) and others, and of servants. || 237 ||
For <s>rākṣasas</s> (demons), <s>piśācas</s> (goblins), and low persons, the two varieties of <s>Paiśācī</s> apply;
<s>Apabhraṃśa</s> is appropriate for <s>caṇḍālas</s>, <s>yavanas</s> (foreigners), and the like. || 238 ||
For all characters, transgression of language rules should be made when there is cause:
due to the decline of dignity, or due to excess of intoxication, || 239 ||
or for concealment, or in confusion, or when reading something aloud —
sometimes also for repetition — these are declared as the causes. || 240 ||
For heroines, female friends, courtesans, gamblers, and <s>apsarases</s> likewise,
<s>Saṃskṛta</s> should be employed occasionally for the sake of displaying wit. || 241 ||
The examples of these are clear.
Now, the <s>vṛttis</s> (dramatic styles) —
Now are described the supremely wonderful <s>vṛttis</s> (dramatic styles), which by nature
arose from <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> at the slaying of <s>Madhu</s> and <s>Kaiṭabha</s>. || 242 ||
Being in the form of the protagonist's activities and indicative of the abiding of <s>rasa</s> (aesthetic sentiment),

children.text: catasro vṛttayo dhīraiḥ proktā nāṭyasya mātaraḥ || 243 ||
children.translated_text: the four <s>vṛttis</s> are declared by the wise to be the mothers of drama. || 243 ||

children.text: bhāraty ārabhaṭī caiva sātvatī kaiśikī tathā |
children.translated_text: <s>Bhāratī</s>, <s>Ārabhaṭī</s>, <s>Sātvatī</s>, and <s>Kaiśikī</s> likewise.
Of these, <s>Bhāratī</s> —
This is called <s>Bhāratī</s> because speech is predominant in it. || 244 ||
Being useful for the <s>prastāvanā</s> (prologue), it is especially noted there;
devoid of women, performed by the best of men, and predominantly verbal. || 245 ||

children.text: bhāratī saṃskṛtair yuktā vṛttiḥ syāc caturaṅgikā |
children.translated_text: <s>Bhāratī</s>, employed with Sanskrit, is a <s>vṛtti</s> having four limbs.
Abounding in illusion, <s>Indra</s>'s magic, various battles and actions, || 246 ||
Now, <s>Ārabhaṭī</s> —
rich in display, cutting, and breaking — this style is known as <s>Ārabhaṭī</s>.

children.text: aṅgāny asyās tu catvāri saṅkṣiptir avapātanam || 247 ||
children.translated_text: Its limbs are four: <s>saṅkṣipti</s> (condensation), <s>avapātana</s> (tumultuous entry), || 247 ||
<s>vastūtthāpana</s> (raising of an illusory object), and <s>sampheṭa</s> (combat) — thus says the sage <s>Bharata</s>.
<s>Saṅkṣipti</s> is said to be the creation of a wondrous condensed narrative. || 248 ||
Of these, <s>saṅkṣipti</s> (condensation) —
For example —

children.text: vidhinā hate śiśu-kule tādṛśam aparaṃ haris tathā vyatanot |
children.translated_text: When the clan of infants was slain by fate, <s>Hari</s> produced another such [clan] in the same way,

children.text: viramatu parasya vārtāṃ svayam eva visismaye sa yathā ||
children.translated_text: so that the enemy would cease [his efforts] and would himself be amazed.

children.text:
athāvapātanam -
vibhrāntir avapātaḥ syāt praveśa-drava-vidravaiḥ |
yathā -

children.translated_text: Striking down the elephant <s>Kuvalayāpīḍa</s> before him as if destroying an obstacle, with gentle sport,

children.text: tuṅgāṃ raṅga-bhuvaṃ praviśya tarasā pratyarthināṃ trāsanaḥ |
children.translated_text: entering the lofty arena with speed, terrifying the adversaries,
a rain-cloud to the fire of the proud wrestlers, putting to flight even the petty ones with a moving glance —
behold! <s>Keśava</s> assumes the form of <s>Garuḍa</s>, with delight, before the serpent <s>Kaṃsa</s>!

Now, <s>avapātana</s> (tumultuous entry) —
<s>Avapāta</s> is bewilderment through entries, flights, and stampedes.
For example —
<s>Vastūtthāpana</s> is an object fabricated by magic. || 249 ||
Now, <s>vastūtthāpana</s> (raising of an illusory object) —
Concealing the wickedness clearly [present] in her heart with deceitful affection,
<s>Pūtanā</s>, assuming a beautiful form contrived by <s>māyā</s> (illusion), arrived in <s>Vraja</s>.

children.text: tasyāḥ suṣṭhu tathā payodhara-rasaḥ prītaḥ śiśu-krīḍayā
children.translated_text: The milk of her breast was so thoroughly [sucked] by him, pleased with infant play,

children.text: vaikuṇṭhena haṭhād yathā na sa punaḥ mātus tathā pāsyate ||
children.translated_text: that <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s>) forcibly [drank it] such that it would never again be drunk thus even from a mother.
For example —
<s>Sampheṭa</s> is a clash engaged in by the enraged and the furious. || 250 ||
Now, <s>sampheṭa</s> (combat) —
As between the wrestler <s>Cāṇūra</s> and <s>Murāri</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>),
there was a fierce mutual combat,
by which the chests of both <s>Kaṃsa</s> and <s>Ānakadundubhi</s> (<s>Vasudeva</s>)
burst with anguish and anxiety.
For example —
Now, <s>Sātvatī</s> —
Endowed with <s>sāttvika</s> (noble) qualities such as renunciation, heroism, and the like,
predominantly joyful and free from sorrow — this is declared as <s>Sātvatī</s>. || 251 ||

children.text: aṅgāny asyās tu catvāri saṃlāpottāpakāv api |
children.translated_text: Its limbs are four: <s>saṃlāpa</s> (dialogue) and <s>utthāpaka</s> (incitement),
<s>saṅghātya</s> (alliance-breaking) and <s>parivarta</s> (reversal) — their definitions are now stated. || 252 ||
Now, <s>saṃlāpa</s> (dialogue) —
Profound mutual speech, infused with emotions such as jealousy, anger, and others,
and with <s>rasas</s> (sentiments) such as the heroic and the marvelous, is called <s>saṃlāpa</s> (dialogue). || 253 ||

children.text: vayaṃ bālās tulyaiḥ saha racayituṃ yuddham ucitaṃ
children.translated_text: We are boys — it is proper to fight with equals;
before us, you wrestlers display the dreadful appearance of mountains.
Who would be wise enough to arrange a sporting arena
for tender-bodied young elephants against lordly bull-elephants intoxicated with rut?
For example —
Truly you are a boy — yet you split the form of Time itself,
subduing the mighty elephant-lord with mere child's play!
Here indeed, for the commencement of arm-wrestling,
this row of boys, having made friendship with your body, shall be the witnesses.

children.text:
athotthāpakaḥ -
preraṇaṃ yat parasyādau yuddhāyotthāpakas tu saḥ |
children.translated_text:
Now, <s>utthāpaka</s> (incitement) —
<s>Utthāpaka</s> is the initial provocation of another to battle.
I am about to uproot the <s>Pārijāta</s> tree, the essence of the good fortune of the city of <s>Triviṣṭapa</s> (heaven),
the lord of the gods' [tree], the fulfiller of the desires of the divine women,
the expert in the sport of the water-creatures playing on the pitcher-like breasts of <s>Paulomī</s> (<s>Śacī</s>) —

children.text: pāṇis tena hi dakṣiṇaḥ katham asua dambholim udyac-chate ||
children.translated_text: so how is it that his right hand raises the thunderbolt against me?
For example —
<s>Saṅghātya</s> is the breaking of an alliance through power, counsel, divine [aid], and the like. || 254 ||
Now, <s>saṅghātya</s> (alliance-breaking) —
Of these, through power, for example —
Waving her garment, crying out loudly 'Victory, victory, victory!'
standing near the arena, her face exalted with the weight of love,
beholding some wondrous and beautiful power

children.text: hareḥ kaṃsopekṣāṃ vadhita bata sākṣān madhupurī ||
children.translated_text: of <s>Hari</s> — alas! The city of <s>Madhupurī</s> itself vanquished <s>Kaṃsa</s>'s disregard!
Through counsel, for example —
Having heard the plan of <s>Danujārdana</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>),
bound with passion for the worship of <s>Govardhana</s>,
the entire assembly of the <s>Ābhīra</s> cowherds impetuously
desisted from the sacrifice to the king of the gods.

children.text:
atha parivartakaḥ -
prārabdha-kāryād anyasya karaṇaṃ parivartakaḥ |
children.translated_text:
Now, <s>parivartaka</s> (reversal) —
<s>Parivartaka</s> is the doing of something other than the task begun.
Upon you who, out of great pride, were causing torrential rains in the land of <s>Vraja</s>,
fear arose in my heart today through the experience of your [divine] influence.

children.text: tvam asi kila kṛpālur dogdhu-kāmo'pi kāmaṃ
children.translated_text: You are indeed compassionate, though you wished to milk [us] at will;

children.text: tad iha mayi śaraṇye gokulendra prasīda ||
children.translated_text: therefore, O lord of <s>Gokula</s>, be gracious to me who have taken refuge [in you].
For example —
Now, <s>Kaiśikī</s> —
The style embellished with soft erotic gestures
such as dance, song, and graceful play, is <s>Kaiśikī</s>, adorned with delicate ornaments. || 255 ||
It is called <s>Kaiśikī</s> because of its connection with <s>Keśa</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>).

children.text: aṅgāny asyās tu catvāri narma-tat-pūrvakā ime || 256 ||
children.translated_text: Its limbs are four: <s>narma</s> (jest) and those preceded by it — || 256 ||

children.text: sphañjaḥ sphoṭaś ca garbhaś cety eṣāṃ lakṣaṇam ucyate |
children.translated_text: <s>sphañja</s> (throbbing), <s>sphoṭa</s> (revelation), and <s>garbha</s> (seminal implication) — their definitions are now stated.
Predominantly of the erotic <s>rasa</s>, delighting the mind of the beloved, || 257 ||
Of these, <s>narma</s> (jest) —

children.text: agrāmyaḥ parihāsaḥ syān narma tat tu tridhā matam |
children.translated_text: refined humor, not vulgar, is <s>narma</s> — and it is considered to be threefold:
arising from erotic humor, from pure humor, and from fear-humor. || 258 ||
<s>Narma</s> arising from erotic humor is declared to be threefold:
from the manifestation of desire for union, from the disclosure of love, || 259 ||
and from the reproaching of the beloved who has committed an offense.
The manifestation of desire for union is threefold: through speech, dress, and gestures. || 260 ||
Of these, through speech, as in the <s>Padyāvalī</s> (207) —

children.text: gacchāmy acyuta darśanena bhavataḥ kiṃ tṛptir utpadyate
children.translated_text: "I am going, O <s>Acyuta</s> — does satisfaction arise from merely seeing you?

children.text: kiṃ tv evaṃ vijana-sthayor hata-janaḥ sambhāvayaty anyathā |
children.translated_text: Moreover, wicked people will think otherwise of us two alone in this secluded place."
Thus clinging to the <s>gopī</s> whose feigned reluctance, indicated by the gesture of farewell, betrayed her sorrow at vainly remaining,

children.text: āśliṣyan pulakotkarāñcita-tanur gopīṃ hariḥ pātu vaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Hari</s>, his body bristling with horripilation, may he protect you!
When the moon rises, the graceful and lovely messenger-woman [appears],
with eyes and minds agitated by passion;
indeed, the first act of adornment by the women is reversed ornament-arrangement,
making their friends laugh at the [disordered] placement.
Through dress, as in the <s>Rasārṇava-sudhākara</s> (1.273) —
Through gestures, for example —
O dark one, the one you are courting, standing among a group of dear friends,

children.text: savyāṃ smeramukhī dṛśaṃ madhubhidaḥ smere mukhāmbhoruhe |
children.translated_text: casts her left glance, with a smiling face, toward the smiling lotus-face of <s>Madhubhid</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>),

children.text: bhṛṅgodbhāsini dakṣiṇāṃ tu kiratī krīḍā-nikuñje muhuḥ
children.translated_text: while with the right [glance], sparkling like a bee, she scatters it repeatedly in the pleasure-grove;

children.text: sūrye rajyati sacchalaṃ vicinute tapāya puṣpāvalim ||
children.translated_text: when the sun shines, she pretends to gather a garland of flowers for heating [her ornaments].
The disclosure of love is also threefold, like the desire-for-union <s>narma</s>.
Of these, through speech, for example —
"O goddess, you will say 'Give me <s>kunda</s> flowers' —
that which you said to <s>Mukunda</s> without delay,
your family guardian's vow
has thereby now become broken-voiced."
"That you always mock me for being eager-hearted
for the secret rendezvous — that is quite fitting here;
but at the mere mention of <s>Hari</s>'s story upon your body,
how is it that a row of horripilation has bloomed?"
Through dress, for example —
Through gestures, for example —
"O friend, while practicing the weaving of a forest-garland in solitude,
you have been found out — enough of words about your unbroken conjugal fidelity!"
"O prince of <s>Vraja</s>, do not display
your considerable cleverness through gestures of praise!
By your groundlessly suspicious
words, I have been greatly enlightened!"
Of these [reproaching the offending beloved], through speech, for example —
Through dress, as in <s>Lalita-Mādhava</s> —
<s>Candrāvalī</s> (with a mocking smile) —
"With collyrium-dark center and sprout-red radiance, the lip of <s>Mukunda</s> —

children.text: guṃjāphallaṃ bba aharaṃ sahi pekkhantī pamodāmi ||
children.translated_text: like a <s>guñjā</s> berry, friend, beholding it I rejoice!"
["With collyrium-dark center and sprout-red radiance, the lip of <s>Mukunda</s> —
like a <s>guñjā</s> berry, friend, beholding it I rejoice!"] 9.54
Through gestures, as in the <s>Rasa-sudhākara</s> (1.273) —
With a trembling brow-creeper she shakes her head at the suggestion of the rival's quarter;
upon seeing that [rival's] retinue, she makes an embarrassed smile without bowing;

children.text: roṣāt tāmarakapola-kāntini mukhe dṛṣṭyā nataṃ pādayor
children.translated_text: in anger, on her lotus-cheek-beautiful face, her gaze falls upon his feet;

children.text: utsṛṣṭo guru-sannidhāv api vidhir dvābhyāṃ na kālocitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: even in the presence of elders, the two abandoned the time-appropriate conduct.

children.text: śuddha-hāsyajam apy uktaṃ tadvad eva tridhā budhaiḥ || 262 ||
children.translated_text: That arising from pure humor is also declared by the wise to be threefold in the same manner. || 262 ||
Now, [<s>narma</s>] arising from pure humor —

children.text: vṛddhe candra iti pratāraya na mām ajñāsiṣaṃ mad-bhayān
children.translated_text: "O old <s>Candra</s> (moon), do not deceive me — do you think I did not know? Out of fear of me,
mother <s>Rādhā</s> placed the ball of fresh butter on a high shelf today.

children.text: gūḍhaṃ pātayitāsmi dīrghatarayā yaṣṭyeti vācaṃ harer
children.translated_text: I shall secretly knock it down with a very long stick" — hearing these words of <s>Hari</s>,

children.text: indu-nyasta-dṛśo niśamya mukharā kṣemaṃ hasantī kriyāt ||
children.translated_text: who gazed at the moon, may <s>Mukharā</s>, laughing, grant you well-being!
Of these, through speech, for example —
Through dress and gestures, for example —
Seeing <s>Hari</s> disguised as a bull using a blanket, with agitation orchestrated by <s>Bhṛṅga</s>,

children.text: prekṣya hariṃ vidhir ahasīn mudira-cchanno gabhīro'pi ||
children.translated_text: <s>Brahmā</s> laughed, though deep [in nature], concealed behind a cloud.
Now, [<s>narma</s>] arising from fear-humor —
That which is born from humor combined with fear is called fear-humor <s>narma</s>;

children.text: tad dvidhā mukham aṅgaṃ tu tad dvayaṃ pūrvavat tridhā || 263 ||
children.translated_text: it is twofold — primary and subsidiary — and both are threefold as before. || 263 ||
The primary, through speech, for example —
When the herd of cows was protected by the sport of lifting the king of mountains,
seeing the thousand-eyed one (<s>Indra</s>) who had come with the desire to offer praise,

children.text: pratyāsīdati paśya rākṣasa-patiḥ sākṣād ayaṃ pāhi māṃ
children.translated_text: "Behold! The lord of <s>rākṣasas</s> (demons) himself is approaching! Save me!"

children.text: ity utkrośati mugdha-vallava-śiśau smero hariḥ pātu vaḥ ||
children.translated_text: — thus the innocent cowherd boy cries out; may the smiling <s>Hari</s> protect you!
Similarly, examples through dress and gestures may also be given.
Now, the subsidiary. Of these, through speech, for example —

children.text: yady ullaṅghya giraṃ visarpati tataḥ svāṅge vraṇaṃ pāṇijaiḥ
children.translated_text: "If he transgresses my word and creeps forth, then I shall inflict wounds on my own body with my nails

children.text: kurvann eva kṛtaṃ tvayeti jaratī-laksāya vakṣyāmy aham |
children.translated_text: and tell the old woman 'You did this!'"

children.text: ity ukte svaram ākulām iva bhayād ālokya rādhāṃ punaḥ
children.translated_text: Upon hearing this, seeing <s>Rādhā</s> as if confused with fear, and then again

children.text: stabdhībhūta-gatiṃ hariḥ smita-mukhaḥ śliṣyan mudaṃ vaḥ kriyāt ||
children.translated_text: stopped in her tracks — may <s>Hari</s>, with a smiling face, embracing [her], grant you joy!
Through dress, for example —
When the enemy of <s>Mura</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) appeared before <s>Rādhā</s> disguised as <s>Abhimanyu</s>,
she was slightly seized by fear;
[but] recognizing the natural inclination of her own heart toward the loving one,
the clever girl extended a smile.
Through gestures, as in the <s>Rasa-sudhākara</s> (1.275) —
"O lover of <s>Prahlāda</s>, we are afraid of this amorous sport" —
thus the <s>gopīs</s> uttered jests;
while playfully and softly pressing nail-marks upon the slopes of their breasts,
may the one crowned with peacock feathers protect you!
This <s>narma</s> has been clearly demonstrated in eighteen varieties.
<s>Narma-sphañja</s> is a new union of one striving for pleasure, afflicted by fear. || 264 ||
Now, <s>narma-sphañja</s> (jest-throbbing) —
While the two, anxiously casting glances in every direction, their hearts numb with shyness,
were more frightened by the fierce words of the old woman asking 'Where have you gone at night?' —
then, in the hollow of the heap of cow-dung placed at the entrance of the cow-pen,

children.text: rādhā-mādhavayor abhūt kvaṇikaras tasmin navaḥ saṅgamaḥ ||
children.translated_text: there occurred that tinkling, new union of <s>Rādhā</s> and <s>Mādhava</s>.
For example —
<s>Narma-sphoṭa</s> is considered to be [a scene] hinted at by traces of emotion, with slight <s>rasa</s>. || 265 ||
Now, <s>narma-sphoṭa</s> (jest-revelation) —
As in <s>Vidagdha-Mādhava</s> —
<s>Madhumaṅgala</s> (looking at <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, aside) —
Seeing the golden-hued mass of full-blown blossoms,
the <s>campaka</s> creeper indeed trembles.
I suspect that <s>Rādhā</s>'s face, fair as fresh spotless <s>kuṅkuma</s> (saffron) paste,
has become a <s>tilaka</s> (ornamental mark) on the tablet of his heart. || (2.25)
Now <s>narma-garbha</s> (concealed humor) —

children.text: netur vā nāyikāyā vā vyāpāraḥ svārtha-siddhaye |
children.translated_text: The activity of the hero or the heroine for the accomplishment of their own purpose,

children.text: pracchādana-paro yas tu narma-garbhaḥ sa ucyate || 266 ||
children.translated_text: which is intent upon concealment, is called <s>narma-garbha</s> (concealed humor). || 266 ||
As in <s>Rasa-sudhākara</s> (1.279) —
Due to pangs of remorse arising from the languor of offended <s>Lakṣmī</s>'s (the beloved's) pride, with a smiling face,
having secretly taken residence among the circle of friends, rising suddenly,

children.text: samaneṣye dhūrtaṃ tam aham iti jalpan nata-mukhīṃ
children.translated_text: [saying] 'I shall bring that rogue,' speaking thus, embracing

children.text: priyāntām āliṅgan harir arati-khedaṃ haratu vaḥ ||
children.translated_text: his beloved with downcast face — may <s>Hari</s> remove the affliction of your sorrows!
Three modes of expression (<s>vṛtti</s>) relating to meaning have been stated; the verbal mode is <s>bhāratī</s>;
now the propriety of these four [modes] with respect to <s>rasa</s> is stated. || 267 ||
The <s>sātvatī</s> (mode) is appropriate for the <s>śānta</s> (tranquil), <s>vīra</s> (heroic), <s>adbhuta</s> (wondrous), <s>prīta</s> (loving), and <s>vatsala</s> (tender) [rasas];

children.text: preyaḥ śṛṅgāra-hāsyeṣu proktā vṛttis tu kaiśikī || 268 ||
children.translated_text: the <s>kaiśikī</s> (mode) is declared for <s>preyaḥ</s> (affection), <s>śṛṅgāra</s> (erotic), and <s>hāsya</s> (comic) [rasas]. || 268 ||
The <s>ārabhaṭī</s> (mode) is for the <s>bībhatsa</s> (disgusting), <s>karuṇa</s> (compassionate), <s>vīra</s> (heroic), and <s>bhayānaka</s> (terrifying) [rasas];
the <s>bhāratī</s> (mode) is generally present in all <s>rasas</s>, including <s>karuṇa</s> (compassionate) and others. || 269 ||
Thus concludes the <s>Śrī Nāṭaka-candrikā</s>, composed by <s>Śrīmad Rūpa Gosvāmī Prabhupāda</s>, the supreme preceptor in the establishment of <s>dhvani</s> (poetic suggestion).
